jobs.title: Senior Director, Solutions Architecture — Americas
jobs.description:
Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

As the Senior Director of Solutions Architecture for the Americas at Cohere, you will own the US and Canada commercial Solutions Architecture function. You will lead the team that turns enterprise interest in agentic AI into deployed, production systems, and you will be accountable for the technical win in the most competitive AI market in the world. The United States and Canada are our largest commercial opportunity, and this seat owns how we win them.

You will take an established, distributed team of strong technical people and raise what it can do — setting the bar and establishing the operating rhythm that lets a team of generalists run consistent, industry-fluent plays at enterprise scale. You will set direction for the function, sit on the Solution Architecture leadership team alongside the regional leaders for EMEA and Asia Pacific, and contribute to company-wide decisions with your peers across Sales, Product and Engineering.

In This Role, You Will

Lead and Scale the Organization: Build, coach and develop a high-performing Solutions Architecture organization across the US and Canada, and grow the senior technical talent within it.
Own the Technical Win: Be personally accountable for the technical outcome of the region’s most strategic pursuits, and be in the room for the ones that decide the year.
Own the US Market: Lead how Cohere positions, proves and sells into US enterprises — our largest commercial opportunity, and the market this seat is measured on.
Extend Our Reach: Grow the share of the region’s pipeline the team is technically leading, and make sure we are engaged early on the opportunities that matter most.
Own the Number with Sales: Partner with regional Sales leadership as a co-owner of the region’s number, not as a support function to it.
Set Direction for the Function: Define the vision, strategy and operating model for Americas Solutions Architecture, and hold your leaders accountable for delivery and execution against it.
Build Repeatable Solution Practices: Establish scalable solution-selling methodologies, industry playbooks, executive narratives, business cases and technical delivery frameworks that improve consistency and win rates.
Architect Enterprise AI Solutions: Guide customers in designing secure, scalable, production-ready agentic AI solutions across cloud, hybrid, VPC and on-premises environments.
Shape Product Direction: Partner closely with Product and Engineering to translate customer feedback and market needs into platform improvements and roadmap priorities.
Attract Talent to Cohere: Bring senior technical field talent with you and continue to attract it. Building the bench is part of the job, not a consequence of it.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and develop the Americas commercial Solutions Architecture team through coaching, hiring, performance management and career development.
Partner with regional Sales leadership to pursue and close strategic enterprise opportunities across financial services, healthcare, energy, technology and other key verticals.
Own the region’s technical coverage model, and ensure the team is engaged early and consistently on the opportunities that matter most.
Lead executive workshops, discovery sessions, solution presentations and technical deep dives with C-suite and senior customer stakeholders.
Develop business cases, solution architectures, implementation roadmaps and technical proposals that align customer objectives with Cohere’s platform.
Guide customers through the deployment of enterprise AI solutions, ensuring scalability, security, governance and operational readiness.
Create repeatable solution assets, industry playbooks and best practices that enable the team to consistently deliver high-quality customer engagements.
Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Sales and Customer Success to ensure alignment between customer needs and platform evolution, and contribute to decisions that reach beyond your own function.
Serve as the voice of the field by capturing customer feedback and competitive insights that influence product strategy.
Own and report on the region’s operational and commercial metrics, including technical win rates, pipeline health, coverage and team performance.

What We’re Looking For

Leadership Experience: 15+ years in Solutions Architecture, Solutions Engineering, Technical Consulting or Enterprise Architecture, including 7+ years leading customer-facing technical teams, and a record of developing people into senior and leadership roles.
People Leadership: A proven record of hiring, coaching and developing high-performing Solutions Architecture or Solutions Engineering teams, and of building or transforming an organization rather than inheriting a healthy one.
Executive Presence: You command a room. You are credible in front of a CEO and their business leaders, the people who own the problem and the budget, and equally credible in front of a Chief Information Officer, a Chief AI Officer or a Chief Information Security Officer. You can move between the business case and the architecture without losing either audience.
Hands-On Technical Credibility: You are technical enough to be believed by a strong engineering bench. You work with models and agents yourself, you can pressure-test your team’s architecture, and you can be the most useful person in a design conversation when it matters. This is a player-coach seat, not an overlay.
Commercial Acumen: A demonstrated ability to partner with enterprise Sales leadership, influence strategic deals, and articulate business value to executive stakeholders. You have carried a number and can point to deals you personally moved.
Consulting Mindset: Experience leading complex enterprise solution engagements, developing business cases, implementation plans and executive-ready recommendations.
Technical Expertise: A strong understanding of modern AI architectures, including large language models, agentic systems, retrieval, enterprise integrations, cloud platforms, hybrid and on-premises deployments, security and governance.
Enterprise Experience: Experience designing and delivering enterprise technology solutions in complex, regulated or large-scale environments.
Cross-Functional Influence: A record of contributing to decisions beyond your own function, and of working effectively with Product and Engineering leadership.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience building or turning around a regional technical field organization, and evidence of what changed as a result.
Background in enterprise AI, cloud, or data platform companies, or applied AI consulting organizations.
Experience supporting customers in regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, energy, or the public sector.
Experience building repeatable solution-selling methodologies and helping generalist technical teams operate at a consistently high level.
A network of senior technical field talent you can attract to Cohere.
Experience operating in high-growth environments where speed, ownership and cross-functional collaboration are critical.

Full-Time Employees At Cohere Enjoy These Perks

A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.
Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.
RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.
100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.
Annual enrichment benefits:

Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.

Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)
Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

How And Where We Work

Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.
For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.
For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.
Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form, and we will work together to meet your needs.

We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.

Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers page.

Excellent communication and leadership skills

jobs.description:

Those in deal integration and valuation realisation at PwC will focus on assisting clients in successfully integrating acquisitions and maximising the value of their investments. The Opportunity

Leading high-profile analytics engagements across sell-side, buy-side, value creation, and performance improvement contexts, translating complex data into clear commercial insights
Helping management teams and investors understand business performance, growth drivers, customer behaviour, pricing, revenue quality, margins, operational efficiency, and value creation opportunities
Bringing together financial, commercial, operational, and technical perspectives to support fact-based decision making
Structuring ambiguous problems, defining analytical workplans, and guiding teams from data discovery through to executive-ready insights and deliverables
Leading business development activities, including opportunity identification, relationship building, proposal development, client pitches, and broader practice growth
Building relationships across PwC to support integrated client solutions, including across Deals, Consulting, Tax, Assurance, and data and AI teams
Supporting the development of the Value Creation Analytics practice, including methodologies, tools, reusable assets, delivery standards, and market-facing propositions
Coaching and developing team members across technical, commercial, financial, and client-facing skills
Most importantly, we need you to become a business partner and strategic advisor to our clients, translating and communicating your analysis to help answer critical commercial questions.

Significant experience in analytics, corporate finance, value creation, management consulting, corporate development, private equity, M&A, or a related field
Experience leading client engagements, managing teams, and delivering high-quality work under tight timelines

Experience working with complex data environments and guiding teams through data structuring, transformation, analysis, visualization, and insight development

Strong people leadership skills, with a demonstrated ability to coach, mentor, and develop high-performing teams

jobs.title: Director, Corporate Underwriting Analytics and Digital Risk
jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do.

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

Job Description:

Location
: hybrid, work from home

The Director, Corporate Underwriting Analytics and Digital Risk is a high performer in the underwriting risk community who thrives on the challenge of applying innovative problem-solving skills and solutions that align with Sun Life's risk tolerance. As a member of the Corporate Risk team, this person will foster a forward thinking, collaborative, and results oriented mindset within the team and key stakeholders throughout the Sun Life Enterprise. This position is a global risk role and will interact and liaise with risk management teams across the world.

What will you do?

Direct and complete activities related to the redesigning of existing programs to manage mortality and morbidity risk as they pertain to the underwriting risk management framework for the enterprise.
Develop performance management tools and processes to ensure compliance with the Enterprise Underwriting Operating Guideline.
Assess mortality and morbidity experience and report to the Corporate Chief Underwriter with thorough investigation of findings, assessment of any material risk implications, and recommendation for corrective actions.
Serve as an expert resource for referral of complex medically underwriting cases and financial underwriting risks. Make final decisions on complex underwriting risks within stated approval authority.
As Second Line of Defense, review and challenge the Business Unit's policies and practices to ensure compliance to the Underwriting Enterprise Operating Guideline.
Provide updates to the Director, Risk Controls and Compliance regarding any non-compliances to the UWEOG.
Develop strong relationships and partnerships with the Global Underwriting teams, product and pricing teams, Insurance Risk team and internal and external reinsurance partners.
Under the direction of the VP, Chief Underwriter, assist in driving changes to methodologies and practices which may present unfavorable mortality/morbidity experience through research, analysis of medical and non-medical risk factors, and presentation of key findings to underwriting leadership.

What do you need to succeed?

Minimum 10 years experience as an individual Life Underwriter, underwriting of multiple lines of business or products for multiple distribution channels.
Previous life approval authority of $10,000,000 and critical illness approval authority of $1,000,000.
Knowledge of and practical application of various risk assessment tools such as AI, risk propensity models, automated underwriting workflows, and various point of sales tools such as direct to consumer, and how they impact mortality/morbidity results as well as a strong understanding of non-medical issues such as fraud.
Knowledge of product development practices and concepts and assessment of risk to the organization, adherence to UWEOG and corporate risk appetite.
Ability to learn on the fly and with limited knowledge and in a dynamic work environment, as well as take a project from ideation to implementation.
Ability to apply underwriting, statistical analysis, mathematical, and actuarial knowledge to ensure delivery of team deliverables and implement projects/assignments to completion.
Knowledge of industry best practices and standards.
In-depth knowledge of underwriting risk assessment tools and standards as they relate to risk management programs.
Well-developed interpersonal as well as excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to work independently and make complex decisions in a risk setting.
As this position is posted in several locations, we specify that bilingualism (French, English, both oral and written) is required for Quebec only for the frequent interactions with English and French-speaking colleagues or internal partners across Canada or worldwide.

Reasons why should you join us under the sun

A collaborative and interactive team environment.
Opportunities to own your career development with programs to continuously learn, build skills, grow through coaching and more.
As a hybrid organization, you and your leader use business and Client needs to choose where you work, at home or in the office.
Our unique Sabbatical Program gives you the opportunity to take up to 6 weeks off, every five years.
We are proud to be on the 2026 Best Workplaces in Canada list by Great Place to Work.

The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.

Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

We are proud to be a hybrid organization that offers our employees the choice and flexibility to work from both the office and virtually based on the needs of the business, our Clients and you.

We may use artificial intelligence to support candidate sourcing, screening, interview scheduling.

We thank all applicants for showing an interest in this position. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.description:
Join one of Canada’s fastest-growing companies and be part of something extraordinary – welcome to goeasy
! At goeasy, our people and culture are at the heart of everything we do, and we’re proud to be recognized for it. We’ve earned prestigious accolades such as Waterstone Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures
and Canada’s Top Growing Companies
. We’re also honoured to be named a Greater Toronto Top Employer
and recognized by Great Place to Work®
as having the Best Workplaces for Women
& Most Trusted Executive Teams
, and included on TIME Magazine’s 2025 list of Canada’s Best Companies
. These honours reflect our commitment to fostering an inclusive, high-performance culture where talent thrives and innovation drives us forward.

As one of Canada’s leading alternative consumer lenders, we’re passionate about helping everyday Canadians create a brighter future. Our vision is to provide a path to a better tomorrow, today. We offer a full range of products, including non-prime leasing, unsecured and secured loans, and point-of-sale financing through easyhome
, easyfinancial
, and LendCare
.
If you're seeking an exciting, high-growth environment where your contributions truly matter, we want to hear from you! Join us, and together, let's create a future of financial empowerment.

About The Role

At goeasy, we believe everyone deserves access to fair and responsible credit. Every day, we help Canadians who are building or rebuilding their financial future access the products and support they need to move forward with confidence. We're looking for a Director, Collections Strategy & Performance
who understands that Collections is about more than recoveries. It's about finding the right balance between customer outcomes, responsible lending, risk management, and business performance. We are looking for a strategic and analytical problem solver who can use data, insights, and sound business judgment to identify opportunities and improve how we operate.

This is not a traditional Collections Director role.

You'll have the opportunity to influence strategy, lead transformation, and help shape the future of one of goeasy's most important functions. With significant autonomy and visibility, you'll partner across Operations, Analytics, Technology, Risk, and Compliance to build better experiences for customers while driving strong business results.

What You'll Do

Help define and execute the strategy for a critical part of goeasy's business.
Identify opportunities to improve customer outcomes, portfolio performance, and operational effectiveness.
Lead initiatives across Collections, Recoveries, Third-Party Partners, Offshore Operations, Technology, and Analytics.
Use data and insights to inform decisions and influence business strategy.
Diagnose complex and ambiguous business problems, identify underlying performance drivers, and develop practical solutions.
Translate analysis and insights into clear recommendations, priorities, and execution plans.
Develop performance frameworks, reporting, and operating rhythms that improve visibility, decision-making, and accountability.
Strengthen risk management, governance, and regulatory compliance practices.
Build and improve processes that create better experiences for customers and employees.
Develop high-performing teams and future leaders.
Bring new ideas, challenge assumptions, and help drive the next phase of goeasy's evolution.

What We're Looking For

8-15 years of leadership experience in Collections, Operations, Strategy, Risk Management, Financial Services, Consulting, Analytics or a related field.
Strong analytical capabilities and the ability to turn complex information into clear business insights and recommendations.
Demonstrated experience solving ambiguous business problems and identifying the underlying drivers of performance.
Strong business judgment, curiosity, and a practical, outcomes-oriented approach.
Experience leading large-scale business improvements and transformational change.
Strong business acumen, analytical capabilities, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to connect strategy with execution and lead initiatives from analysis through implementation.
Ability to balance customer needs, business objectives, and regulatory requirements.
Experience in Collections, call centre operations, third-party vendors, agencies, or offshore partners is considered an asset but is not required.

We offer a Flexible Work Program that provides you the ability to work three days onsite per week
, from our Mississauga office.

Internal Applicants:
please apply through the link and provide written endorsement from your current manager.

Why should you work for goeasy?

Financial Benefits

In keeping with our mission to create better tomorrows for our employees, each year goeasy commits to continuously enhancing its total rewards. Here are some of the perks we offer:
Performance-based annual bonus and long-term equity incentives designed to support leadership impact and long-term wealth creation.
As a TSX-listed company (GSY), goeasy offers long-term equity incentives, giving team members the opportunity to contribute to and benefit from our continued success.
Employee discounts on furniture, electronics, and appliances.
MAT & PAT leave top-up.

Leadership & Career Growth

Access to high-impact, high-visibility roles with direct influence on business outcomes.
Participation in goeasy’s executive leadership development programs.
Lead your own development journey with personalized growth plans, supported by coaching and mentorship to help you reach your leadership goals.
Fuel your personal and professional growth with our Tuition Assistance Program.

Health and Lifestyle

Immediate enrollment in comprehensive health, dental, and vision benefits.
Access 24/7 healthcare with Virtual Doctor Appointments.
Exclusive access to our free on-site goeasy gym and fitness studio at head office.
Explore a wide range of wellness options through our new Wellhub benefit – from fitness memberships to mental health resources.
Enjoy a state-of-the-art office space with perks like a games room, healthy snack program, free gated parking.
Give back with company-paid volunteer days and Company Matched Charitable Donations.

Diversity, Inclusion, And Equal Opportunity Employment

At goeasy, we believe that we can only be the best when people are able to bring their best selves to work every day. goeasy is committed to an inclusive, equitable and accessible workplace. By learning from each other’s differences, we gain strength through our people and our perspectives. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to providing accommodations (including accessible meeting rooms, captioning for virtual interviews, etc.) to help us remove barriers so that you can participate throughout the interview process. Please let the talent acquisition team know if you require an accommodation during any aspect of the recruitment process and we will work with you to address your needs.

Additional Information

All candidates considered for hire must successfully pass a criminal background check, credit check, and validation of their work experience to qualify for hire. We thank all interested applicants; however, we will only be contacting those for interview who possess the skills and qualifications outlined above.

jobs.title: Director, Pricing Strategy and Operations
jobs.description:
At Varicent, We’re Not Just Transforming The Sales Performance Management (SPM) Market—we’re Redefining How Organizations Achieve Revenue Success. Our Cutting-edge SaaS Solutions Empower Revenue Leaders Globally To Design Smarter Go-to-market Strategies, Maximize Seller Performance, And Unlock Untapped Potential. Varicent Stands At The Forefront Of Innovation, Celebrated As a Market Leader In The 2025 Forrester Wave Report For SPM, 2023 Ventana Research Revenue Performance Management (RPM) Value Index, Gartner Peer Insights, 2024 Gartner SPM Market Guide, And G2. Our Solutions Are Trusted By a Diverse Range Of Global Industry Leaders Like T-Mobile, ServiceNow, Wawanesa Bank, Shaw Industries, Moody's, Stryker And Hundreds More. Here’s Why You’ll Thrive At Varicent

Innovate with Purpose: Build impactful solutions for customers worldwide.
Join Excellence: Work in a diverse, collaborative, and innovative team.
Shape the Future: Lead in redefining revenue optimization.
Grow Together: Unlock your potential in a supportive environment.

Join us at Varicent—where your talent and ambition meet limitless opportunities for success!

Summary Of The Role And Team

As Director of Deal Desk & Pricing, you will lead and scale Varicent's Deal Desk function, serving as the central authority for deal governance, pricing operations, quote-to-booking processes, and commercial execution. You'll work closely with Sales, Customer Success, Renewals, Finance, Legal, Product, and Revenue Operations to drive pricing accuracy, data integrity, operational efficiency, and compliance throughout the customer lifecycle. This role combines strategic leadership with hands-on execution — you'll establish the processes, governance frameworks, systems alignment, and team structure that enable scalable growth. This is a people leadership role: you'll manage and grow Deal Desk professionals while improving deal velocity, profitability, forecasting accuracy, and operational excellence.

What You Will Be Doing

Lead and develop the Deal Desk team, including coaching, performance management, capacity planning, and workload prioritization.
Establish and run Deal Desk operating processes: deal intake, approvals, escalations, service-level expectations, and stakeholder communications.
Own quote-to-booking governance for new business, renewals, expansions, and cross-sell opportunities, ensuring pricing accuracy and policy compliance.
Work with Sales and Customer Success on deal structuring, pricing decisions, exception management, and commercial approvals.
Maintain data integrity and system alignment across Salesforce, CPQ platforms, pricing tools, and related commercial systems.
Partner with Finance on forecasting activities, revenue recognition requirements, commercial risk assessments, and audit readiness.
Build and maintain governance frameworks, policies, documentation, and enablement resources that drive consistent business practices.
Lead process improvement and change management initiatives to reduce deal cycle times and improve scalability and reporting quality.

What You Bring

Demonstrated expertise in Deal Desk, Pricing, Revenue Operations, Commercial Operations, FP&A, Commercial Finance, or related business functions (typically gained over 10–12+ years)
Experience leading teams, programs, or cross-functional operational functions (typically 5+ years)
Experience with complex B2B sales motions, including new business, renewals, expansions, and cross-sell transactions
Expertise in Deal Desk operations, pricing governance, quote-to-booking workflows, commercial approvals, and process design
Experience working with Salesforce, DealHub CPQ, or comparable CPQ/CRM platforms
Solid grasp of how pricing structures, commercial terms, ACV, and contract structures impact forecasting and revenue recognition
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a track record of using operational data to improve business processes and decisions
Ability to influence senior stakeholders across Sales, Finance, Legal, Customer Success, Product, and Revenue Operations

Success Outcomes

First 90 Days

Build a working understanding of Varicent's pricing structure, commercial processes, systems landscape, and quote-to-booking workflows.
Establish strong relationships with Sales, Customer Success, Finance, Legal, Product, and Revenue Operations stakeholders.
Assess current Deal Desk processes, governance controls, approval workflows, and reporting capabilities.
Identify opportunities to improve deal execution efficiency, data quality, and process consistency.

Within 6 Months

Roll out clear governance frameworks, approval structures, and operational standards across the Deal Desk function.
Raise quote quality, pricing accuracy, and first-pass approval rates while cutting rework and processing delays.
Set up consistent forecasting workflows with Finance using Deal Desk insights and commercial data.
Strengthen data integrity and alignment across Salesforce, CPQ platforms, pricing tools, and related systems.
Develop scalable team operating rhythms and performance metrics aligned to business objectives.

Within 12 Months

Position Deal Desk as a go-to strategic partner across Go-To-Market, Finance, and Executive teams.
Show measurable gains in deal cycle times, pricing governance, compliance, and forecasting accuracy.
Deliver scalable quote-to-booking processes that support growth while maintaining strong controls and audit readiness.
Build a high-performing Deal Desk organization with clear accountability and operational excellence.
Create a sustainable operating model that supports revenue growth, profitability objectives, and commercial scalability.

This posting is for a existing
vacancy.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

Welcome to TELUS Digital, where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital product consultancy and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture.

With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across eight core service areas: Digital Product Consulting, Digital Marketing Services, Data & AI, Strategy Consulting, Enterprise Technology, Enterprise Applications, Cloud Engineering, and QA & Test Engineering.

From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are, all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

Location

This role will be based out of one of our major US or Canada
office locations: Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.

The Opportunity

This business unit specializes in data-driven solutions and strategic AI implementation. We help our clients unlock the full potential of their data and transform their business through innovative, AI-powered strategies.

Our Managing Director, Data, AI & Cloud, will lead our Data & AI advisory, AI solutions, Data platforms, and cloud transformation capabilities. In this role, you will be responsible for driving the growth, profitability, and success of the practice. You will provide strategic guidance, lead cross-functional teams, and deliver outstanding client value across our global footprint. The Managing Director, Data, AI & Cloud will have P&L responsibility and will play a critical role in shaping our company's overall vision, strategy, and growth.

This is an exceptional opportunity for a talented and results-oriented leader to make a significant impact in shaping our company's future and driving data-driven solutions in the evolving digital landscape. If you are passionate about data, AI, and strategic consulting, we invite you to apply and join our high-performing team.

To learn more about our AI practice: https://www.telusdigital.com/solutions/enterprise-ai

To learn more about our Cloud practice: https://www.telusdigital.com/solutions/enterprise-technology-modernization/cloud-services

Responsibilities

Strategy and Leadership:

Collaborate with the executive leadership team to define the company's Data, AI & Cloud vision, strategy, and goals
Drive growth by identifying emerging trends, market opportunities, and industry best practices
Lead the planning, development, and execution of the Data, AI & Cloud strategic roadmap

P&L Responsibility

Assume overall accountability for the financial performance of the Data, AI & Cloud consulting practice
Partner with Practice Leaders and Business Development to continue to grow managed accounts
In partnership with Business Development, develop and implement effective revenue generation strategies to meet or exceed annual revenue targets
Monitor financial performance, identify areas for improvement, and implement corrective actions as necessary

Team Leadership And Management

Build and lead high-performing teams, including Data Engineers, Data Scientists, AI Strategists, and AI Engineers
Foster a culture of excellence, innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning within the Data, AI & Cloud teams globally and more broadly through the Practice Advisor team

Client Engagement And Delivery

Partner with clients to identify their business challenges and design tailored Data, AI & Cloud solutions
Oversee the delivery of high-quality data-driven insights, models, and strategic recommendations
Provide thought leadership and build trusted advisor relationships with key client stakeholders

Competencies

Experience

10+ years of relevant leadership and team management experience within a top-tier management consultancy (Partner-level) or global and publicly traded enterprise (VP, SVP, or C-level) with a focus on AI, Data Engineering, Data Science, or Related Fields
Leads a line of business for a mid-size to large consultancy (i.e., office, industry, etc.)
Leadership experience in technology consulting, project management, and executive partnerships

jobs.title: Chief Technology and Information Officer
jobs.description:
Who We Are

For more than 130 years, The Salvation Army has served people in need in communities across Canada and Bermuda. Building on our roots as a world-wide Christian church, each year we help more than 2 million people, providing necessities such as food, clothing and shelter. In addition, we support people experiencing unemployment, addiction and family challenges. We continually adapt and innovate to meet emerging needs and live out our mission, vision and values of hope, service, dignity and stewardship. As a faith- and values-based organization, we hire and serve people of all backgrounds and walks of life - there is a place for everyone to belong here.

Mission Statement

The Salvation Army exists to share the love of Jesus Christ, meet human needs and be a transforming influence in the communities of our world.

Job Description

POSITION PURPOSE SUMMARY

The Chief Technology and Information Officer (CTIO) provides enterprise leadership and strategic direction for technology, information systems, data, cybersecurity and digital capabilities across The Salvation Army Canada and Bermuda Territory.

As a senior organizational leader, the CTIO ensures technology strategy and investment support The Salvation Army’s mission, strategic priorities and operational needs. The role is accountable for technology, cybersecurity and resilience, enterprise systems, data and digital capability, technology operations, vendor partnerships, financial stewardship and the ongoing development of a high-performing technology function.

Working across a large, geographically dispersed and decentralized organization, the CTIO builds trusted relationships with leaders and stakeholders, balances enterprise consistency with operational realities, and drives technology adoption and organizational efficiencies in a way that reflects The Salvation Army’s mission, values and culture.

Accountabilities

Mission, Culture and Organizational Leadership

Authentically lead in alignment with The Salvation Army’s mission, vision, values, Christian identity and spiritual foundations, recognizing that its social and community services are expressions of its higher purpose to share the love of Jesus Christ, meet human needs and be a transforming influence in communities.
Ensure technology strategy, investment and decision-making ultimately enable people, ministry and services to advance the mission.
Contribute as an enterprise leader to organizational strategy, priorities and decisions beyond the technology portfolio.
Balance enterprise standards and priorities with legitimate operational, geographic and ministry-specific needs.

Executive and People Leadership

Build and lead a high-performing technology leadership team with clear accountability, a service-oriented culture, strong succession and workforce planning, and the appropriate balance of internal and external capability.
Provide strategic advice to senior leadership, translating complex technology, cybersecurity, data and digital issues into clear organizational choices, risks, opportunities and investment decisions.
Lead significant organizational change associated with technology transformation, recognizing that successful adoption depends on people, process, culture and technology.
Build strong relationships with operational leaders and users to understand needs and continuously improve technology effectiveness.
Model strong stewardship, integrity and accountability in leadership and decision-making.

Enterprise Technology Strategy

Develop and execute a multi-year enterprise technology strategy aligned with organizational priorities and mission.
Stabilize and simplify the technology environment, strengthening reliability, integration, interoperability and sustainable adoption.
Optimize existing technology platforms and investments before introducing new solutions.
Improve connectivity and interoperability between systems to create a more seamless technology and user environment.
Establish technology roadmaps, portfolio governance and prioritization that sequence investments appropriately and balance innovation, affordability, risk, organizational readiness and capacity.
Lead targeted modernization and transformation where it creates clear organizational value, while assessing emerging technologies thoughtfully.
Oversee the technology project and investment portfolio, ensuring appropriate governance, stakeholder engagement and benefits realization.

Cybersecurity, Data and Technology Risk

Provide executive oversight of cybersecurity, information security, privacy, technology risk and resilience.
Ensure appropriate controls, governance and compliance are in place to protect organizational information, systems and technology assets.
Maintain effective disaster recovery, business continuity and technology resilience capabilities.
Ensure security, privacy, data protection and risk considerations are embedded in technology investments, vendor relationships and emerging technology adoption.

Technology Operations and Service Delivery

Ensure reliable, secure, responsive and cost-effective delivery of enterprise applications, infrastructure, networks, cloud services, end-user technology and service management.
Establish service standards, performance measures and continuous improvement practices that strengthen user experience and technology effectiveness.
Maintain an enterprise technology architecture that supports integration, scalability, security and future organizational requirements.

Financial, Vendor and Investment Stewardship – Money, Sourcing and Commercial Discipline

Lead technology operating and capital budgets and multi-year investment planning, ensuring investments demonstrate strategic value, affordability and sustainability.
Oversee business cases, cost-benefit analysis and benefits realization for significant technology investments.
Establish effective sourcing strategies and lead strategic vendor relationships, contract performance and commercial negotiations.
Drive cost effectiveness through technology simplification, optimization, disciplined sourcing and effective management of technology assets and services.

Strategic Business Enablement, Data and Artificial Intelligence

Connect technology, data and digital priorities directly to organizational strategy, mission outcomes, service delivery and measurable value.
Act as an enterprise integrator across ministries, functions and geographies, using technology and data to simplify processes, strengthen service delivery and improve decision-making.
Lead enterprise data strategy, governance, stewardship, quality, analytics and reporting to enable trusted and actionable information.
Establish and oversee responsible AI and automation governance, ensuring use cases are mission-aligned, secure, ethical, legally compliant, operationally practical and supported by appropriate human oversight.
Establish governance and performance measures that allow senior leaders to monitor technology value, data maturity, digital adoption and AI readiness.

Education, Experience And Qualifications

Mission and Organizational Alignment

Demonstrated alignment with and ability to authentically lead within The Salvation Army’s mission, values and Christian foundations.
Demonstrated understanding that The Salvation Army’s social and community services are expressions of a broader mission to share the love of Jesus Christ, meet human needs and be a transforming influence in communities.
Ability to operate effectively within a large, complex, values-based and decentralized organization.
Demonstrated commitment to ethical leadership, stewardship, collaboration and service.

Education And Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, Engineering or a related discipline is required.
Master’s degree in Business Administration, Technology, Information Systems or a related field may be considered an asset.
Relevant executive technology, cybersecurity, enterprise architecture, governance or program management certifications may be an asset.
An equivalent combination of education and significant relevant executive experience may be considered.

Experience and Knowledge

Significant progressive leadership experience in technology, information systems, digital or related discipline, including substantial senior executive or enterprise leadership experience.
Demonstrated success developing and executing enterprise technology strategies and leading transformation or modernization.
Experience leading technology within a large, complex, multi-site and/or geographically dispersed organization.
Broad executive-level understanding of enterprise applications, infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity, data, integration, digital capability and technology operations.
Demonstrated experience overseeing cybersecurity, technology risk, resilience and business continuity.
Experience with enterprise data governance, analytics and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.
Significant experience managing technology budgets, investment decisions, strategic vendors and major contracts.
Proven success in building and developing high-performing leadership teams.
Demonstrated experience leading complex organizational change and influencing senior stakeholders.
Demonstrated experience advising executive leadership and governance bodies on technology strategy, investment, cybersecurity, risk and organizational implications.
Experience in a decentralized, faith-based, not-for-profit, healthcare, public sector or similarly complex service organization is considered an asset.
Demonstrated experience establishing or maturing enterprise data strategies, data governance, analytics capability and information management practices across a complex organization.
Experience reviewing, governing and deploying artificial intelligence or advanced automation capabilities with appropriate attention to ethics, privacy, cybersecurity, risk, adoption, benefits realization and operational readiness.

Skills And Leadership Capabilities

Strategic enterprise thinker who connects technology, data and digital priorities to organizational strategy and mission outcomes.
Strong executive judgment with the ability to prioritize competing demands and balance innovation, risk, cost, organizational capacity and readiness.
Proven people leader who builds organizational capability, develops senior leaders and creates clarity and accountability.
Exceptional relationship builder and influencer who can navigate a decentralized, relationship-driven organization while advancing enterprise priorities.
Clear and compelling communicator who translates complex technology issues into understandable organizational implications and decisions for technical and non-technical audiences.
Proven people leader who builds organizational capability, develops senior leaders and creates clarity and accountability.
Strong business, financial and commercial acumen, including technology investment, vendor management and benefits realization.
Data-driven and digitally fluent executive who can establish trusted information, enable analytics and guide responsible AI and automation adoption with appropriate governance and human oversight.
Values-based leader who demonstrates integrity, humility, stewardship and a strong service orientation.
Comfortable with complexity and ambiguity, with the ability to bring clarity, structure and direction to challenging organizational situations.

Compensation

The target hiring range for this position is $244,046.40 to $305,052.80 with a maximum of $366,059.20.

Placement in the salary range will be based on factors such as market conditions, internal equity, and candidate experience, skills, and qualifications relevant to the role.

At Seneca Polytechnic, we offer a flexible working environment that supports innovative thinking and encourages exploring new ideas and approaches. As we adapt to an ever-changing landscape, we continue to promote opportunities for career growth and development. We focus on health and well-being in all ways to provide great employee experience.

Chief Information Officer

Do you believe that technology, data, and digital platforms should open new possibilities? Are you motivated by the opportunity to lead large scale digital transformation while advancing equity, innovation, and employee and student success at one of Canada’s leading post-secondary institutions?

Seneca Polytechnic is seeking a Chief Information Officer
to provide institution-wide leadership and strategic direction for information technology, digital platforms, enterprise systems, and data. Reporting to the Vice President, Students and IT, you will play a critical role in shaping Seneca’s digital future, ensuring secure, reliable, and innovative technology services that support teaching, learning, research, and operations.

In this critical role, you will lead IT modernization, strengthen Seneca’s leadership in artificial intelligence, and partner with academic and administrative leaders to ensure technology investments deliver meaningful organizational value.

How You Approach the Role

Seneca operates in a complex post-secondary environment with rapid technological change, evolving learner needs, and increasing cybersecurity risks. In this context, you will

Set a clear and compelling vision for Seneca’s information technology and digital strategy, aligned with institutional priorities and long-term plans.
Lead the development and execution of a multi-year IT and digital transformation roadmap, including enterprise architecture and technology governance.
Advance innovation by collaboratively identifying and leveraging emerging technologies that enhance teaching, learning, research, and institutional effectiveness.
Maintain and grow Seneca’s leadership in artificial intelligence, ensuring responsible, ethical, and impactful application across the institution.
Embed principles of equity, diversity, and inclusion into technology strategies, policies, and service delivery.
Build strong partnerships with academic and administrative leaders to translate institutional needs into effective technology solutions.
Foster trust through transparent decision-making, thoughtful communication, and consistent follow through.

What You’ll Do in This Role

As CIO, you will provide strategic, operational, and people leadership across a broad and integrated portfolio, leading a senior IT leadership team and fostering collaboration, accountability, and high performance. You will ensure the secure, reliable, and effective delivery of enterprise technology services while overseeing cybersecurity, data privacy, system resilience, business continuity, and compliance. You will guide the modernization and lifecycle management of enterprise platforms, establish meaningful performance measures, and lead budgeting, resource allocation, vendor management, and contract negotiations. You will also strengthen staff engagement, professional development, and workforce sustainability within a complex and evolving technology environment.

What You Bring

You are a seasoned technology leader who balances strategic vision with operational excellence and brings extensive, progressive experience leading complex IT organizations, enterprise systems, digital transformation, and multi-year initiatives. You exercise strong judgment in managing risk, security, and compliance while enabling innovation, agility, and evidence-based decision-making through data, analytics, and emerging tools. An effective communicator and collaborative partner, you translate complex technical concepts into clear, actionable insights and influence diverse stakeholder groups. You have built inclusive, high-performing leadership teams and lead with integrity, accountability, transparency, and respect.

Seneca supports flexible and inclusive work practices, recognizing diverse leadership styles and experiences. We recognize that leadership experience may be gained through a variety of career paths, including community-based work, sector transitions, or lived experience alongside formal roles. A combination of education and experience will be considered.

Seneca is Canada’s leading, and Ontario's first, polytechnic with more than 40,000 full-time students and 18,500 part-time students. Since opening our doors for the first time more than 55 years ago, we remain dedicated to getting our students career and world-ready.

jobs.title: Director, Artificial Intelligence, Finance
jobs.description:
Overview

AtkinsRéalis is looking for a Director, Artificial Intelligence, Finance to turn the potential of AI into measurable improvements in how Finance works and how the business makes decisions.

This is a hands-on leadership role. The Director will define a practical AI strategy, identify the opportunities worth pursuing and lead a disciplined portfolio from business case through adoption and verified results. They will also personally design, build, test and help deploy practical Finance agents and AI-enabled workflows within approved enterprise environments.

Success means tangible outcomes: capacity released for higher-value work, faster and better-informed decisions, stronger controls, improved cash performance and protection of project margins. The role is not about deploying technology for its own sake or accumulating pilots that never change how Finance operates.

Leading a small team with a global mandate, the Director will bring together Finance leaders and process owners with the Financial Systems Centre of Excellence (CoE), IT, Global Digital, the Chief Digital Officer's'organization, and data, cybersecurity, privacy and risk specialists. They will develop Finance-specific strategy and governance within enterprise standards, not create competing platforms or policies.

You are a business-led AI and transformation leader who combines strategic ambition, financial discipline and genuine hands-on ability. You can inspire executives, challenge a weak business case and align Finance, Digital, IT and control teams. You are as comfortable discussing strategy as you are building an agent to test an idea with users.

Your role

Set The Strategy And Build Alignment

Define and communicate a value-first AI strategy and roadmap for Global Finance, aligned with Finance priorities, enterprise AI strategy, technology standards and the Financial Systems roadmap.
Determine where AI can materially improve outcomes, where conventional automation or process redesign is preferable, and where an opportunity should not proceed.
Build a shared agenda across FP&A, Controllership, Project Finance and other Finance teams; engage regional and business leaders to identify needs that can scale.
Advise Finance leadership on investment choices, dependencies and risks; secure sponsorship and rally teams that do not report to the Director.

Own a Disciplined Portfolio Of Use Cases

Establish transparent intake and prioritization connected to enterprise channels and governance; assess business value, process and data readiness, feasibility, adoption, total cost and risk.
Maintain a sequenced portfolio with named sponsors, accountable process owners, delivery partners, milestones and clear decisions to proceed, change direction or stop.
Prioritize a few opportunities with a credible path to impact over a large collection of pilots. Candidate areas include reporting commentary, Finance knowledge access, exception handling, forecasting support, collections and project-margin early warning; each requires its own assessment and business case.

Make The Business Case And Prove The Return

Require proportionate business cases before material investment, with baselines, expected benefits, implementation and ongoing costs, risks, dependencies, adoption assumptions and alternatives.
Distinguish time saved from capacity genuinely redeployed and from cost removed; do not treat these as interchangeable financial benefits.
Agree measurement methods and benefit owners before delivery; track investment and realized value at use-case and portfolio levels, with independent validation where appropriate.
Report candidly on adoption, net value, cost and control effectiveness; recommend whether to improve, scale or discontinue initiatives that underperform.

Build, Test And Demonstrate Solutions Personally

Personally design, build and refine selected Finance agents and AI-enabled workflows, especially early prototypes and focused solutions that accelerate learning.
Use Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio hands-on to configure agents, test them with users, assess reliability and improve outputs based on feedback.
Use AI tools regularly in professional work to improve analysis, research, drafting and workflow execution, applying appropriate review and data-handling requirements.
Turn Finance problems into working demonstrations; assess limitations and costs, and decide whether a solution should stop, improve or enter the approved production route.
Stay close enough to delivery to challenge designs, troubleshoot barriers and coach builders, without being the sole developer of enterprise-scale products; partner with Digital and IT on supported deployment.

Establish Practical, Responsible Governance

Translate enterprise AI policy and standards into a Finance operating model covering ownership, intake, risk assessment, testing, approvals, human oversight, monitoring and lifecycle management.
Partner with Digital, IT, the Chief Digital Officer's'organization, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Legal, Risk and Internal Audit to clarify decision rights and navigate the path from idea to approved production use.
Protect sensitive Finance and client information through appropriate access, validation, traceability and human review before AI outputs inform reporting or decisions.
Work with data and process owners on source quality, definitions and controls; reuse approved enterprise platforms and challenge unnecessary complexity without bypassing security or technology accountabilities.

Deliver Through Partnership And Adoption

Partner with the Financial Systems CoE so initiatives fit ERP, EPM and reporting architecture without creating competing technology roadmaps.
Agree delivery responsibilities with Digital and IT while retaining Finance accountability for business outcomes; redesign workflows with process owners around human decisions, exceptions and controls.
Lead communications, training and feedback to build user confidence; create reusable approaches that can scale across regions while respecting genuine process and risk differences.

Lead a Lean, High-impact Team

Build and coach a small team with commercial judgment, hands-on capability and delivery discipline; mobilize a federated network of Finance champions, process owners and enterprise specialists.
Create a culture of curiosity, constructive challenge, accountability and collaboration, including the confidence to recommend "not AI" when appropriate.
Represent Finance in enterprise AI forums and lead by example as both sponsor and practitioner: demonstrate tools, share what works and acknowledge limitations.

About You

A degree in Finance, Business, Technology, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience, is expected.
Significant experience leading AI, data, automation or digital transformation in a complex organization, with demonstrated outcomes beyond proofs of concept.
Experience navigating architecture, cybersecurity, privacy, data governance and risk requirements without losing sight of business value or delivery pace.
Deeper practical experience with Copilot Cowork or Claude Cowork, including a proven record of deploying agentic workflows and demonstrating value in another organization.
Demonstrated hands-on experience building, testing and deploying AI agents, preferably in Microsoft Copilot Studio, with examples you personally created or materially developed.
Experience in an engineering, professional-services or project-based business; familiarity with enterprise Finance platforms, including Oracle-based environments.
Working knowledge of generative AI, agents, analytics and intelligent automation, sufficient to build focused solutions and challenge complex technical designs.
Strong understanding of Finance processes and decisions, ideally including FP&A, reporting, project or contract performance, working capital and financial controls.
Evidence of moving solutions beyond demonstrations to adoption, changed workflows and measurable business outcomes.
Active, capable use of Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT or Claude in day-to-day professional work, with sound judgment about approved tools, sensitive information and human review.
Proven ability to build investment cases, evaluate total cost and alternatives, establish benefit baselines and demonstrate return on investment.
Exceptional collaboration, executive communication and matrix leadership skills; sound judgment about when to scale, simplify or stop.

Rewards & benefits

Explore the rewards and benefits that help you thrive – at every stage of your life and your career at AtkinsRéalis in Canada.

Enjoy competitive compensation, employee recognition, and a brilliant range of flexible benefits you can tailor to your health, wellbeing, financial and lifestyle needs.

Make the most of diverse opportunities for training and professional development to grow your skills and expertise.

And take advantage of our hybrid working culture and generous time-off policies to balance a fulfilling career with your personal life.

Be rewarded. Find out more.

We're AtkinsRéalis, a world-class engineering services and nuclear organization. We connect people, data and technology to transform the world's'infrastructure and energy systems. Together, with our industry partners and clients, and our global team of consultants, designers, engineers and project managers, we can change the world. We're committed to leading our clients across our various end markets to engineer a better future for our planet and its people.

jobs.title: Interim Chief Information Officer
jobs.description:
IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Chief Information Officer

Reports to: President

Location: Greater Toronto Area, Ontario

Duration: 6-12 Months

Hybrid working

Our client, a large and complex Ontario post-secondary institution, is seeking an accomplished Interim Chief Information Officer
to provide leadership through an important period of transition, modernization and organizational evolution.

This is an exciting opportunity for a seasoned technology executive who can combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution
.

The organization recognizes that technology has the potential to play a much greater role in how it operates, how decisions are made, how services are delivered and how students experience the institution. The Interim CIO will be asked not simply to manage the existing technology environment, but to challenge conventional thinking about how technology is deployed and where it can fundamentally improve the operating model.

Leading a team of more than 100 technology professionals, the successful executive will initially provide stability, clarity and leadership through transition. Beyond this, they will help establish the priorities, capabilities, operating model and roadmap required for the next stage of the organization's technology journey.

This is therefore a mandate for a builder, modernizer and objective disruptor
, someone able to respect what is working while constructively challenging what could be done differently.

The Mandate

The Interim CIO will provide overall leadership to the technology function while working closely with the organization's senior leadership team to determine how technology can better enable its academic, student and operational priorities.

A central component of the mandate will be assessing the technology operating model
and identifying opportunities to improve effectiveness, service, scalability and value.
The Interim CIO will be expected to create alignment between technology strategy and organizational strategy, while maintaining a bias toward execution and measurable outcomes.

Key priorities will include:

Technology Strategy & Operating Model

Assess the current technology environment, capabilities, organizational structure and priorities and establish a clear roadmap for the next phase of modernization.
Challenge existing assumptions around how technology services are organized, delivered and supported.
Identify opportunities to simplify processes, reduce complexity, improve scalability and improve the value generated from technology investment
.
Evaluate the appropriate balance between internal capabilities, external partnerships, managed services and selective outsourcing.
Introduce stronger prioritization and governance disciplines to ensure technology resources are focused on the areas of greatest institutional impact.
Translate technology strategy into a practical execution agenda with clear accountabilities and outcomes.

Leadership Through Change

The Interim CIO will inherit a substantial team of 100+ technology professionals
and will need to quickly establish credibility and provide visible, confident leadership.

The organization operates within a unionized environment. Accordingly, the executive must understand how to lead meaningful organizational and operational change while respecting collective agreements, established processes and employee relationships.

The successful individual will:

Provide stability and clarity during transition.
Assess organizational capability, structure and accountabilities.
Coach and develop technology leaders.
Build stronger accountability for results.
Engage employees in the modernization journey.
Create a strong service and performance culture.
Navigate change thoughtfully within a complex unionized environment
.
Maintain momentum while making difficult decisions where required.

ERP Optimization & Enterprise Platforms

An important priority will be continuing to optimize the organization's ERP and broader enterprise technology environment.

The Interim CIO will:

Assess the current ERP implementation and identify opportunities to increase adoption, functionality and organizational value.
Address process, integration, data and operating-model issues that may inhibit the organization from realizing the full value of its enterprise platforms.
Challenge the proliferation of unnecessary processes, applications and workarounds where these create complexity.
Ensure technology modernization is accompanied by process modernization rather than simply automating existing ways of working
.
Strengthen the connection between enterprise systems, organizational processes and user experience.

Cybersecurity, Risk & Resilience

Cybersecurity will be a significant part of the mandate.

The Interim CIO will assess and evolve the organization's cybersecurity posture, governance and protocols, ensuring they remain appropriate for a large, complex and highly distributed post-secondary environment.

The executive will work to strengthen areas including security governance, accountability, organizational awareness and operational resilience, while ensuring cybersecurity is understood as an enterprise risk rather than simply an IT responsibility
.

The successful candidate will balance increasingly sophisticated security requirements with the accessibility, flexibility and innovation expected within a modern educational institution.

Cloud & Technology Modernization

The organization has begun elements of its cloud journey, but further opportunity remains to modernize its technology architecture and operating environment.

The Interim CIO will assess where further migration and modernization create genuine operational, financial, resilience or user-experience benefits.

They will bring an objective perspective regarding cloud strategy, legacy environments, technical debt, architecture and application rationalization
, ensuring modernization is driven by institutional value rather than technology for technology's sake.

Data Governance, Analytics & Decision Support

Data represents a significant opportunity for the organization.

The Interim CIO will help establish stronger data governance, ownership, quality and analytics capabilities
, enabling leaders across the institution to make better and faster decisions based on reliable information.

The mandate will include helping the organization move beyond reporting toward a culture where trusted data and actionable insights routinely inform operational, financial, academic and student-focused decision-making.

This will require both technology leadership and the ability to address the governance, accountability and behavioural changes necessary to establish a more mature data culture.

Artificial Intelligence

The organization recognizes the potentially significant role AI could play in both its operating model and the broader evolution of post-secondary education.

The Interim CIO will help leadership distinguish between experimentation and sustainable enterprise adoption, identifying practical opportunities where AI, automation and emerging technologies can improve productivity, decision-making and service delivery
.

Equally important will be establishing appropriate governance around the adoption of these technologies, including cybersecurity, privacy, data, risk and responsible use.

The successful executive will bring curiosity and ambition around AI while maintaining the pragmatic judgment required to translate emerging technology into sustainable institutional value.

The Evolving Student Experience

Technology is increasingly integral to the complete student journey.

How students learn, interact with faculty, access services, consume information and engage with an institution continues to evolve.

The Interim CIO will work across the organization to consider how technology can help create a simpler, more integrated, personalized and contemporary student experience
.

The opportunity extends beyond classroom technology. It is about understanding how technology can differentiate the institution and reduce friction across the entire student journey.

Service Culture

A key leadership priority will be continuing to evolve the technology function toward a highly responsive, accountable and customer-focused service organization.

The Interim CIO will establish clear expectations around service delivery, ownership, responsiveness and partnership with internal stakeholders.

Technology should increasingly be viewed as an enabler and partner to the organization
, rather than simply a provider of systems and infrastructure.

The Ideal Interim Executive

The successful candidate will be an accomplished CIO or senior enterprise technology executive
who has led a sizeable, complex technology function through significant modernization and organizational change.

They will bring experience across a combination of:

Enterprise technology strategy and execution.
Leadership of large, multidisciplinary technology teams.
Technology operating-model transformation.
ERP and enterprise application optimization.
Cloud migration and modernization.
Cybersecurity, risk and technology governance.
Data governance, analytics and information management.
AI, automation and emerging technologies.
Process optimization and organizational simplification.
Managed services, strategic sourcing and outsourcing.
Vendor and commercial management.
Digital/customer experience transformation.
Leadership in a unionized environment.
Organizational change and talent development.

Experience within higher education or the broader public sector
would be highly relevant, although the organization will also be interested in executives from other large, complex and regulated environments who can bring fresh thinking and transferable experience.

Leadership Style

This mandate requires more than technical credibility.

The ideal executive will be pragmatic, curious, commercially minded and comfortable challenging the status quo
. They will know when to listen and preserve institutional knowledge, but equally when to push the organization toward a different approach.

They will be capable of moving comfortably between the boardroom and the technology organization, translating complex technology issues into clear discussions about risk, cost, service, productivity and organizational outcomes
.

Most importantly, this individual will be an objective disruptor with strong execution discipline
.
They will leave the organization not simply with better technology, but with a stronger technology function, clearer priorities, improved governance, better use of data, enhanced cybersecurity and a pragmatic roadmap for how technology can enable the institution's future operating model.

The attraction of the assignment

For an experienced CIO, this is a rare opportunity to have meaningful impact in a relatively short period.

The mandate combines people leadership, technology modernization, ERP optimization, cyber, cloud, data and analytics, AI, operating-model transformation and student experience
within one of the most rapidly changing sectors in Canada.

The successful interim will have the platform to challenge existing thinking, accelerate decisions and help redefine the role technology plays across the institution.

This is not a mandate to simply keep the lights on. It is an opportunity to shape what technology leadership, capability and service should look like for the organization's next chapter.

to lead and evolve our strategy practice across the Americas. Experience working across brand, marketing, data, and technology transformation initiatives.
Established relationships with strategic alliance or technology partners.
Experience supporting global clients and large-scale transformation programs.

position based in Canada

Citi, the leading global bank, has approximately 200 million customer accounts and does business in more than 160 countries and jurisdictions. About the Team:

Citi is looking for a Lead AI/ML Data Scientist
to join the Olympus Data Reconciliation and Engineering team, where you will shape the next generation of AI and machine learning capabilities powering enterprise-scale reconciliation across global processing hubs.

In this role, you will drive the full lifecycle of ML model development — from ideation and architecture through to deployment and adoption — delivering measurable impact across Capital Markets operations, risk, and finance. Your work will sit at the intersection of advanced data science and real-world financial systems, influencing outcomes at a global scale.

Responsibilities:

Design, build, and deploy AI and machine learning models — including Agentic AI and Generative AI solutions — to solve complex reconciliation and data engineering challenges at enterprise scale.
Lead the end-to-end ML model development lifecycle, from requirements gathering and data preprocessing through to ensemble modeling, validation, and production integration.
Analyze large volumes of structured and unstructured financial data to uncover trends, patterns, and opportunities for optimization across banking platforms.
Define and deliver ML model roadmaps in collaboration with technical and business teams, ensuring alignment with project timelines, budgets, and Citi's architecture standards.
Translate complex data findings into clear visualizations and strategic recommendations that inform decisions made by senior business and technology leaders.
Partner with engineering, operations, and cross-functional teams to ensure seamless model integration, long-term scalability, and reliable performance in production environments.
Identify and communicate technology risks and their business implications, developing mitigation strategies and maintaining transparency with stakeholders at all levels.
Maintain comprehensive model documentation and support knowledge transfer to ensure continuity and adoption across teams.

Technical Expertise:

6+ years hands-on experience in AI/ML development and big data engineering within Financial Services, Insurance, or Telecom environments
Expert-level proficiency in Python (scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch, Pandas, NumPy), R (caret, tidyverse, mlr3), and SQL (PostgreSQL, Oracle, MySQL)
Deep technical knowledge implementing supervised and unsupervised ML algorithms: linear/logistic regression, neural networks (CNN, RNN, LSTM, Transformers), k-means clustering, DBSCAN, decision trees (CART, C4.5), and ensemble methods (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost)
Proven experience building and deploying Agentic AI and LLM-based solutions using:
LangGraph for complex agent orchestration and state management
LangChain for chain-of-thought reasoning and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
Agent Development Kit (ADK) for enterprise-grade autonomous agent development

Beneficial Skills & Qualifications:

Hands-on experience with advanced statistical modeling: Generalized Linear Models (GLM), Random Forest, Gradient Boosting (AdaBoost, XGBoost), and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques including text mining, topic modeling (LDA), and sentiment analysis
Experience with model versioning and experiment tracking tools (Mlflow, Weights & Biases, DVC)
Proficiency with Git/GitHub/Bitbucket for version control and collaborative development
Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines for ML model deployment (Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions)
Familiarity with data visualization libraries (Matplotlib, Seaborn, Plotly) and BI tools (Tableau, Power BI)
Experience with real-time streaming data frameworks (Kafka, Kinesis)
Passion for staying current with emerging AI/ML frameworks, research papers, and open-source contributions

Education:

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science
, Data Science
, Software Engineering

, Statistics
or related fields of study.
