jobs.title: Senior Director, Financial Planning and Analysis
jobs.description:
Join a Challenger

At EQ, we're remaking banking so every Canadian gets ahead, every day. Serving nearly 4 million Canadians from coast to coast, we offer a wide variety of financial services from banking and lending, to trust and credit union solutions.

We've been at this since 1970, challenging the conventions of traditional banking with smarter, faster, and more connected financial experiences.

What's kept us moving?
The people behind it all: challengers who ask better questions, push back on old assumptions, and look for a better way forward.

If you're driven to help reshape how banking works for Canadians and the businesses that power our economy, this could be your next big opportunity.

We can’t wait to get to know you!

The Work

The Senior Director, Financial Planning and Analysis leads the Bank’s enterprise financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, and management reporting activities and oversees the Financial Planning & Analysis Centre of Excellence within the VP, Financial Planning & Analysis portfolio. The role establishes an integrated view of financial performance, outlook, risks, and opportunities to support executive decision-making and disciplined resource and capital allocation.

The role partners with business and functional leaders to translate strategic priorities into financial plans, challenge assumptions, assess performance drivers, and provide timely, decision-useful insight. It is accountable for the quality, consistency, governance, and continuous improvement of planning and forecasting processes and for establishing a high-performing Financial Planning & Analysis Centre of Excellence that scales common standards, tools, models, data, and insight across the Bank.

Financial Planning, Forecasting & Performance Management

Lead the annual budget, periodic forecast, and multi-year financial planning processes, integrating business plans, economic assumptions, balance sheet and income statement drivers, and enterprise priorities.
Establish planning calendars, standards, controls, accountabilities, and review forums that support complete, accurate, timely, and comparable submissions across the Bank.
Provide an integrated view of actual and forecast performance, including revenue, net interest margin, expenses, profitability, return on equity, capital implications, and key non-financial drivers.
Lead scenario and sensitivity analysis to assess the financial implications of changing market conditions, strategic choices, investments, and emerging risks.
Identify material variances, trends, and forecast risks; ensure clear ownership of actions and provide concise recommendations to senior leadership.

Capital Forecasting, Strategic Capital Allocation, ICAAP & Stress Testing

Lead enterprise capital forecasting and provide a forward-looking view of regulatory capital, leverage, capital generation, and deployment under the strategic and financial plan.
Assess capital capacity, requirements, and trade-offs to support the allocation of capital to strategic investments, business growth, acquisitions, and other enterprise priorities.
Partner with Treasury, Risk Management, business leaders, and other Finance teams to align capital forecasts with earnings, balance sheet growth, risk-weighted assets, funding plans, internal capital targets, and management buffers.
Lead the consolidation of financial forecasts and capital impacts for the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process, enterprise-wide stress testing, regulatory stress testing, and related scenario analysis.
Evaluate adverse but plausible scenarios, key sensitivities, and management actions; identify potential capital constraints or vulnerabilities and recommend actions to protect resilience and support strategic objectives.
Establish robust governance, controls, documentation, and executive reporting for capital assumptions, methodologies, forecasts, stress-testing outputs, and capital-allocation decisions.

Executive & Strategic Financial Storytelling

Lead the development and presentation of clear, Board-ready financial narratives that explain enterprise performance, outlook, key drivers, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions.
Translate complex financial, operational, and strategic analysis into concise, decision-oriented messages tailored to the Board, executive leadership, and management governance forums.
Provide strategic oversight of consolidated financial results and outlook, ensuring consistency across the income statement, balance sheet, capital, business segments, and key performance indicators.
Connect actual and forecast performance to the Bank’s strategy, external environment, and value-creation priorities, highlighting the implications of trends, trade-offs, and emerging issues.
Establish executive communication standards that are punchline-first, analytically sound, and supported by clear evidence, sensitivities, and actionable recommendations.
Coordinate across Finance, Treasury, Strategy, Investor Relations, Risk Management, and business finance partners to maintain a consistent enterprise financial story across Board, executive, regulatory, and external materials.

Management Reporting, Data & Insight

Oversee recurring management reporting and dashboards, ensuring that measures, definitions, commentary, and source data are consistent and decision-useful.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators and financial drivers that connect strategic objectives, operating activity, and financial outcomes.
Strengthen data quality, model governance, documentation, controls, and review practices for material planning and management reporting outputs.
Drive automation and simplification of planning, forecasting, modelling, and reporting processes to improve speed, accuracy, transparency, and analytical capacity.
Partner with Data and Technology stakeholders on requirements, prioritization, testing, implementation, and adoption of financial planning and analytics capabilities.

Leadership, Governance & Continuous Improvement

Establish and oversee the Financial Planning & Analysis Centre of Excellence, including its mandate, governance, operating model, service catalogue, priorities, measures, and capability roadmap.
Develop common planning, forecasting, modelling, reporting, and business-partnering standards, and support adoption across Financial Planning & Analysis and partner teams.
Build reusable tools, templates, driver libraries, scenario models, data definitions, and analytical practices that improve consistency, speed, and decision usefulness.
Create a community of practice that strengthens capability through coaching, knowledge sharing, quality review, and continuous learning.
Lead, coach, and develop a team of finance professionals; establish clear accountability, effective succession and development practices, and high standards for analysis and communication.
Maintain an effective control environment for planning, forecasting, modelling, and management reporting, and address issues identified through review, audit, or control testing.

Lets Talk About You!

University degree in finance, accounting, economics, business, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
CPA or CFA designation or an equivalent recognized finance designation.
At least 12 years of progressive finance experience, including substantial experience in financial planning and analysis, forecasting, management reporting, financial modelling, and executive decision support.
Senior leadership and people-management experience, including experience setting functional priorities, reviewing complex work, coaching leaders and professionals, and delivering through others.
Advanced knowledge of financial statements, performance drivers, budgeting, forecasting, scenario analysis, profitability, return on equity, and capital-aware decision-making within financial services.
Experience producing and presenting concise analysis for executives and governance forums, with the judgment to distinguish material issues, challenge assumptions, and recommend action.
Advanced spreadsheet and presentation skills and experience with enterprise planning, reporting, business intelligence, and financial data tools. Specific systems: To be confirmed.
Strong written and verbal communication, stakeholder-management, analytical, problem-solving, organization, and change-leadership skills.
Experience in a Canadian bank or other regulated financial institution, including knowledge of banking products, net interest margin, balance sheet drivers, capital, and regulatory considerations.

What we offer [For full-time permanent roles]

💰 Competitive discretionary bonus

✨ Market leading RRSP match program

🩺 Medical, dental, vision, life, and disability benefits

📝 Employee Share Purchase Plan

👶🏽 Maternity/Parental top-up while you care for your little one

🏝 Generous vacation policy and personal days

🖥 Virtual events to connect with your fellow colleagues

🎓 Professional development and comprehensive Career Development program

💛 A fulfilling opportunity to join one of the top FinTechs and help create a new kind of banking experience

The incumbent will be working hybrid and in office time will be spent working from EQ Bank’s additional office space located at 2200-25 Ontario Street, Toronto, ON
.

Equity, Diversity & Inclusion

EQ is committed to building an inclusive, accessible environment where every employee feels valued, respected, and supported. We believe our organization is stronger — and our people thrive — when we honour and celebrate diverse experiences, identities, and perspectives. We’re equally committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally.

jobs.description:

What You'll Be Doing

As a member of CIBC’s AI, Data and Analytics team, the Senior Director – Decision Science will lead the Insurance Decision Science team and be responsible for developing and executing strategic initiatives across a range of CIBC Insurance products and projects. This is a senior technical leadership role that combines actuarial, statistical, data science and AI enablement capabilities. The role naturally involves a comprehensive understanding of Creditor (Bank Authorized) and Non-Authorized insurance products. You’ll exercise a high degree of independent judgement, setting the technical direction and standards for decision science activities that support pricing, profitability, growth, forecasting, portfolio performance and strategic decision making. You will develop and maintain trusted relationships across the Insurance business, larger Retail Banking organization and the technology and data science communities. In addition, you’ll translate sophisticated analysis of complex business information into clear recommendations for executives and business leaders, while providing independent challenge to assumptions, forecasts and proposed courses of action. You’ll drive innovation across areas of your responsibility and apply expert interpersonal, communication and problem-solving skills.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You'll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you'll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You'll Succeed

Strategy and Planning – Contribute to long-term strategy for the business in collaboration with insurance product and business leaders. Translate actuarial and advanced analytics into decisions on pricing, profitability, growth, forecasting and portfolio performance; identify opportunities, develop strategic proposals and independently challenge key assumptions and targets. Collaborate with internal partners to oversee, communicate and align business plans and ensure delivery on strategy and intended business outcomes.

Build differentiated technical capabilities, establish clear role and proficiency standards, and create development pathways that strengthen the team over time. Manage capacity to ensure initiatives are appropriately staffed, identify capability gaps and remove obstacles to performance. Create a positive work environment and role model by championing CIBC’s mission, vision and values. Comply with policies, standards, guidelines and controls by applying them fairly and consistently so employees understand what to expect.

You are a senior actuarial and analytics leader with strong quantitative knowledge and relevant industry experience. You have a high degree of Insurance product knowledge and understand the regulatory landscape. You have expert knowledge of insurance products (both authorized and non-authorized), banking and insurance frameworks, and the risk and compliance considerations that shape product decisions.
You can demonstrate extensive experience in product management, strategic planning, and project management sufficient to identify, develop, and implement approved initiatives. You give meaning to data. You enjoy investigating complex problems, and making sense of information. You're confident in your ability to communicate detailed information in an impactful way.
You’re an effective leader and collaborator. You build strong relationships across teams, use sound judgment, manage multiple priorities effectively and help create an environment where people can do their best work. Purpose

As the Director of Commercial Pricing and Data Governance at UNFI, you are responsible for developing and executing the company's enterprise-wide pricing strategy while leading the Data Governance function. Your role is critical in driving commercial excellence, ensuring data integrity, and enabling informed business decisions across the organization.

In the area of pricing, your scope includes building and leading a centralized pricing department that will define, govern, and continuously improve UNFI Canada’s brand and customer pricing strategy. This role will move the organization toward a more disciplined pricing model, shifting pricing ownership away from Sales over time so that Sales can remain focused on customer relationships, execution of brand strategies, and commercial growth. You will immediately assume leadership of pricing activities currently managed within SRM and RGM, while developing the structure, tools, processes, resource requirements, governance model, and transition plan required to bring Sales pricing responsibilities into the pricing organization in the medium term. You will establish clear decision-making protocols, pricing guardrails, escalation processes, analytical capabilities, and best practices to support consistent, data-driven pricing decisions that improve margin performance, strengthen customer and supplier strategies, and deliver both immediate and long-term revenue value.

In the area of Data Governance, you will lead the Retalix Pricing, Retalix Maintenance, and MCB teams. You are accountable for ensuring data quality, governance, and integrity across Supplier Services, including pricing updates, GS1 data management, new brand onboarding information, and system master data maintenance. Your leadership will ensure that core data processes are effectively managed and aligned with business and operational requirements.

By partnering closely with cross-functional teams and senior leaders, you will enable the successful execution of UNFI's strategic priorities through the effective use of data and analytics. You will foster a culture of accountability, agility, and data-driven decision-making while ensuring alignment with UNFI's vision and objectives. Ultimately, your role is to drive sustainable revenue growth, improve profitability, and maximize the value of data as a strategic asset across the organization.

Review and optimize our current pricing tools and governance
Immediately take on SRM/RGM pricing and bring forward the recommendation (inclusive of tools and resources) to take pricing on from the sales team

jobs.description:
About QuadReal Property Group

QuadReal Property Group is a global real estate investment, development and operating company headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia. Its assets under management are $98.5 billion. From its foundation in Canada as a full-service real estate operating company, QuadReal has expanded its capabilities globally for investments in equity and debt in both the public and private markets. QuadReal invests directly through operating platforms in which it holds an ownership interest and via programmatic partnerships.

QuadReal seeks to deliver strong investment returns while creating sustainable environments that bring value to the people and communities it serves. Now and for generations to come.

QuadReal: Excellence lives here.

www.quadreal.com

Role Description

The Director, Enterprise Data Governance is accountable for defining and governing the enterprise data QuadReal relies on, anchored in DAMA-DMBOK, covering data definitions, ownership, quality, and observability. This makes QuadReal's data reliable enough to be governed, measured, and controlled, reducing the risk that decisions, reporting, and controls rest on data that can't be trusted. The role reports to the VP, Risk & Integrated Assurance and turns the VP's enterprise-wide mandate into one accountable operating model focused on risk mitigation through data governance lens.

Success is measured by the risk it mitigates: data issues caught before they become decisions made on incorrect information, ownership gaps closed before they become accountability gaps. Holding up under audit is one key aspect of that risk mitigation but not the goal in itself.

The Director also supports the VP's overall view of QuadReal's risk and control environment and represents Data Governance in Risk & Integrated Assurance reporting.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Data Governance
Define QuadReal’s enterprise data definitions, classifications, and Critical Data Elements (CDEs), anchored in DAMA-DMBOK.
Own the data ownership and accountability model: name Data Owners, Stewards, and Custodians, and hold them accountable through a defined sign-off cadence.
Deliver the enterprise business glossary under a tiered governance model, and maintain metadata management, lineage standards, and dbt metadata synchronization across the platform.
Set data quality thresholds and Trusted Layer certification criteria, and hold data observability (freshness, pipeline health, trust scores) to the same standard as financial controls.
Align controls as gates across the data delivery lifecycle (ingestion, definition, build, use, and govern), so a control fires wherever data advances and nothing reaches a certified output without passing.
Build data governance capability across the business through training and playbooks, rather than keeping expertise centralized.
Integration and Decision Authority
Act as the link between Business Controls and Data Governance called for in the integrated operating model: define control standards and evidence expectations alongside data definitions, and build controls into new systems and initiatives from the start.
Where control standards and data definitions conflict, collaborate with relevant stakeholders including, ED&A, Business Owners and Business Controls to resolve these inconsistencies. Work with ED&A / Technology and the Data Platform team so controls and governance are proactively built into the toolchain (Microsoft Fabric, dbt, Airflow, Power BI, Purview, Entra ID, Quadrant) by design.
Represent Data Governance in Risk & Integrated Assurance meetings and support Audit Committee reporting.
Team Leadership
Lead and develop direct report(s) and set clear deliverables and cadence for them..
Build team capability in data analytics, AI literacy, and integrated systems controls as the role grows, and build bench strength to move the environment from project to sustained run-state without single points of failure.
Build a “one team” culture between Business Controls and Data Governance that removes duplicate work and closes the gaps that used to sit between the two groups.

What Success Looks Like

Controls operating as gates, each with a named owner and re-performable evidence.
Audit outcomes: clean walkthroughs, deficiencies remediated, and SOC scope defensible.
Glossary and standards adopted, so certified numbers are built on agreed definitions.
Governance measured by delivery: trusted, in-use data products standing behind reported figures.
Direct reports delivering to plan, with growing capability and bench strength.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, Risk Management, Data Management, Computer Science, or a related discipline; Master is an asset.
8+ years of progressive experience across data governance, risk management, or audit, including at least 2 years leading people, and demonstrable end-to-end delivery of a control or governance environment.
Working knowledge of ICFR, SOC 1 / ISAE 3402, COSO 2013, ITGCs, and DAMA-DMBOK; CPA, CIA, CISA, or CDMP an asset. Familiarity with DCAM / CDMC and data contracts an asset.
Hands-on experience with data cataloguing and governance tooling (Microsoft Purview equivalents such as Collibra an asset) and with controls testing in an ICFR or SOX environment.
Working knowledge of a modern data-platform stack (Microsoft Fabric / lakehouse, dbt, Airflow, Power BI, Entra ID), enough to specify and validate controls.
Working knowledge of Yardi strongly preferred.
Investment and portfolio management literacy or business acumen
Proven ability to build controls that produce retained, re-testable evidence.
Ability to work across Finance, IT, and Data & Analytics, and turn technical and operational complexity into clear governance and control frameworks.
Comfortable preparing materials for senior leadership and the Audit Committee.
Comfortable building or growing an early-stage function.
Experience within real estate, asset management, pension, or investment management environments strongly preferred.

This is a newly created role within our organization.

The expected annualized base salary range for this role is $155,000 – $175,000.

Based on the position, QuadReal offers a competitive total rewards package in addition to the base pay, which may include a performance-based incentive plan, comprehensive health & dental benefits, pension plan, and paid time off.

The actual salary offered will take into consideration a wide array of factors including, but not limited to, the individual’s skill, experience, education and training, the market compensation of the role, and the consideration to internal equity.

We value diverse experiences and perspectives. Even if your skills don’t align 100% with the listed qualifications or salary range, we encourage you to apply – you may be a great fit for this role or others in our community. Applicants may also be considered for alternative positions within the organization where their qualifications and experience align more closely with available opportunities.

jobs.title: VP, Digital
jobs.description:
The Vice President, Digital runs the commercial operation of the digital channel, turning merchandising, marketing and loyalty offers into activated onsite experiences that make the eCommerce plan achievable.

Reporting to the SVP, Digital & Loyalty, accountability spans onsite execution end to end: the merchandising experience, digital assortment and promo activation, online assortment expansion (2P ownership), product content health, and the product data that helps customers discover products, build intent to purchase, and ultimately convert. The mandate is delivered in close partnership with the COO organization. As the primary digital partner to the Banner Presidents and merchandising teams, the VP translates banner and category plans into onsite execution.

The position also owns how customers find Canadian Tire in a changing discovery landscape. As search shifts from traditional engines to answer engines, generative surfaces and agentic shopping assistants, this role leads the SEO, AEO and GEO agenda — from early experimentation to scaled, repeatable practice. The VP is a key stakeholder in the True North eCommerce Accelerate strategy, shaping business requirements that Digital Product teams can translate into new capabilities across the digital commerce ecosystem, including Digital Harmonization, 2P and Digital Experience Drivers.

What You'll Do

Digital Merchandising

Own the onsite merchandising experience across homepage, category pages, navigation and onsite search relevance.
Own digital assortment presentation and promo execution onsite, aligned to banner, category and enterprise promo plans.
Ensure marketing, merchandising and loyalty offers are activated consistently across the websites and the CTR app.
Surface the right products earlier in the shopping journey, converting discovery into considered intent to purchase.
Partner with Pricing & Promo and Brand & Marketing so onsite execution reflects the enterprise promotional calendar and price architecture.
Serve as the senior digital partner to Banner Presidents and category teams, translating their plans into a clear onsite execution plan with visible trade-offs where capacity is constrained.

Digital Analytics & Activation

Act as the key owner driving the agentic commerce ambition forward — defining how CTC's assortment, content and offers are surfaced to AI shopping assistants and agent-mediated journeys.
Lead the AEO and GEO agenda alongside SEO, treating traditional and AI-driven discovery as one connected practice.
Own onsite performance analytics, including KPI definition, competitive benchmarking and the digital measurement fact base used in commercial decisions.
Build the measurement approach for AI-driven discovery — visibility, citation, referral quality and downstream intent to purchase — and use it to steer investment.
Run the digital activation and experimentation practice, converting test wins into standing site practice rather than one-off lifts.
Own the digital performance management rhythm: KPI reporting, performance reviews and early escalation of risks to the outlook.
Partner with IT on the technical integrations required for search, LLM and agentic discoverability.

Digital Content Operations

Own onsite content health across copy, imagery and specification accuracy, at the quality standard the banners expect.
Own content grooming and meta tagging so customers can discover our products across search, generative and agentic surfaces.
Ensure product content answers the questions that drive purchase decisions, building customer confidence and intent at the point of discovery.
Run vendor product data onboarding, data quality and bilingual compliance, scaling throughput as assortment expands.
Set the structured data and content standards that allow customers — and the assistants acting for them — to discover our products and understand why to choose them.

Product Content Capabilities

Own the content platform agenda across Product 2.0 including PIM, PCM and DAM, defining the operational requirements that the roadmap must satisfy.
Drive product process automation and AI-assisted rules that scale onboarding without scaling headcount.
Lead a team of product managers and manage IT delivery of new capability and ongoing support.
Partner with Digital Product on roadmap sequencing so capability lands against real category and banner plans.

Online Assortment (2P)

Serve as the True North 2P initiative lead, accountable for the initiative's direction, milestones and reported outcomes.
Build the 2P assortment expansion agenda — onboarding, content readiness and onsite presentation at scale.
Connect 2P growth to the broader discoverability agenda so expanded assortment is surfaced to customers and AI-driven discovery alike.
Represent 2P progress, risks and trade-offs in True North governance and enterprise forums.

Team & Leadership

Lead a multi-disciplinary team spanning digital merchandising, analytics and activation, content operations and content management products.
Build capability and bench strength across the function, with clear accountability at the AVP level and a deliberate approach to vacancy and succession risk.
Set a performance culture grounded in evidence, speed and commercial ownership.

What You Bring

Senior leadership experience in eCommerce, digital commerce or omni-channel retail, with the ability to operate as a peer to senior commercial, banner and merchandising leaders.
A proven record of delivering commercial results through digital execution, onsite activation and measurable customer experience improvements in a large, multi-banner retail environment.
Depth across digital merchandising, onsite search, digital analytics and experimentation, product content operations, and AI-enabled discovery practices including SEO, AEO and GEO.
Experience leading enterprise initiatives end to end, including 2P, Digital Harmonization or similar scaled capability programs, with clear governance, milestone and reporting accountability.
Strength translating commercial strategy and banner priorities into clear business requirements that Digital Product and Technology teams can convert into new capabilities.
Strong people leadership, including building high-performing teams, developing leaders and setting a culture of evidence-based decision making, speed and commercial ownership.

jobs.title: Director of AI Content Systems, Marketing
jobs.description:
Please Note: This is a fully remote role for candidates with Eastern Timezone overlap.

The role

You won't write most of our content, you'll design, build, and run the AI-powered system (think content engineering) that turns product, customer, and expert knowledge into content that drives organic pipeline.

You're not a software engineer, but you think like one. You're as comfortable vibe coding and building agents as you are customizing WordPress, writing brand guidelines, or proofreading a white paper.

This is the first hire on a new team at Time Doctor. We run it like an engineering team whose product is content: a clear spec, a repeatable production system, quality gates, and measured output. The team stays small and gets its leverage from AI, automation, freelancers, agencies, and subject-matter experts.

Who we are

Time Doctor is a workforce analytics platform that gives distributed teams the visibility they need to improve trust and performance. We serve remote, hybrid and outsourced organisations worldwide, with particular strength in BPO, healthcare and tech services. We are bootstrapped, profitable and fully remote, with team members across 30+ countries. We built a durable business on customer revenue rather than venture capital, and we are now focused on growing it.

What you'll own

Content strategy.
Decide what we publish, for whom, and why, based on search demand, AI-search behavior, buyer questions, and revenue marketing priorities.
The content production system.
Design and run the AI workflows, agents, prompt libraries, briefs, and QA gates that produce content at scale. Treat it like a product: version it, measure it, and keep improving it.
Expert input pipeline.
Build repeatable ways to capture knowledge from product, customer success, sales, customers, and outside experts, and feed it into the system so our content says things competitors can't.
Verbal and visual brand.
Own voice, tone, and editorial standards, and encode them into the system so every asset meets them by default.
SEO and AI search (GEO).
Own strategy for organic search and visibility in AI answers (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and others).
The website.
Own site architecture, content structure, conversion paths, and the website roadmap.
Tooling and vendors.
Choose and manage the AI tools, automation platforms, and outside partners the team runs on, within a budget.

How you'll be measured

You own three outcomes: organic leads, organic traffic, and AI + SEO search visibility. Because organic results lag, your first two quarters are weighted toward leading indicators that show the system is working.

What you'll manage and who you'll work with

You'll build and manage: content development, technical SEO/GEO implementation, and visual design. You'll do the work yourself when speed matters, and bring in agencies, contractors, or freelancers you select and direct against our brand guidelines when scale matters.
Your inputs:
positioning, messaging, and personas come from the VP of Marketing. You turn them into content at scale; you don't own positioning.
Your team:
Freelancers and contractors as needed, with a path to hire as the system proves out.

Who you are

Must have
5+ years in B2B SaaS content, SEO, or growth marketing, including 1+ years leading a function or program.
You've built and run AI-powered content workflows in production. You can walk us through one end to end: inputs, tools, prompts, skills, QA gates, output volume, and results.
Hands-on with AI and automation tools (LLMs, agents, and automation platforms).
Comfortable tinkering with HTML and CSS. Can read Python and scripts. Comfortable with Claude code or eager to learn it.
A track record of growing organic traffic and leads through SEO, with a working understanding of how AI search surfaces and cites content.
Strong editorial judgment. You know when an AI draft is off-brand, generic, or wrong, and you design the system to catch it.
Experience directing freelancers, agencies, and subject-matter experts to a quality bar.
You think in systems and metrics: throughput, cycle time, cost per asset, and outcomes.

Nice to have
Experience owning a B2B website roadmap and conversion optimization.
Background in time tracking, workforce analytics, HR tech, or remote-work software.

This role is not a fit if you want to be the primary writer, or if your strength is CMS or content platform architecture rather than marketing outcomes.

How we'll evaluate:
a walkthrough of a content system you've built, and a short exercise designing a workflow for one of our content types. We won't ask for writing samples.

Why this role

You are the first hire on a new team, and you get to design the content system from the ground up.
You own real outcomes: organic leads, traffic, and AI search visibility, with the authority to choose the tools and partners you run on.
You work AI-first from day one, at a company that expects it and funds the tools.
We are profitable and bootstrapped. Your budget comes from customers, not from a burn rate.
Professional development resources and a learning budget.
Fully remote and flexible, working with talented people in 30+ countries.

Our hiring approach

This is a full-time, 100% remote role. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we value diversity and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status or disability.

We hire globally, but this particular role is open only to candidates based in the United States or Canada, with at least four hours of daily overlap with US Eastern hours. Our Talent Attraction team will walk you through the details during your first conversation.

Vice President – Governance & Reporting, Internal Audit

About Us

The Maples Group is a global leader in financial services, trusted by many of the world’s largest hedge fund managers, private equity firms, and international corporations.
Our side-by-side financial and legal teams consistently deliver award-winning services to a global client base, offering unrivalled learning and career opportunities to our 2,500 colleagues worldwide. With 18 locations across the Americas, Asia, Europe and the Middle East, our international presence offers a unique springboard for career development and cross- cultural immersion.

What’s it like to work here?

We are driven to excel, and collaboration is key to our continued success. We can go further for our clients because we go further for each other too. We are committed to diversity, inclusion and equal of opportunity as we attract, retain and develop world-class talent. Our inclusive culture creates an environment where people can be themselves at work while doing their best work. No matter where you work in the Maples Group, you will be part of a global team.

The Opportunity

The Maples Group is seeking a Vice President – Governance & Reporting to join our Internal Audit team in Montreal. This is newly created leadership role is responsible for designing, executing and continuously enhancing the governance, reporting and quality-assurance framework for our global Internal Audit function. Acting as a key architect of our third line of defence, the successful candidate will ensure that Internal Audit delivers clear, timely and data-driven insight to the Audit Committees and key stakeholders, while aligning with the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) global Internal Audit Standards.

Consistently recognised as one of Montreal’s Top Employers, the Maples Group established our operations in the central downtown area in 2009. Our Montreal office exemplifies our culturally rich and entrepreneurial organisation, with over 300 colleagues from 50 countries collaborating to deliver best-in-class solutions to clients worldwide.

Reporting directly to the Senior Vice-President, you will:

Own the end-to-end Internal Audit governance calendar, including timely preparation and delivery of reporting packs for audit meetings
Produce concise, visually engaging dashboards on audit plan delivery, thematic issues, outstanding audit findings, emerging risks and quality metrics for senior stakeholders and the Audit Committees
Design, implement and maintain a comprehensive Quality Assurance and Improvement Programme (QAIP) in line with the IIA Standards and local regulatory requirements
Govern the creation, periodic review and formal approval of audit methodology (IA Charter, Internal Audit Procedures Manual, templates and guidance notes) ensuring timely updates for regulatory and professional-standards changes
Operate the escalation framework for delays, scope changes and impediments, ensuring early and transparent communication
Track and report on audit findings, actions and remediation progress
Manage the automation agenda for Internal Audit, including digitisation of audit processes and report templates, exploration of automation technologies, and enhancement of risk-rating methodologies through data analytics and predictive indicators
Serve as Internal Audit’s primary liaison on governance and quality matters with senior management, risk and compliance heads, and external auditors; present complex technical concepts in a clear, business-oriented manner tailored to diverse audiences

Whilst governance and reporting are the primary functions of this role, the candidate may be requested to assist with or conduct audit engagements.

What You Bring

In addition to indisputably high ethical standards and autonomy, the ideal candidate possesses the following:
A minimum of 5 years’ experience in internal audit within financial services or a similarly regulated environment
Proven expertise in designing and operating an Internal Audit quality-assurance framework; prior responsibility for a QAIP or equivalent is strongly preferred
Strong knowledge of the IIA Standards and associated guidance
Demonstrated success in governance reporting to boards of directors, Audit Committees and regulators, with superior written and verbal communication skills

Key skills and qualifications for this role are as follows:

Attention to detail, professionalism and a team first mentality
Experience with data-analytics and automation tools; ability to translate technology opportunities into practical efficiency gains
Strong understanding of risk and control assessment techniques, risk taxonomies and audit-universe construction
Highly organised self-starter, capable of working independently, managing multiple priorities and influencing without direct authority
Excellent time management, organisational, prioritisation and communication skills (fluent written and oral English)

Benefits & Rewards

The most enduring professional relationships are reciprocal relationships. The Maples Group prioritises employee health and wellbeing. We offer a range of benefits, including:

Comprehensive health coverage (medical, dental and optical)
Competitive vacation packages
Educational assistance and professional development programs
Savings or pension plan
Life insurance
Travel insurance
Global mental wellness program
Social events

Disclaimer:
All personal information collected during the application process will be used for recruitment-related purposes only. Please refer to our Job Applicant Privacy Notice at maples.com/privacy for details on how we handle personal information relating to job applicants.

“Please note that it is the Maples Group standard policy to undertake various background screening checks on all applicants to whom a conditional job offer is made. Except for roles based in the Republic of Ireland, the background checks will include criminal records checks when a conditional job offer is made. If you have a criminal record, it does not mean that your job offer will be automatically withdrawn. The Maples Group will make all job offer decisions on a case-by-case basis and will take a number of factors into account, such as the role that you are applying for and the nature and circumstances of the past offence. You will have the opportunity to discuss the matter with us before a decision is made. Further details will be provided at the time any conditional job offer is made.”

Poste :
Vice-président – Gouvernance et production de rapports, Audit interne
Emplacement :
Montréal

À propos de nous

Le Groupe Maples est un leader mondial des services financiers auquel font confiance de nombreux gestionnaires de fonds de couverture, sociétés de capital-investissement et entreprises internationales parmi les plus importants au monde.
Nos équipes financières et juridiques, qui travaillent côte à côte, fournissent constamment des services primés à une clientèle mondiale, offrant ainsi des possibilités d’apprentissage et de carrière inégalées à nos 2 500 collègues dans le monde. Répartie dans 18 régions en Amérique, en Asie, en Europe et au Moyen-Orient, notre présence internationale offre un tremplin unique pour le perfectionnement professionnel et l’immersion interculturelle.

L’occasion

Nous recherchons un Analyste des données et des rapports

jobs.title: Vice President, Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
Our VP, FP&A is a strategic partner and a critical enterprise leader who shapes how the business plans, allocates capital, measures performance, and makes decisions. This role combines deep financial expertise with strong executive presence, business acumen, and the ability to influence across a complex, franchise system.

As we shift toward a Product Operating Model, this leader will modernize FP&A into a proactive, insight-driven, technology-enabled function. They will help guide the business through this evolution, bringing structure, clarity, challenge, and strategic framing to elevate financial maturity across the organization.

The VP, FP&A must be both a relationship-builder and a systems thinker — equally comfortable diving into models, simplifying complexity, coaching a tactical FP&A team, and advising senior leaders with confidence and credibility.

A DAY IN THE LIFE

CFO Partnership & Executive Influence

Serve as trusted advisor to the CFO, providing structure, insight, guidance, and challenge on key decisions.
Strengthen the CFO’s influence by preparing high-quality narratives, decision frameworks, and financial storytelling for the Executive.
Bring clarity to ambiguity — shaping options, risks, and trade-offs in a way that enables confident decision-making.
Uplift FP&A capability and bring discipline to planning, forecasting, scenario thinking, and enterprise prioritization.

Modernize FP&A for a Product Operating Model

Translate traditional FP&A into a future-state model aligned with product planning, value streams, capacity-based resourcing, and multi-quarter bets.
Align financial rhythms with product cycles, investment governance, and product portfolio management.
Build FP&A frameworks that support experimentation, iterative planning, and benefit realization.

Enterprise Planning & Forecasting Leadership

Lead the company’s planning cycles: annual plan, rolling forecast, and long-term model.
Ensure assumptions, targets, and resource allocations align with strategy and enterprise priorities.
Elevate forecasting accuracy and enforce strong financial discipline across functions and brands.

Performance Management & Decision Support

Build standardized KPIs, dashboards, and reporting that unify financial and operational performance.
Run monthly and quarterly business reviews with a focus on insight, action, and accountability.
Provide functional and brand leaders with high-quality decision support, scenario analysis, and commercial insight.
Connect franchisor, brand, and franchise partner economics into a clear view of system-wide value creation.

Investment Governance & Capital Allocation

Operate the investment governance framework: ROI, payback, prioritization, and benefit realization.
Support the CFO in modeling and communicating enterprise value, including key drivers and risk factors.
Ensure investment decisions are aligned with strategic priorities and supported by clear financial logic.

FP&A Technology, Systems & Data Modernization

Modernize FP&A processes through improved systems, automation, and real-time insight (Cube, NetSuite, Tableau).
Strengthen data flows to eliminate manual overhead and improve the accuracy and speed of business insights.
Ensure the Finance team remains effective during the transition by supporting Excel- and Sheets-based processes while building toward a more automated future state.

Leadership, Culture & Team Development

Lead, coach, and elevate a high-performing FP&A team
Build a culture of clarity, curiosity, accountability, and cross-functional partnership.
Increase the commercial, analytical, and business-partnering capability of FP&A professionals.
Model behaviors aligned with the Product Operating Model: transparency, collaboration, system thinking, and customer obsession.

What You Bring To The Table

Proven experience leading FP&A in complex, multi-stakeholder, or high-growth environments, with accountability for forecasting, planning, analysis, and decision support.
Demonstrated success as a strategic partner to a CFO or senior executive, providing backbone support, structured thinking, and trusted challenge.
Strong understanding of how FP&A evolves in a Product Operating Model (value streams, portfolio planning, capacity modeling, investment governance, benefit realization).
Executive presence and relationship strength — able to build trust quickly, influence without friction, and communicate with clarity.
Technical and process depth, including financial modeling, scenario planning, and the ability to build, audit, and simplify models in Excel/Sheets.

jobs.title: Head of Marketing Strategy & Insights
jobs.description:
Summary

Generosity X is hiring a  Head of Marketing Strategy & Insights
 to lead marketing strategy for our charity clients, helping them grow donor acquisition, strengthen retention and improve the donor experience. This role focuses on our clients’ fundraising programs rather than Generosity X’s own marketing.
This is a role for someone who can zoom all the way out to see the strategy and all the way in to understand what is actually happening in the data, the campaign or the donor experience. You'll own reporting and analytics across the client portfolio, lead Generosity Experience Roadmaps (GXR), become a trusted strategic resource for the team and clients and help build the next evolution of Generosity X's strategy function.
If you're a strong technical marketer who loves the craft, asks why the numbers moved rather than simply reporting that they did and wants the opportunity to build something, this may be your next step.

At a glance

Organization:
 Generosity X
Location:
 Remote; anywhere in Canada
Reports to:
 Matthew Hussey, Founder
Compensation:
 $105,000 to $130,000 CAD, depending on experience
Application deadline:
 Open until a qualified candidate is hired
Position status:
 New

About Generosity X

Generosity X is a fundraising growth partner built on one belief: generosity is designed, not demanded. We partner with charities to grow annual giving through a combination of data, experimentation, strategy and thoughtful donor experience. We want to understand not only  what  caused someone to give, but  why  it worked and how we can build on that insight to make generosity happen again. Our work brings together two things that are too often treated as opposites: the rigour of data and experimentation and the art of understanding real human behaviour. We work with charities that want to grow, which makes donor acquisition the cornerstone of all that we do.
Learn more:
 https://generosityx.com

The Opportunity

Generosity X has grown to the point where we need another senior strategic mind who can bring technical depth and keep raising the bar.
This isn't a role where you'll sit above the details.
One day you may be looking across an entire donor program, spotting patterns and advising a client on where their strategy needs to go. The next, you may be deep in retention cohorts, reviewing an A/B test or improving how we use AI to generate reporting.
You need to be comfortable doing both.
You'll lead our Donor Experience function, own reporting and analytics across our client portfolio and be a senior strategic resource for our Client Experience Managers and clients.
You'll also be building something. There's no established strategy team waiting for you. At first, you'll be hands-on in the work while shaping the function, improving our systems and eventually building the team.
For the right person, that's part of the opportunity.

Key Responsibilities

Own the Generosity Experience Roadmap (GXR)
Own the data analysis, financial forecasting and senior strategic lens for each GXR, working closely with the project lead and Client Experience Manager
Look across the full donor experience while still being willing to get into the details
Continuously improve the GXR and turn what we learn into a stronger, repeatable product for every client

Own reporting and analytics across the client portfolio
Set the cadence, standard and substance of what a Generosity X report says about a client's year, quarter or campaign
Personally work with the data rather than simply overseeing the process
Own key measures across acquisition and retention, including cost per lead, lead-to-donor conversion, cost to acquire a donor by channel, retention by cohort, second-gift and monthly conversion, reactivation, revenue per thousand, mid-level giving and lifetime value by channel.
Build forecasting and projections
Prepare and present standard donor and retention reports to clients every two months, with additional quarterly, annual or board-level reporting as required for certain clients.

Be a strategic resource for the team
Serve as a senior subject matter expert that Client Experience Managers can turn to when they're thinking through strategy, testing an idea or trying to solve a client problem
Help the team move between the big strategic question and the tactical details required to execute it
Teach and share your thinking so that the team's strategic capability continues to grow

Build and run the A/B testing roadmap
Develop testing plans that move each client's marketing and fundraising forward
Look beyond which version won and ask  why  it won
Turn individual tests into broader learning that can strengthen work across the entire client portfolio

Understand the human behind the data
Bring genuine curiosity about donor psychology and human behaviour to the work
Look beyond dashboards and results to understand what may have caused someone to respond, give again, disengage or change their behaviour
Use those insights to form hypotheses, design better tests and improve the donor experience

Own and evolve the HEARTS framework™
Deepen the IP itself and build fluency across the team and our clients
Help HEARTS become the shared language for how generosity experiences are interpreted and evaluated at Generosity X

Present and lead in the room
Bring analysis into regular client reviews every two months, alongside additional quarterly reviews, annual strategy sessions, in-person strategy days, management presentations and board-level sessions as required.
Translate complex analysis into a clear story and a practical path forward
Be comfortable offering a point of view, explaining the evidence behind it and holding your position when appropriately challenged

Use AI to make the work better
Step comfortably into AI-enabled reporting and strategy workflows already being used at Generosity X
Look for opportunities to improve those systems rather than simply following them

Build what's next
Help standardize offerings such as website audits and strategic roadmaps
Build new initiatives alongside the Founder
Identify opportunities, solve problems and move ideas forward without waiting for a fully built playbook
Help shape the strategy function as Generosity X grows

Eventually, build the team
This is a new role and an emerging function. You won't walk into a large team on day one.
You'll begin by being close to the work yourself. As the function grows, you'll have the opportunity to help define the roles around you, coach the craft and build a team capable of carrying the work forward.

What We’re Looking For

You should bring:
8+ years of relevant experience in fundraising, direct response or marketing strategy  or
 5+ years of strong agency-side experience
At least 2 years of experience presenting to executives, boards or other senior stakeholders
Strong technical marketing instincts and the ability to move comfortably between strategy and execution
Confidence personally working with data and analysis rather than simply managing others who do it
A solid grasp of acquisition economics: you know what a new donor costs, what they’re worth over time and when a channel pays back
Experience with experimentation, testing and using results to shape future strategy
Genuine curiosity about donor psychology and human behaviour. You want to understand  why  something worked, not just that it worked
Experience using AI as part of real workflows, processes, analysis, automation or problem-solving, beyond basic chatbot use
The ability to communicate complex analysis clearly and credibly to clients
Comfort working independently in a fast-moving, remote and highly asynchronous environment
Strong alignment with Generosity X's values

Previous people-management experience is welcome but not required.
 We're more interested in whether you have the capability and desire to grow into leadership as this function grows.

You May Thrive Here If…

You can spend the morning on a three-year donor strategy and the afternoon working out why one campaign behaved unexpectedly.
When something works, you want to know why. New ideas and technology energize you.
You're comfortable moving things forward before every process is built.
At Generosity X, you'll have real autonomy. When the Founder asks, "How could we make this better?", you see it as collaboration, not criticism.
Most of all, you're ready to build this function from the ground up.

Overview of Benefits

Three weeks of paid vacation
Additional time off from December 25–31
Health Spending Account and Wellness Spending Account
Paid Fridays off from May 1 through the August long weekend, without moving to a compressed workweek
Quarterly in-person retreats to connect, grow, learn and collaborate
A culture where you're trusted to lead, not just execute

Working Conditions

Generosity X has core collaboration hours of 9am-3pm, Mountain Time, and your working schedule will need to provide consistent availability during that window.
Travel of up to 20% should be expected.
While candidates across Canada will be considered equally, being located in Calgary may provide occasional opportunities to work alongside Matt in person.

How to Apply

Please upload your resume, and send your cover letter to operations@vocareunion.com.
We'd particularly love to understand  why this role interests you and what you've built, tested or improved that you're proud of.

At Generosity X, we are dedicated to fostering a workplace culture that embraces diversity, equity, and inclusion. As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome and encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds and abilities. Accommodations are available upon request throughout the recruitment process.

Artificial intelligence Statement: Vocare Union takes a personal, relationship-focused approach to recruitment. AI may support our work, while our recruiters make candidate assessments and recommendations. Generosity X may use AI to screen or assess applicants during its hiring process.
Vocare Union is the search team supporting Generosity X through this recruitment process.

jobs.description:
About BoomerangFX?

BoomerangFX is a rapidly growing global healthcare technology company transforming how private-pay healthcare practices operate, acquire patients and accelerate growth. Our AI-powered SaaS platform brings together practice management, electronic medical records, patient engagement, marketing automation, revenue growth solutions and autonomous AI capabilities into one integrated ecosystem. Operating across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other international markets, BoomerangFX serves healthcare practices across medical aesthetics, cosmetic surgery, dermatology, wellness and other high-growth specialty healthcare segments. We are building the next generation of AI-powered healthcare infrastructure, with an ambition to become the global operating system for private-pay healthcare. As we enter our next phase of growth, we are seeking an exceptional, hands-on financial and operational executive to lead our global finance, administration and business transformation functions.

Vice President, Finance & Administration

BoomerangFX | Global Healthcare AI & SaaS

We are seeking a highly accomplished, commercially minded Vice President, Finance & Administration with proven experience in private-equity-backed SaaS companies that have scaled from approximately $5 million to $50 million in Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR).

This is a senior executive leadership role combining strategic financial management, hands-on operational execution, corporate administration and cross-functional business transformation.

Reporting directly to the CEO, the successful candidate will be responsible for strengthening financial discipline, improving operating performance, building scalable administrative infrastructure and leading initiatives that support profitable international growth.

We are not seeking a traditional accounting executive focused primarily on financial reporting and compliance. We are looking for a business-oriented finance leader who has operated in demanding, high-growth, private-equity-backed environments, understands SaaS unit economics, has managed multidisciplinary teams and can personally drive organizational improvements.

The ideal candidate has played a meaningful leadership role in scaling a SaaS business, professionalizing its financial and administrative functions, improving EBITDA and cash flow, and implementing the systems and processes required to support the next stage of growth.

Key Responsibilities

1. Financial Leadership, Planning & Performance

Lead the company’s global finance function, including accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, treasury, financial controls and financial planning and analysis.
Develop and maintain integrated financial models, annual operating plans, rolling forecasts and cash flow projections.
Establish financial accountability across business functions, departments and international operations.
Drive operating margin improvement, EBITDA performance, cash management and working capital optimization.
Analyze financial performance, identify variances and implement corrective actions.
Partner with executive leadership to evaluate resource allocation, operating investments, headcount and business performance.
Strengthen financial reporting and management information to support timely, data-driven executive decisions.
Oversee external accounting, audit, tax and professional advisory relationships.

2. SaaS Financial Metrics & Unit Economics

Establish rigorous reporting and analysis of key SaaS performance indicators, including ARR, MRR, NRR, GRR, churn, ARPU, CAC, LTV and CAC payback.
Develop revenue and profitability reporting by product, customer segment, geography and business unit.
Improve subscription revenue forecasting, billing accuracy, collections and revenue recognition processes.
Partner with Sales, Customer Success and Operations to improve customer economics and operating leverage.
Build scalable financial systems capable of supporting growth from early-stage SaaS operations to $50 million or more in ARR.
Provide actionable financial insights to improve pricing, margins, productivity and capital allocation.

3. Corporate Administration & Global Business Operations

Oversee the company’s corporate administrative functions, ensuring efficient and consistent execution across international operations.
Lead administrative teams responsible for corporate services, office administration, procurement, vendor management, facilities and operational support.
Establish clear responsibilities, performance standards, service levels and accountability across administrative functions.
Improve administrative productivity, cost efficiency and organizational responsiveness.
Oversee corporate policies, internal controls, contract administration and governance processes in coordination with legal and other functional leaders.
Standardize administrative workflows, reporting and operating procedures across geographies.
Ensure corporate infrastructure scales efficiently without unnecessary increases in overhead.

4. Organizational Leadership, Training & Development

Lead, coach and develop finance, accounting, administration and corporate services teams.
Assess organizational capabilities, identify skill gaps and implement structured training and professional development programs.
Build a culture of financial accountability, operational excellence, continuous improvement and ownership.
Establish clear departmental KPIs, performance scorecards and management reporting.
Improve the quality, productivity and independence of managers and functional team members.
Recruit and develop strong financial and administrative leaders capable of supporting global growth.
Implement succession planning, cross-training and standardized operating procedures to reduce organizational dependency on individual employees.
Drive the adoption of best practices in financial management, corporate administration and business operations.

5. Business Transformation & Strategic Projects

Lead cross-functional transformation projects designed to improve operating efficiency, profitability, organizational effectiveness and scalability.
Identify opportunities to simplify processes, eliminate duplication, reduce operating costs and improve service delivery.
Implement financial systems, reporting tools, workflow automation and AI-enabled business processes.
Lead process redesign and operational improvement initiatives across finance, administration and corporate functions.

jobs.description:
About Patra

Patra is an outcome-focused operating partner working exclusively for the insurance industry. Combining expert global teams, process intelligence, and purpose-built technology, Patra delivers measurable results to clients. With 20 years of deep domain expertise, exceptional client retention rates, and significant sustained investment in AI, Patra partners with agencies, brokers, MGAs, MGUs, and carriers to transform how insurance operations are delivered.

Core Duties

AI and data are becoming foundational capabilities across Patra’s technology organization. The AI & Data Architecture function establishes the enterprise architecture, platforms, governance, and shared capabilities that enable product teams to build intelligent applications safely and at scale.

As AI Architect, you will lead Patra’s AI & Data Architecture function, operating at a Sr. Director-level scope with responsibility for its strategy, team formation and management, systems architecture, strategic priorities, and, most importantly, reliable and impactful execution.

The function has particular responsibility for document-intensive and unstructured-data environments, including retrieval-augmented generation, semantic and vector search, AI agents, evaluation datasets, enterprise analytics, and granular AI observability.

You will report to the Chief Digital Officer (CDO) and partner with senior leaders across Engineering, Product, Security, Compliance, Business Intelligence, Operations, and other business functions.

What you'll do

Lead the AI & Data Architecture function. Own the strategy, organizational structure, technical direction, priorities, delivery, quality, and operating model for Patra’s enterprise AI and data capabilities.
Form and lead the organization. Determine staffing requirements and build multidisciplinary teams spanning AI engineering, data engineering, machine learning, enterprise data architecture, analytics infrastructure, and shared AI services, while personally delivering on urgent business priorities at the same time
Manage talent and performance. Establish objectives for direct reports as your team grows, evaluate performance, provide career and leadership development, and exercise delegated authority to make or recommend decisions concerning hiring, promotions, compensation, organizational assignments, and other personnel actions.
Own the enterprise AI and data architecture. Establish Patra’s target-state architecture for how data is ingested, governed, modeled, stored, streamed, retrieved, analyzed, and consumed by enterprise applications, analytics platforms, and AI systems.
Direct architecture for document-intensive and unstructured domains. Establish enterprise standards and approve architectural approaches for document ingestion,

metadata extraction, indexing, semantic retrieval, vector search, knowledge enrichment, and AI consumption. Detailed design and implementation are delegated to subordinate professional teams.

Industrialize the Agentic AI platform. Direct the evolution of agentic capabilities into production-grade enterprise infrastructure supporting agent orchestration, tool integration, retrieval-augmented generation, model interaction, security boundaries, evaluation, observability, and appropriate human oversight.
Own AI evaluation and data strategy. Establish the standards and organizational processes governing training, fine-tuning, benchmarking, and evaluation datasets, including quality, provenance, versioning, access, retention, and appropriate use.
Treat AI observability as a strategic data asset. Establish the architecture and governance for capturing and using event streams across agent activity, model interactions, retrieval operations, tool execution, quality signals, latency, cost, failures, and human interventions.
Lead the enterprise data platform strategy. Set direction for cloud-native data capabilities including AWS services such as S3, Redshift, streaming and event technologies, together with platforms such as Snowflake and/or Databricks where appropriate.
Establish enterprise data standards. Define and govern modern approaches to operational, analytical, event-driven, semantic, and AI-oriented data modeling and ensure common architectural standards are adopted across engineering teams.
Make Business Intelligence a first-class platform stakeholder. Ensure enterprise data capabilities support analytics, operational reporting, experimentation, decision support, and executive intelligence without relying on fragmented downstream data extraction.
Build governance into the architecture. Establish standards for data ownership, lineage, provenance, classification, quality, lifecycle management, access control, AI usage, auditability, and enterprise data governance.
Protect customer and tenant data. Establish architecture and controls for strict multi-tenant client-data segregation across storage, processing, analytics, retrieval, model interaction, evaluation, and observability systems.
Own jurisdiction-aware data architecture. Establish retention, archival, residency, and deletion strategies supporting differing contractual, regulatory, and jurisdictional requirements.
Set quality and reliability expectations. Establish SLAs, SLOs, quality metrics, and operational standards for critical data assets, pipelines, AI services, retrieval systems, and shared platform capabilities.
Establish reusable platform capabilities. Direct the development of common capabilities for identity, access, observability, model access, AI evaluation, security, compliance controls, tenancy, CI/CD, and data services that can be consumed across product organizations.
Direct enterprise integration architecture. Establish standards for integrating AI and data platforms with Patra products, internal business systems, partner platforms, APIs, event streams, and external data providers.
Run AI and data capabilities as enterprise products. Treat product engineers, analytics teams, business stakeholders, and other internal organizations as customers of the platform. Establish adoption, reliability, quality, and developer-productivity measures for shared capabilities.
Own architecture governance. Lead reviews of material AI, data, and platform architecture decisions; establish reference architectures and engineering standards; approve significant architectural approaches; and resolve cross-organizational technical decisions.
Direct the AI and data portfolio. Establish priorities across concurrent AI, data, and platform programs and allocate engineering and data-science resources according to business value, organizational capacity, technical dependencies, and enterprise risk.
Manage technology investment. Participate in annual planning, determine staffing and platform requirements, develop budget recommendations, evaluate strategic technology vendors, and make or recommend investment decisions involving AI, cloud, data, and infrastructure platforms.
Shape the multi-year technology roadmap. Partner with executive engineering and product leadership to define Patra’s AI and data roadmap and translate strategic objectives into sequenced, staffed, and measurable organizational programs.
Represent the function with senior leadership. Advise executives on AI strategy, enterprise data architecture, platform investments, organizational capacity, delivery risk, AI risk, governance, and major technology trade-offs.

How You Think About AI And Data Platforms

We are looking for a leader whose operating instincts align with how we build.

Build shared capabilities once. Identity, observability, model access, evaluation, security, governance, tenancy, CI/CD, and data access should be established as reusable platform capabilities rather than repeatedly implemented by individual teams.
Data is a product. Enterprise data, documents, application events, model interactions, evaluation results, and observability signals are strategic assets with defined owners, contracts, quality expectations, governance, and consumers.
AI-ready from ingestion onward. Documents, metadata, events, permissions, lineage, and semantic context should be designed so that they can safely support applications, analytics, machine learning, retrieval, and agentic systems.
Governance is architecture. Customer isolation, security, retention, residency, auditability, Responsible AI, and regulatory considerations are architectural requirements rather than controls added after systems have been built.
Evaluation precedes confidence. Production AI requires measurable success criteria, curated evaluation datasets, regression testing, observability, and mechanisms for detecting degraded behavior.
Observability is a first-class data asset. Agent activity, retrievals, model calls, tool calls, cost, latency, failures, quality signals, user feedback, and human interventions should produce structured and governed telemetry.
Automation over operational heroics. Repeated manual intervention represents an architectural or platform gap. Provisioning, deployment, evaluation, governance checks, and operational processes should increasingly be automated.
Self-service over central bottlenecks. The AI & Data Architecture organization exists to increase the leverage of engineering and product teams, not to become a ticket queue they must pass through.
Human oversight is intentional. Increasing autonomy should be accompanied by explicit decision boundaries, escalation mechanisms, auditability, and controls appropriate to the risk of the workflow.
Incremental over big-bang. Major platform transitions should produce measurable production value incrementally, with explicit migration plans and accountable milestones.
Specifications precede implementation. As AI accelerates implementation, clear requirements, contracts, architectural boundaries, evaluation criteria, and ownership become more important.
Decisions are explicit. Make trade-offs visible across cost, risk, reliability, security, scalability, and time-to-value. Once a decision is made, establish ownership and execute against it.

Organizational leadership. Demonstrated experience forming, scaling, and leading multidisciplinary engineering and data organizations.

Enterprise AI credibility. Deep understanding of production AI systems including LLM applications, RAG, embeddings, semantic and vector search, agentic architectures, AI orchestration, evaluation, observability, governance, and human-in-the-loop systems.
Enterprise data architecture. Significant experience directing the architecture of platforms supporting structured, semi-structured, and unstructured enterprise data.
Document-intensive domains. Experience with architectures where documents and unstructured information are important business assets supporting operational workflows, search, analytics, AI, and governance.
