Own Human-Centered Design as a funded, staffed, and measured workstream from mobilization — not a go-live activity.
Start from user jobs-to-be-done for Finance, rather than screens; ensure personas and journey maps for finance, operations, and service users drive requirements before build.
Prototype and test with real users ahead of build, and use “art-of-the-possible” demonstrations of modern and AI-enabled capability to build executive and user confidence early.
Ensure HCD findings materially shape scope — including where an AI or automation use case is not yet appropriate for the client’s data maturity or risk tolerance.

Organizational Change Management and Adoption

Own OCM as a funded, measured workstream: leader alignment and visible sponsorship from day one, stakeholder analysis, communications, resistance management, role-based training, and readiness scoring.
Baseline adoption targets and tie them explicitly to benefits realization — system usage, process compliance, automation acceptance rates, exception volumes, and reporting adoption.
Lead the business through the behavioral shift that modernization demands: fewer manual reconciliations, more trust in a single data source, and confident supervision of automated and agent-assisted work.

Backlog, Value Mapping and Delivery Cadence

Lead weekly backlog refinement and own product backlog integrity and value mapping — from business drivers through requirements, capabilities, features, adoption outcomes, and measurable benefits.
Participate in each sprint’s feature review and system demonstration alongside the client Product Owner and the Platform & Delivery Lead, assessing whether what was built changes how the business actually works.
Participate in increment planning and Inspect & Adapt retrospectives, testing outcomes against the client’s original drivers.
Ensure outcome milestones are tracked alongside technical and delivery milestones.

Transformation Leadership and Client Confidence

Serve as the bridge between technical delivery and executive confidence, presenting evidence of business change to sponsors, steering committees, and the Executive Risk Committee.
Escalate early, with a recommended action rather than a status — particularly on scope that risks delivering a platform without an operating-model change.
Plan for complexity: competing stakeholder demands, third-party and systems-integrator friction, legacy-process attachment, and key-person risk on both sides.
Bring in-person presence to large or sensitive transformations.

Practice and People Leadership

Contribute to the growth of RSM’s Total Consulting transformation capability, including methods, tools, and reusable intellectual property for operating-model design, HCD, and adoption measurement.
Mentor, coach, and develop managers and senior associates across HCD, process design, and change workstreams
Support pursuits, proposals, and thought leadership that position RSM as a leader in integrated, outcome-led modernization; help shape scope, approach, and change-workstream sizing before mobilization.
Support account expansion through demonstrated value, and maintain strong attention to engagement economics within your workstreams.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree.
10+ years of consulting or advisory experience, including significant experience leading business-side transformation on large enterprise technology programs.
Demonstrated ownership of the Finance future-state operating model and end-to-end process design on ERP, cloud, data, or AI-enabled programs.
Demonstrated ownership of change and adoption as a funded workstream, including baselined adoption targets tied to benefits.
Experience operating in a fixed Agile or scaled-Agile cadence, including product backlog ownership, backlog refinement, and sprint demonstrations with an active client Product Owner.
Strong executive presence and the ability to hold candid, evidence-based conversations with C-suite sponsors.
Practical understanding of modern ERP, cloud, data, and AI platform capability — sufficient to shape requirements and challenge design, without acting as the technical architect.
Commitment to responsible AI use with a human in the loop and human accountability for all client-facing judgments and outputs.
Willingness and ability to travel as needed, generally up to 50%, with in-person presence on large programs.

Preferred Qualifications

CPA and / or Masters in Business Administration, with a focus on Accounting, Finance or Operations
Experience on transformations where an implementation was deliberately converted into a program as scope expanded across process, organization, and adoption.
Experience designing operating models for finance, supply chain, or shared-services functions in a modernized core environment.
Experience establishing AI and automation governance from a business-process and control perspective.
Change certification such as Prosci/ADKAR; design-thinking or service-design credentials; SAFe Agilist, PMI-ACP, or Scrum Master certification

The role spans AI strategy and governance, enterprise adoption and value realization, organizational capability, and the external AI ecosystem. Translate priorities into funded plans and measurable outcomes, strengthen executive decision-making, and enable the AI leadership team to operate effectively across a global organization.

Strategic Planning & Executive Advisory

Develop decision briefs with clear recommendations, alternatives, financial implications, and risks. Provide candid advice and test the assumptions behind major proposals

Lead strategic initiatives and special projects from problem definition through delivery, establishing ownership and transitioning ongoing responsibilities to the appropriate teams

Drive portfolio visibility across priorities, dependencies, investment, and results. Work with Finance and business owners to validate value assumptions and distinguish realized benefits from forecasts
Coordinate budget and workforce planning with Finance and HR. Surface resource trade-offs and recommend where to accelerate, adjust, or stop investment
Resolve execution barriers with accountable leaders and escalate material risks early, with options and a recommended course of action
Represent the CAIO as delegated, exercising judgment within agreed decision rights and keeping the CAIO informed of consequential commitments

Cross-Functional Alignment & Stakeholder Engagement

Build trusted partnerships with executive leaders, Chiefs of Staff, and business owners to secure sponsorship and drive enterprise AI adoption and value realization
Resolve cross-functional dependencies and competing priorities. Make ownership explicit and address difficult issues directly and constructively
Lead preparation of Board and executive materials, decision memos, and organizational communications, translating technical detail into clear business implications and specific asks
Prepare the CAIO for customer, partner, and industry engagements. Define the purpose of each engagement and drive follow-through, aligning external messaging with Communications and Marketing

Organizational Effectiveness & Transformation

Partner with the AI leadership team and HR on operating model evolution, workforce priorities, and leadership development. Identify capability gaps and clarify responsibilities as the organization scales
Coordinate with AI governance, Security, Legal, and other control functions to bring responsible AI requirements and unresolved risk decisions into portfolio planning and executive reviews
Advance AI fluency and change initiatives with business leaders, using adoption and outcome evidence to identify what needs to change
Improve how the organization works through simple processes and practical use of AI, reducing manual reporting and unnecessary meetings. Model a culture of High Standard, Low Bureaucracy, Zero Blame

Qualifications

Knowledge & Experience

10+ years of experience in strategy, business operations, consulting, Chief of Staff, product, data, AI, or related leadership roles, with demonstrated ownership of execution and business results
Strong understanding of enterprise AI and technology operating models, including generative AI, agents, shared platforms, adoption barriers, and AI economics and risk. Able to engage credibly with technical and business leaders
Proven experience delivering complex initiatives across a large, global, matrixed organization, including resolving competing priorities and recovering work that is off track
Strong financial and analytical acumen, with experience in business cases, investment prioritization, budget planning, and benefits measurement
Experience personally developing executive communications, Board materials, and strategic plans that require limited revision and support consequential decisions
Experience partnering with C-suite executives through ambiguity and organizational change. Prior Chief of Staff experience is valuable; equivalent operating leadership experience is equally relevant

Executive communication: Synthesize complex issues into concise, accurate writing and clear discussion
Trust and discretion: Handle sensitive matters with integrity and the confidence to challenge respectfully

Learning agility: Develop technical and business context quickly, use AI tools effectively, and verify their outputs
Calm leadership: Remain effective under pressure, recognize when to act independently and when to escalate, and put team outcomes first

Job Description

WHAT IS THE OPPORTUNITY?

Director, ALM Analytics & Applied Research is responsible for research, simulation, and forecasting of RBC’s Canadian banking balance sheet and income statement for the purpose of measuring stress exposure, in support of the Bank's Asset Liability Management, IRRBB metrics, and stress testing. The role focuses on econometric modeling of client behaviour assumptions for retail banking products, with strong emphasis on statistics, fixed income valuation modeling, and database management. Responsibilities include applied research relating to behavioural options in retail banking, risk and simulation model development, design input and output criteria, model performance evaluation, model and assumption documentation, process design, and econometric research related to dynamic forecasting assumptions.

WHAT WILL YOU DO?

Simulate and forecast Canadian Banking balance sheet and income statement under stress scenarios for purposes of IRRBB risk measurement.
Develop econometric models for forecasting purposes to project cashflows of RBC banking book positions used for IRRBB measurement, using internal and external time series and panel data sets; maintain strong database extract, transform, and load capabilities; and leverage industry, economic, and market information to improve model intelligence through liaison with internal and external resources.
Design, develop, and implement robust financial risk, valuation, and forecast models within RBC’s QRM risk engine.
Conduct research and analytics pertaining to model inputs and assumptions, ensuring correct model use and governance requirements.
Evaluate internal and external data to understand balance sheet dynamics, product characteristics, client behaviour, and balance sheet flows with focus on retail banking products.
Lead and perform end-to-end modelling responsibilities, including process evaluation of data quality, model performance tracking, ensuring consistency across models employed for forecasting and stress testing, and maintaining clear documentation of approach, methodologies, and processes.
Maintain requisite model governance, model documentation, model inventory, and process mapping requirements. Ensure efficient and effective model risk and compliance management, including performance of regular model validation submissions and model finding remediations.
Leveraging industry best practices including use of AI, develop and implement an internal toolkit for assessing hypotheses and mathematical models behind applied and proposed risk methodologies, stress testing, and projections.
Consider, understand, and evaluate general ledger, accounting and finance, and regulatory reporting processes, as they relate to IRRBB measurement, management, and modelling.
Perform ad hoc scenario analysis in support of balance sheet IRRBB hedging, with high degree of interaction with business units to promote business segment review, challenge, and alignment.

WHAT DO YOU NEED TO SUCCEED?

Must-have:

Graduate degree in a quantitative field such as financial engineering, mathematics, statistics, or economics.
7+ years related experience with a strong grasp of ALM practices.
Understanding of banking book balance sheet dynamics, product characteristics, client behaviour, and balance sheet flows, with focus on retail banking products.
Solid understanding of financial principles and risk concepts, including financial modelling and engineering, pricing models, econometrics, and fixed income mathematics.
Excellent capabilities in statistical and analytical principles, tools, and techniques.
Strong understanding of applicable regulatory guidelines and accounting principles, and related systems.
Strong communication and negotiation skills.
Well-organized and detail oriented, with ability to tailor analysis to the required level of precision.

Nice-to-have:

CFA and/or FRM designations, or equivalent.
Prior exposure to ALM risk engine platforms and software (e.g., QRM or similar).

WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock where applicable

Ability to make a difference and lasting impact
Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
A world-class training program in financial services
Flexible work/life balance options
Opportunities to do challenging work

Analytical Thinking, Analytics, Applied Research, Balance Sheets, Critical Thinking, Datasets, Decision Making, Financial Regulation, Interest Rate Risk Management, Mathematics Modeling, Research and Development, Risk Management, Strategic Thinking, Treasury Management

Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp. (AQN), parent company of Liberty, is a diversified international generation, transmission, and distribution utility. jobs.description:
Vice President, Finance

Our Edmonton client is a privately held, internationally recognized healthcare technology organization providing specialized medical equipment, clinical solutions, and technical support to healthcare providers across North America. The company has established a reputation for operational excellence, strong customer partnerships, and a commitment to advancing patient care through innovative technologies.

Reporting to the CFO and serving as a key member of the leadership team, the Vice President, Finance will provide strategic and operational leadership for the organization’s global finance function.

This role is responsible for ensuring the integrity of financial reporting, planning, controls, taxation, treasury, and compliance while providing timely financial insight that supports business strategy, sustainable growth, and informed decision-making. The successful candidate will lead a global finance team and partner closely with executive leadership, Operations, Commercial, and other functional leaders to align financial priorities with business objectives.

This opportunity is ideally suited for a collaborative finance leader who combines strong technical expertise with business partnership skills and enjoys operating in a complex, multi-entity, global environment.

Key Responsibilities

The responsibilities of this role include, but are not limited to:

Lead the global finance function, including financial reporting, accounting, budgeting, forecasting, treasury, taxation, compliance, and financial governance.
Ensure timely and accurate financial reporting in compliance with applicable accounting standards and regulatory requirements.
Provide financial reporting, analysis, and insight to the Board, executive leadership, lenders, and other relevant stakeholders.
Oversee global consolidated reporting, annual audits, bank reporting, and financial oversight across multiple entities and jurisdictions.
Lead the Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) function, including budgeting, forecasting, scenario planning, financial modelling, and performance analysis.
Provide financial insight and recommendations to support strategic and operational decisions.
Establish and maintain an effective global financial control environment, including policies, approval authorities, segregation of duties, and financial governance practices.
Manage the company's cash flow and liquidity, including cash management, investment governance, debt management, and foreign exchange risk management.
Ensure compliance with tax, legal, and regulatory requirements, including transfer pricing and global reporting obligations.
Serve as the finance leader responsible for the ongoing maintenance, optimization, and continuous improvement of the global ERP system.
Partner with Operations, Commercial, and executive leadership to evaluate investments, growth opportunities, pricing decisions, and other strategic initiatives.
Lead, develop, and support a high-performing finance team by setting clear expectations, fostering accountability and engagement, providing regular coaching and feedback, and managing performance to achieve objectives.

Candidate Experience

While no individual will embody every quality, the successful candidate will bring many of the following professional qualifications and personal competencies:

Recognized accounting designation (CPA).
University degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
10-15 years of progressive finance experience, including significant senior leadership experience.
Experience in global operations, manufacturing, or a similarly complex business environment.
Experience leading consolidated reporting, audits, budgeting, forecasting, treasury, taxation, and financial controls across multiple entities and jurisdictions.
Strong understanding of enterprise-scale global ERP systems and the ability to lead finance system optimization and adoption.
Advanced financial modelling, analysis, and reporting capabilities, including strong proficiency with Excel and enterprise reporting tools.
SAP experience is considered an asset.
In-depth knowledge of finance, accounting, budgeting, and cost accounting principles.
Strategic and commercially minded, with the ability to connect financial results to business priorities.
Demonstrates sound judgment, integrity, discretion, and accountability.
Builds trust and productive relationships across Operations, Commercial, and corporate functions.
Communicates complex financial information clearly to financial and non-financial audiences.
Demonstrates strong analytical, problem-solving, prioritization, and decision-making capabilities.
Strong leadership, coaching, and managerial skills.
Organized problem solver who excels in fast-paced environments and demonstrates strong judgment under pressure.

Location

Edmonton, AB

As Director, Planning & Allocations - NAM, you will lead the end-to-end Retail and eCommerce DTC planning strategy across North America, driving growth, profitability, inventory productivity, and customer experience. You will develop annual, seasonal, and long-range plans while overseeing inventory, sales, margin, and operational planning strategies across the product lifecycle. Partnering cross-functionally with Merchandising, Retail Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, Digital, and Regional Commercial leaders, you will translate business priorities into actionable strategies and data-driven decisions that support regional objectives and business growth. This role is based out of our North Vancouver office and is open to hybrid remote work. Candidates must be eligible to work in Canada.

Meet Your Future Team:

You’ll join our regional planning and allocations team – the group responsible for planning and allocating product across every Direct-to-Consumer touchpoint in the region, spanning merchandise financial planning, demand planning, inventory planning, and allocations.  Together, we make sure the right product reaches the right place at the right time, balancing growth, profitability, inventory productivity, and an exceptional guest experience across Retail and eCommerce.  We’re a collaborative, curious group that partners closely across the business and takes pride in turning ambitious commercial goals into smart, data-driven plans.

If you were in the Director, Planning & Allocations – NAM role now, here are some of the core activities you would be doing:

Owning the end-to-end planning strategy for Retail and eCommerce DTC across the North American region

Developing annual, seasonal, and long-range plans in alignment with company objectives

Establishing inventory, sales, margin, and productivity targets to support growth and profitability

Developing a holistic, strategic, approach to inventory throughout the product lifecycle to meet plan and minimize stock outs

Ensuring planning strategies support growth and profitability objectives

Building best-in-class planning teams across; Merchandise Financial Planning, Demand Planning and Inventory Planning.

Owning adoption and optimization of o9, our enterprise planning platform

Driving automation and exception-based planning process to improve efficiency and responsiveness

Leading planning process improvement and transformation initiatives

Developing and executing the DTC planning strategy aligned with business and regional priorities

Balancing growth, profitability, inventory productivity, and customer experience across channels

Partnering cross functionally and influencing cross-functional decision making across Merchandising, Retail Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, and Digital

Translating business priorities into actionable planning strategies and execution plans

Anticipating business risks and proactively developing mitigation plans to address

Driving organizational transformation and planning maturity, supporting organizational change and advancement of planning capabilities and process

Leveraging data-driven insights to influence business decisions and planning outcomes

Partnering with the Regional Commercial leadership team on business planning strategy, supporting key account business growth, while controlling inventory risks

Overseeing inventory forecasting, allocation, and resolution strategies across business units while ensuring alignment to regional objectives

Here are some of the things you could be working on in the future:

Contributing to the creation of a regional product framework and assortment structure that guides merchant execution within retail stores, ecommerce channels and wholesale to maximize sales, profit and brand positioning

Leading the creation of differentiated product strategies by channel, region and format at scale to achieve revenue and product margin goals through product range, life cycle management and pricing

new_jobs.title: Cloud Architecture & Engineering, Director
new_jobs.description:
At PwC, our people in infrastructure focus on designing and implementing robust, secure IT systems that support business operations. They enable the smooth functioning of networks, servers, and data centres to optimise performance and minimise downtime. Those in site reliability engineering at PwC will focus on enabling the reliability, scalability, and performance of organisational technology infrastructure. This will include working to automate processes, monitor systems, and resolve incidents to maintain a seamless user experience.

Meaningful work you’ll be part of

As a Director, Cloud Architecture & Engineering, you’ll work as part of a team of problem solvers, helping to solve business issues, deliver high-quality client service and operational efficiency. Responsibilities include but are not limited to: 

You will play a pivotal leadership role at the intersection of cloud strategy, architecture, engineering, and client engagement.  
This role combines deep technical cloud expertise with strategic leadership, practice development, and team coaching.  
You will shape and scale cloud capabilities, guide clients through complex transformation journeys, and help drive PwC’s cloud first vision. 
You will be responsible for designing and governing enterprise grade cloud architectures while also driving advisory engagements, leading teams, strengthening client relationships, and contributing to the innovation pipeline for cloud-based solutions and assets. 
This role requires a seasoned cloud leader who can operate fluently across business strategy, modern cloud architectures, and hands-on technical depth—while mentoring teams and influencing both internal and client executives.

Cloud Architecture & Engineering Leadership

Lead the design, governance, and implementation of end-to-end cloud architectures aligned to business goals and industry best practices. 
Architect scalable, secure, and cost optimized cloud solutions across AWS, Azure, and GCP. 
Develop cloud foundation blueprints, reference architectures, and reusable patterns. 
Oversee the design and optimization of Kubernetes platforms (EKS, AKS, GKE) and containerized environments. 
Guide the development and automation of cloud infrastructure using Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform, CloudFormation, AWS CDK, ARM, etc.). 
Provide technical guidance on compute, storage, networking, security, identity, data services, and DevOps tooling. 

Cloud Advisory & Client Engagement

Serve as a trusted advisor to executive-level stakeholders, helping them define and execute cloud strategies and operating models. 
Assess existing environments, develop modernization roadmaps, and oversee cloud migration programs. 
Lead proposal creation, solutioning activities, statements of work, and client presentations. 
Communicate complex technical concepts to nontechnical audiences clearly and effectively. 
Identify and prioritize client use cases and translate business requirements into architectural approaches and execution plans. 

Practice & Team Leadership

Build, lead, and mentor teams of cloud architects, engineers, and technical specialists. 
Foster a culture of continuous learning, experimentation, and cloud innovation. 
Recruit and grow diverse technical talent, ensuring strong career development and retention. 
Collaborate with practice leadership to define strategic direction, emerging offerings, and go-to-market assets. 
Lead initiatives that strengthen practice foundations: capability models, delivery frameworks, accelerators, patterns, and reusable assets. 

Innovation, Delivery & Thought Leadership

Lead technical innovation cycles to evaluate, test, and showcase new cloud technologies, tools, and architectures. 
Drive and participate in hands-on cloud prototyping, labbing, and solution validation. 
Develop technical demos, asset-driven solutions, and market-aligned accelerators. 
Present at internal and external events, contributing to PwC’s thought leadership presence. 
Maintain active engagement with cloud provider alliances and product engineering teams to share early insights and influence product evolution. 

Experiences And Skills you’ll use To Solve 

Technical Expertise

Extensive experience in cloud architecture and engineering across AWS (primary), Azure, and/or GCP. 
Deep knowledge of Kubernetes, containers, microservices, serverless architectures, and modern DevOps practices. 
Hands-on experience with IaC tools (Terraform strongly preferred), CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, Argo, etc.), and automated deployment patterns. 
Strong understanding of cloud security, IAM, network segmentation, encryption, monitoring, cost optimization, and governance frameworks. 
Experience supporting modernization programs such as application migration, refactoring, API strategies, and technical debt remediation. 
AI-assisted development and prior experience deploying agentic workloads and MLOps pipelines is an asset.

Leadership & Consulting Skills

Demonstrated experience leading cloud-focused teams and initiatives in a complex, multistakeholder environment. 
Strong executive communication skills suitable for client-facing consulting environments. 
Ability to bridge business and technical perspectives and articulate value propositions, architecture decisions, and tradeoffs. 
Strategic mindset with a bias toward execution, innovation, and measurable impact. 

Qualifications 

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience). 
Significant cloud architecture and engineering leadership experience. 
Preferred:  AWS Solutions Architect (Professional); Azure or GCP Architect certifications; Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) or CKAD; Terraform Associate Certification.
Ability to obtain Government of Canada Security Clearance; Level 2 security clearance is an asset.
This role does not require professional engineering licensure and is not classified as a formal engineering position under provincial regulatory definitions. While individuals with a P.Eng designation are welcome to apply, the responsibilities of this role do not involve the practice of professional engineering as defined by applicable legislation.

Senior Director, AI Business Enablement

What's the opportunity?

We're looking for a transformational leader who can serve as a strategic peer to senior business executives and drive AI-powered business transformation across an entire Line of Business or Function. As a Senior Director on the AI Business Enablement team, you will own the full AI transformation ambition for your domain — setting the vision, building the opportunity pipeline, and ensuring executive alignment from ideation through to program framing and handoff.

You will be expected to challenge, provoke, and co-develop transformation roadmaps with senior business leaders — bringing a combination of strategic rigour, AI fluency, and the credibility that comes from having built and shipped solutions, not just recommended them.

Executive partnership: Holding sustained, peer-level strategic relationships with senior business leaders (SVP+); co-developing and communicating the AI-enabled transformation vision for your domain
Pipeline origination: Identifying, sizing, and prioritising a rigorous pipeline of AI transformation opportunities — including new ideas not yet on the business’ horizon — with quantified value hypotheses ready for delivery intake

Cross-enterprise pattern recognition: Surfacing reuse opportunities, multi-LOB programs, and horizontal themes that no single vertical would initiate alone
Team leadership: Leading and developing a small team of high-performing leaders aligned to sub-segments within your domain

Have 15+ years of progressive experience in management consulting, technology, AI/ML product development, or a combination thereof

About the role:

BMO Canada Wealth Digital is accelerating the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across its customer-facing digital platforms to enhance client experiences, improve operational efficiency, and enable innovative wealth management solutions. We are seeking an experienced AI Delivery Director to lead the planning, execution, and delivery of strategic AI initiatives that support the evolution of our Wealth Management digital capabilities.

This is a senior delivery leadership role requiring the coordination of cross-functional teams across Engineering, Architecture, Security, Risk Management, Compliance, and Business organizations. The AI Delivery Director will provide end-to-end leadership across the delivery lifecycle, from intake, discovery, and prioritization through implementation, deployment, adoption, and business value realization by adopting and utilizing AI tools in SDLC. End-to-End Technology Delivery

AI Engineering and AI SDLC Leadership

Drive environment readiness, infrastructure as code, automated deployment, telemetry, performance engineering, capacity planning, disaster recovery, and production support readiness.
Promote reuse of enterprise AI capabilities, shared services, patterns, and controls while preserving clear service boundaries and ownership.
Advanced Agile and Value-Stream Delivery
Establish and continuously improve an advanced Agile operating model organized around persistent, cross-functional teams and measurable client or business outcomes.
Lead portfolio and product-level planning, backlog readiness, dependency management, release forecasting, and flow optimization across multiple teams.

Lead incident response, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and learning reviews for technology or AI quality events.
Maintain transparent risk, issue, dependency, and decision records and ensure material risks are escalated promptly.
Stakeholder, Financial and Partner Leadership
Serve as the senior technology delivery voice for Em with InvestorLine, Wealth, Technology & Operations, Applied AI, governance partners, and executive forums.
Provide concise, fact-based reporting on outcomes, delivery confidence, risks, financials, quality, and decisions required.
Own technology delivery financial stewardship, resource planning, vendor performance, commercial dependencies, and delivery commitments.
Lead co-build and vendor engagements with clear accountability, knowledge transfer, architecture compliance, security obligations, and measurable outcomes.
Create an inclusive, high-accountability environment that develops leaders, strengthens technical depth, and keeps teams focused on client outcomes.

Key Success Measures

Predictable delivery of roadmap outcomes and releases, with transparent forecast accuracy and controlled scope change.
Measurable improvement in delivery flow, engineering productivity, automation, quality, and time to value.
AI evaluation thresholds and non-functional requirements met before release and sustained in production.
Stable, secure, resilient production performance with effective observability, incident management, and continuous improvement.
Clear ownership, faster decisions, fewer cross-team handoffs, and effective dependency resolution.
Measurable client adoption, experience, business value, and risk outcomes delivered in partnership with the Product Owner.

Expert-level technology delivery leadership in large, complex, regulated environments, with accountability for multiple teams and production outcomes.
Deep practical knowledge of AI/ML and generative AI delivery, including agentic architectures, LLM application patterns, evaluations, guardrails, observability, and responsible AI controls.
Strong knowledge of wealth management and digital investing platforms, including client journeys, advice or guidance experiences, market and portfolio data, trading-related integrations, and regulatory considerations.

Qualifications And Experience

Do you think like a management consultant, thrive in a startup environment, and can’t stop thinking about the intersection of data, technology, and marketing?

Founded and headquartered in Paris, Artefact is a next-generation consulting firm, specializing in data, analytics & AI consulting, dedicated to transforming data into business impact across the entire value chain of organizations. We are proud to say that we help our clients grow their data and digital capabilities, and that we’re also growing in parallel.

You will lead a team of AI & machine learning engineers and managers, driving the design and delivery of production-grade AI solutions — from classical machine learning models to LLM-powered applications — and the pipelines that power them. You’ll bring senior technical judgment to architecture and model decisions, partner closely with clients and business stakeholders — including hands-on pre-sales work shaping proposals and solution designs — and define how context engineering, agent harnesses, and fine-tuning practices get embedded into every solution, while reporting into senior AI/technology leadership on strategy and priorities.

Context Engineering: Defining and standardizing context engineering practices — prompt and system design, RAG architectures, vector stores, memory management, and tool/function calling — so models receive the right information at the right time.

Platform Stack: Architecting and deploying solutions on Google Gemini Enterprise and Vertex AI as the primary stack, applying working knowledge of Microsoft AI Foundry and AWS Bedrock where client contexts require.

Pre-Sales & Business Development: Supporting pre-sales activities — scoping engagements, building demos and proofs of concept, and presenting solution architectures to prospective clients alongside account teams.
Machine Learning Modeling: Overseeing the development of classical and modern ML models — predictive modeling, forecasting, recommendation, and deep learning — choosing the right technique for each business problem, LLM or not.
Contributing to AI Strategy: Partnering with senior leadership to shape GenAI architecture direction, tooling decisions, and platform roadmap within your area.

What We Are Looking For

The ideal candidate has a substantial software engineering and AI background with 8+ years of experience, including at least 2–3 years working on LLM architecture, agentic design, and harness & context engineering.
Strong expertise in generative AI/LLM engineering — context engineering, agent harnesses, RAG, and agentic coding — and in cloud-native software architecture, with proven production deployments.
Master’s degree (or higher) in computer science, software engineering, or a related field.
Hands-on command of agentic SDKs (LangGraph/LangChain, Google ADK, Claude Agent SDK), agentic coding tools (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor), and modern full-stack frameworks (TypeScript/React front ends; Python/Node backends).
Experience designing cloud architectures: microservices, serverless, containers/Kubernetes, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code.
Solid grasp of AI system design: agents, tool use, evaluation harnesses, guardrails, observability, and LLMOps.
Experience with data & context modeling and ingestion/processing pipelines on data lakes and data warehouses, including vector and graph storage strategies (embeddings, knowledge graphs).
Deep experience with Google Gemini Enterprise / Vertex AI; basic working knowledge of Microsoft AI Foundry and AWS Bedrock.
Experience leading and growing engineering teams, and supporting pre-sales: proposals, demos, and solution scoping with clients.
Excellent communication skills and comfort collaborating across teams and with stakeholders.
Strong business acumen with an interest in business-facing work.
Adaptability and a start-up mentality to thrive in a dynamic environment.

We are united by our values
and strengthened by our hybrid expertise
.

There is always a way: We're from the breed of does, of diggers, of makers. Because ideas are valuable only if executed.
Client trust is won on the field: Addressing client needs flows better hands on at their side.

new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

Motive empowers the people who run physical operations with tools to make their work safer, more productive, and more profitable. For the first time ever, safety, operations and finance teams can manage their drivers, vehicles, equipment, and fleet related spend in a single system. Combined with industry leading AI, the Motive platform gives you complete visibility and control, and significantly reduces manual workloads by automating and simplifying tasks.

Motive serves nearly 100,000 customers – from Fortune 500 enterprises to small businesses – across a wide range of industries, including transportation and logistics, construction, energy, field service, manufacturing, agriculture, food and beverage, retail, and the public sector.

Visit gomotive.com to learn more.

About The Role

Motive is moving to an AI-driven development lifecycle. Agents that plan, generate, test, review, and help operate our systems — with engineers directing the work rather than typing all of it — are where software engineering at Motive is going. That direction is set. What we need now is a leader to build it.

We are hiring a Director of Developer Platform & Experience to own that execution and the platform underneath it. This role owns Motive's internal developer ecosystem end to end: developer experience, developer infrastructure, build and CI/CD systems, and the testing frameworks that let hundreds of engineers move quickly without breaking things. It also owns AI-DLC in practice — the tooling, cloud agent infrastructure, evaluation practice, and governance that determine whether agentic development actually makes us faster or just makes us noisier.

Our engineering organization spans North America, Europe, and Asia, across a Rails monolith, Go services, mobile, and embedded systems. How fast and how confidently that organization ships is one of our most important business levers.

This is a builder's leadership role, not a strategy role. You will inherit real systems and real teams, and be measured on whether engineers at Motive ship faster, with higher confidence, and with less friction than they did the quarter before.

The mandates

AI-driven development — make agentic development a governed, measured, everyday part of how Motive builds software.
Cloud-based agentic development infrastructure — build the substrate that lets agents run in the cloud, in parallel, safely.
Developer experience — make the inner loop fast and the right path the easy path.
Developer infrastructure — make build, CI/CD, and release systems fast, reliable, and cost-aware at scale.

The defining challenge: agentic development in the cloud

Most AI coding adoption stops at the laptop — one engineer, one agent, one local checkout. That ceiling is low, and moving past it is the signature technical challenge of this role.

You will build the infrastructure that runs agentic development in the cloud: ephemeral, reproducible, isolated environments where many agents work concurrently on real Motive codebases, run real tests against real dependencies, and open real pull requests — without an engineer babysitting a terminal, and without compromising security or blowing up spend.

This is a hard distributed-systems and platform problem, not a tooling procurement exercise. Done right, engineers stop being throughput-bound by their own machines and start operating as reviewers and directors of parallel work. We want a leader who finds that problem exciting and has the platform depth to solve it.

What you'll own

AI-driven development lifecycle (AI-DLC)

Translate Motive's AI-driven development direction into an executable multi-year plan — how agents plan, generate, test, review, and operate under human direction, what "human in the loop" means at each stage, and where engineers spend their time as a result.
Evaluate, select, and roll out AI developer tools (coding agents, code review, test generation, incident investigation, documentation) and build the internal scaffolding — context, MCP servers, evals, guardrails — that makes them effective on Motive's actual codebases rather than on a demo repo.
Stand up a rigorous LLM and agent evaluation practice: benchmarks, offline and online evals, quality and cost regression tracking, and a defensible model and vendor selection process that survives a fast-moving landscape.
Own the governance layer with Security, Legal, and Platform: acceptable use, code provenance and licensing, secrets and data handling, and audit trails for AI-generated changes.
Define and report the adoption and impact metrics that tell us whether this is actually working — not just seat counts and enthusiasm.
Bring the organization along. Drive enablement, internal advocacy, and the cultural shift from "write code, then review" to continuous review of agent-generated work.

Cloud-based agentic development infrastructure

Build and own the platform that runs agentic development in the cloud: on-demand, reproducible, isolated workspaces provisioned per task, with the right source, dependencies, secrets, and services already in place.
Design for concurrency and safety — sandboxed execution, least-privilege credentials, network egress controls, and blast-radius limits so many agents can run against real codebases without becoming a security or reliability incident.
Make agent runs fast and cheap: warm environment pools, caching and snapshotting, incremental builds, and test selection so a cloud agent loop is measured in minutes, not tens of minutes.
Own the orchestration and control plane — queueing, scheduling, autoscaling on Kubernetes, session lifecycle, artifact and log retention, and observability into what agents did and why.
Own unit economics. Instrument per-task and per-agent cost, set budgets and quotas, and keep the platform financially sustainable as usage scales across the org.
Build the human interface layer: how engineers dispatch work to cloud agents, monitor fleets of concurrent runs, review and merge results, and intervene when a run goes sideways.
Design for multi-region (US and EU) from the start, with configuration-driven rather than hardcoded regional behavior, and honor data residency and code-egress constraints.

Developer Experience

Own the inner loop end to end: local and cloud development environments, code search and navigation, IDE and agent tooling, dependency management, and onboarding time-to-first-PR.
Treat developers as your customers. Run regular DevEx research — surveys, interviews, instrumented telemetry — and publish a prioritized backlog the whole engineering org can see.
Define and drive the internal developer platform: golden paths, service scaffolding, and self-service capabilities that make the right way the easy way.

Developer infrastructure and engineering velocity

Own build systems, CI/CD, artifact and release pipelines, and the platform's outer loop across a Rails monolith, Go services, mobile, and embedded/firmware codebases.
Drive step-function improvements in DORA and velocity metrics: PR lead time, build and CI duration, CI reliability and flake rate, change failure rate, and time to restore.
Make cost, scale, and reliability of the developer platform a first-class concern — including multi-region (US and EU) behavior and configuration flexibility rather than hardcoded assumptions.

Testing and quality engineering

Own the testing strategy and frameworks: unit, integration, contract, end-to-end, hardware-in-the-loop, and performance. Drive test reliability, isolation, and speed so engineers trust the signal.
Build the infrastructure that makes high-quality testing cheap: fixtures, factories, test data management, environment provisioning, parallelization, and flake detection and quarantine.
Partner with quality and release engineering to shift quality left without slowing teams down.

Leadership

Lead a multi-team organization as a manager of managers, hiring and developing engineering managers and senior/staff-plus ICs.
Run an org distributed across North American and Asian time zones with genuine care for handoffs, overlap hours, on-call fairness, and inclusion — not just calendar math.
Operate as a peer to product and infrastructure leaders, influence a large engineering org without direct authority, and communicate strategy and results credibly to executives.

What we're looking for

Required

12+ years in software engineering with 6+ years leading engineering teams, including 2+ years as a manager of managers (Director, Senior Manager of Managers, or equivalent scope).
A real developer background — you have shipped and operated production systems, and engineers respect your technical judgment.
Deep DevOps and infrastructure depth: CI/CD, build systems, containers and Kubernetes, infrastructure as code (Terraform), cloud platforms (AWS preferred), and observability.
Demonstrated ownership of developer productivity, developer platform, or developer infrastructure at meaningful scale (hundreds of engineers or a large multi-language codebase), with measurable velocity outcomes you can describe.
Hands-on experience with modern AI developer tooling and a clear, opinionated point of view on where agentic development genuinely helps and where it does not.
Experience building or operating cloud-based development or execution environments — remote dev environments, ephemeral CI/build workers, container sandboxing, or multi-tenant compute platforms — including the security and cost controls that make them viable at scale.
Practical understanding of LLM evaluation — how to benchmark models and agents for coding tasks, how to measure quality and cost, and how to avoid being sold a demo.
Strong empathy for developers: you instrument the pain, listen to it, and prioritize accordingly rather than shipping platforms nobody adopts.
Experience leading distributed teams across multiple time zones.

Preferred

Experience with a large monolith undergoing modernization, and with polyglot environments (Ruby on Rails, Go, mobile, embedded).
Background in test infrastructure at scale — flake reduction, test selection, parallelization, hermetic environments.
Experience running platform work as a product: roadmaps, adoption funnels, internal customers, feature-flagged rollouts.
Familiarity with multi-region deployment and data residency constraints (US/EU).
Open source contribution, developer community involvement, or public writing on developer productivity or AI-assisted engineering.

Pay Transparency

Motive offers benefits including health, pharmacy, optical and dental care benefits, paid time off, sick time off, short term and long term disability coverage, life insurance as well as 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). new_jobs.title: Senior Director, Solutions Architecture — Americas
new_jobs.description:
Who are we?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

As the Senior Director of Solutions Architecture for the Americas at Cohere, you will own the US and Canada commercial Solutions Architecture function. You will lead the team that turns enterprise interest in agentic AI into deployed, production systems, and you will be accountable for the technical win in the most competitive AI market in the world. The United States and Canada are our largest commercial opportunity, and this seat owns how we win them.

You will take an established, distributed team of strong technical people and raise what it can do — setting the bar and establishing the operating rhythm that lets a team of generalists run consistent, industry-fluent plays at enterprise scale. You will set direction for the function, sit on the Solution Architecture leadership team alongside the regional leaders for EMEA and Asia Pacific, and contribute to company-wide decisions with your peers across Sales, Product and Engineering.

In This Role, You Will

Lead and Scale the Organization: Build, coach and develop a high-performing Solutions Architecture organization across the US and Canada, and grow the senior technical talent within it.
Own the Technical Win: Be personally accountable for the technical outcome of the region’s most strategic pursuits, and be in the room for the ones that decide the year.
Own the US Market: Lead how Cohere positions, proves and sells into US enterprises — our largest commercial opportunity, and the market this seat is measured on.
Extend Our Reach: Grow the share of the region’s pipeline the team is technically leading, and make sure we are engaged early on the opportunities that matter most.
Own the Number with Sales: Partner with regional Sales leadership as a co-owner of the region’s number, not as a support function to it.
Set Direction for the Function: Define the vision, strategy and operating model for Americas Solutions Architecture, and hold your leaders accountable for delivery and execution against it.
Build Repeatable Solution Practices: Establish scalable solution-selling methodologies, industry playbooks, executive narratives, business cases and technical delivery frameworks that improve consistency and win rates.
Architect Enterprise AI Solutions: Guide customers in designing secure, scalable, production-ready agentic AI solutions across cloud, hybrid, VPC and on-premises environments.
Shape Product Direction: Partner closely with Product and Engineering to translate customer feedback and market needs into platform improvements and roadmap priorities.
Attract Talent to Cohere: Bring senior technical field talent with you and continue to attract it. Building the bench is part of the job, not a consequence of it.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and develop the Americas commercial Solutions Architecture team through coaching, hiring, performance management and career development.
Partner with regional Sales leadership to pursue and close strategic enterprise opportunities across financial services, healthcare, energy, technology and other key verticals.
Own the region’s technical coverage model, and ensure the team is engaged early and consistently on the opportunities that matter most.
Lead executive workshops, discovery sessions, solution presentations and technical deep dives with C-suite and senior customer stakeholders.
Develop business cases, solution architectures, implementation roadmaps and technical proposals that align customer objectives with Cohere’s platform.
Guide customers through the deployment of enterprise AI solutions, ensuring scalability, security, governance and operational readiness.
Create repeatable solution assets, industry playbooks and best practices that enable the team to consistently deliver high-quality customer engagements.
Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Sales and Customer Success to ensure alignment between customer needs and platform evolution, and contribute to decisions that reach beyond your own function.
Serve as the voice of the field by capturing customer feedback and competitive insights that influence product strategy.
Own and report on the region’s operational and commercial metrics, including technical win rates, pipeline health, coverage and team performance.

What We’re Looking For

Leadership Experience: 15+ years in Solutions Architecture, Solutions Engineering, Technical Consulting or Enterprise Architecture, including 7+ years leading customer-facing technical teams, and a record of developing people into senior and leadership roles.
People Leadership: A proven record of hiring, coaching and developing high-performing Solutions Architecture or Solutions Engineering teams, and of building or transforming an organization rather than inheriting a healthy one.
Executive Presence: You command a room. You are credible in front of a CEO and their business leaders, the people who own the problem and the budget, and equally credible in front of a Chief Information Officer, a Chief AI Officer or a Chief Information Security Officer. You can move between the business case and the architecture without losing either audience.
Hands-On Technical Credibility: You are technical enough to be believed by a strong engineering bench. You work with models and agents yourself, you can pressure-test your team’s architecture, and you can be the most useful person in a design conversation when it matters. This is a player-coach seat, not an overlay.
Commercial Acumen: A demonstrated ability to partner with enterprise Sales leadership, influence strategic deals, and articulate business value to executive stakeholders. You have carried a number and can point to deals you personally moved.
Consulting Mindset: Experience leading complex enterprise solution engagements, developing business cases, implementation plans and executive-ready recommendations.
Technical Expertise: A strong understanding of modern AI architectures, including large language models, agentic systems, retrieval, enterprise integrations, cloud platforms, hybrid and on-premises deployments, security and governance.
Enterprise Experience: Experience designing and delivering enterprise technology solutions in complex, regulated or large-scale environments.
Cross-Functional Influence: A record of contributing to decisions beyond your own function, and of working effectively with Product and Engineering leadership.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience building or turning around a regional technical field organization, and evidence of what changed as a result.
Background in enterprise AI, cloud, or data platform companies, or applied AI consulting organizations.
Experience supporting customers in regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, energy, or the public sector.
Experience building repeatable solution-selling methodologies and helping generalist technical teams operate at a consistently high level.
A network of senior technical field talent you can attract to Cohere.
Experience operating in high-growth environments where speed, ownership and cross-functional collaboration are critical.

Full-Time Employees At Cohere Enjoy These Perks

A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.
Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.
RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.
100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.
Annual enrichment benefits:

Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.

Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)
Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

How And Where We Work

Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.
For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.
For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.
Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form, and we will work together to meet your needs.

We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.

Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers page.

new_jobs.description:
Hammond Power Solutions Inc.
is a global manufacturer headquartered in Guelph, Ontario, Canada. HPS has grown to become the leader in North America in the custom design and manufacture of dry type transformers. For the past century, HPS has grown to deliver electrical power solutions to global markets and provides solutions for complex applications like, mining, rectifier, drives, traction, wind, solar and many other electrical power applications. The world relies on HPS to continually conceive and produce state-of-the-art transformer technology. We currently have an opening for a Director, Enterprise Business Applications,
come grow with us!

Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the Director, Enterprise Business Applications is accountable for the strategy, performance, and evolution of the organization’s enterprise business application portfolio. This role ensures that core platforms supporting manufacturing, supply chain, finance, commercial, P&C, and corporate functions are reliable, scalable, secure, and aligned with business priorities in a multinational manufacturing environment, while driving responsible adoption of AI-enabled capabilities.

Key Responsibilities Include

Define and execute a multi-year enterprise applications strategy aligned with business objectives and operating priorities
Partner with business and functional leaders to translate needs into technology roadmaps and investment plans.
Oversee the performance, stability, and lifecycle management of enterprise applications, including incident, change, and release processes.
Lead modernization initiatives across ERP, CRM, HRIS, finance, and manufacturing systems to improve scalability and reduce technical debt.
Drive adoption of AI-enabled capabilities (e.g., vendor AI, Microsoft Copilot, custom solutions) to enhance productivity, decision-making, and automation.
Ensure AI-enabled features and automations are operated reliably, monitored effectively, and supported within standard service models.
Enable system integration, process standardization, and data-driven operations
Support M&A activities by assessing application and data landscapes, defining target-state architectures, and planning phased integrations, including AI and analytics alignment.
Manage budgets, vendors, and implementation partners, ensuring effective delivery and measurable business value (including software licensing, AI services, support and delivery partners)
Establish governance frameworks, ensuring compliance with cybersecurity, data, and regulatory requirements, and managing application and AI-related risk
Lead and develop global application teams, fostering a high-performance, collaborative, and outcome-focused culture.
Partner with risk, security, legal, and compliance teams to proactively identify and mitigate application and AI-related risks.

Do you qualify? We are seeking:

10+ years of experience in enterprise applications leadership
Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related field (Master’s an asset)
Proven experience in complex, manufacturing-focused environments
Proven experience implementing and overseeing AI‑enabled business applications, including embedded vendor AI and productivity copilots, with awareness of data, security, and operational implications.
Strong expertise across ERP-centric ecosystems supporting supply chain, finance, HR, and operations
Solid understanding of application architecture, integration, and governance practices.
Demonstrated ability to translate business strategy into technology roadmaps and outcomes
Relevant certifications (PMP, Agile, ERP, Azure/AWS) considered an asset
Excellent communication and leadership skills

NOTE: Hammond Power Solutions encourages applications from all qualified candidates. HPS has a great record of accommodating persons with disabilities. Contact our People & Culture team if you need accommodation at any stage of the application process or want more information on our accommodation policies.

Some Of The Benefits Of Working At Hammond

We are Great Place to Work Certified! Our people work hard for us—so we make sure our benefits work hard for them. Our equitable pay, benefits, and practices prioritize security, health, and well-being while sharing in our business success through variable pay programs and our Employee Stock Ownership Program.

Our core benefits focus on wellness, mental health, and financial security when employees need them the most, early career or getting ready for retirement. We also support work-life balance through flexible work schedules, paid time off, and leaves of absence. Employees and their families also have access to our confidential, best-in-class Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP).

We are committed to sustainable business practices and offer opportunities for our employees to support the communities where we live and work through our Hammond Giving Strategy.

new_jobs.title: Director, Corporate Underwriting Analytics and Digital Risk
new_jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do.

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

Job Description:

Location
: hybrid, work from home

The Director, Corporate Underwriting Analytics and Digital Risk is a high performer in the underwriting risk community who thrives on the challenge of applying innovative problem-solving skills and solutions that align with Sun Life's risk tolerance. As a member of the Corporate Risk team, this person will foster a forward thinking, collaborative, and results oriented mindset within the team and key stakeholders throughout the Sun Life Enterprise. This position is a global risk role and will interact and liaise with risk management teams across the world.

What will you do?

Direct and complete activities related to the redesigning of existing programs to manage mortality and morbidity risk as they pertain to the underwriting risk management framework for the enterprise.
Develop performance management tools and processes to ensure compliance with the Enterprise Underwriting Operating Guideline.
Assess mortality and morbidity experience and report to the Corporate Chief Underwriter with thorough investigation of findings, assessment of any material risk implications, and recommendation for corrective actions.
Serve as an expert resource for referral of complex medically underwriting cases and financial underwriting risks. Make final decisions on complex underwriting risks within stated approval authority.
As Second Line of Defense, review and challenge the Business Unit's policies and practices to ensure compliance to the Underwriting Enterprise Operating Guideline.
Provide updates to the Director, Risk Controls and Compliance regarding any non-compliances to the UWEOG.
Develop strong relationships and partnerships with the Global Underwriting teams, product and pricing teams, Insurance Risk team and internal and external reinsurance partners.
Under the direction of the VP, Chief Underwriter, assist in driving changes to methodologies and practices which may present unfavorable mortality/morbidity experience through research, analysis of medical and non-medical risk factors, and presentation of key findings to underwriting leadership.

What do you need to succeed?

Minimum 10 years experience as an individual Life Underwriter, underwriting of multiple lines of business or products for multiple distribution channels.
Previous life approval authority of $10,000,000 and critical illness approval authority of $1,000,000.
Knowledge of and practical application of various risk assessment tools such as AI, risk propensity models, automated underwriting workflows, and various point of sales tools such as direct to consumer, and how they impact mortality/morbidity results as well as a strong understanding of non-medical issues such as fraud.
Knowledge of product development practices and concepts and assessment of risk to the organization, adherence to UWEOG and corporate risk appetite.
Ability to learn on the fly and with limited knowledge and in a dynamic work environment, as well as take a project from ideation to implementation.
Ability to apply underwriting, statistical analysis, mathematical, and actuarial knowledge to ensure delivery of team deliverables and implement projects/assignments to completion.
Knowledge of industry best practices and standards.
In-depth knowledge of underwriting risk assessment tools and standards as they relate to risk management programs.
Well-developed interpersonal as well as excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to work independently and make complex decisions in a risk setting.
As this position is posted in several locations, we specify that bilingualism (French, English, both oral and written) is required for Quebec only for the frequent interactions with English and French-speaking colleagues or internal partners across Canada or worldwide.

Reasons why should you join us under the sun

A collaborative and interactive team environment.
Opportunities to own your career development with programs to continuously learn, build skills, grow through coaching and more.
As a hybrid organization, you and your leader use business and Client needs to choose where you work, at home or in the office.
Our unique Sabbatical Program gives you the opportunity to take up to 6 weeks off, every five years.
We are proud to be on the 2026 Best Workplaces in Canada list by Great Place to Work.

The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.

Diversity and inclusion have always been at the core of our values at Sun Life. A diverse workforce with wide perspectives and creative ideas benefits our Clients, the communities where we operate and all of us as colleagues. We welcome applications from qualified individuals from all backgrounds.

Persons with disabilities who need accommodation in the application process, or those needing job postings in an alternative format, may e-mail a request to thebrightside@sunlife.com.

We are proud to be a hybrid organization that offers our employees the choice and flexibility to work from both the office and virtually based on the needs of the business, our Clients and you.

We may use artificial intelligence to support candidate sourcing, screening, interview scheduling.

We thank all applicants for showing an interest in this position. Only those selected for an interview will be contacted.
