This position will define and drive the company’s practical adoption of artificial intelligence across the business. This is not primarily an IT infrastructure, software development or research role. It is a business transformation role for someone who can understand how the company makes money, how its plants and customer programs operate, where decisions and processes break down, and where AI can create measurable advantage.
The person will own the AI opportunity portfolio from discovery through value realization: identifying and sizing high-value use cases, redesigning workflows and decision processes, determining data and technology requirements, coordinating internal and external technical resources, guiding pilots into scaled deployment, building organizational capability, and measuring financial and operational results.
The role will initially operate as a high-leverage individual contributor. Success depends less on personally building every model and more on asking the right questions, selecting the right problems, challenging vendors and specialists, and ensuring solutions are adopted in the business and sustained.

Core Mandate

Build a phased enterprise AI roadmap tied directly to company business priorities, plant economics and customer-program economics.
Create a repeatable method for finding, evaluating and prioritizing AI opportunities based on value, feasibility, data readiness, adoption requirements and risk.
Turn selected opportunities into implemented solutions that change how work is performed and how decisions are made, rather than producing disconnected pilots or demonstrations.
Develop the internal operating model, governance, external partner ecosystem and AI literacy required to scale successful solutions across facilities and functions.
Own value realization: each meaningful initiative should have a baseline, business case, accountable owner, adoption plan and measurable outcome.

Key Responsibilities

1. AI Strategy, Opportunity Portfolio & Roadmap
Develop and maintain the enterprise AI transformation roadmap across manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, quality, R&D/formulation, commercialization, commercial/customer processes, finance and supporting functions.
Build a decision and process inventory to identify repetitive, high-value, data-rich business situations where AI, automation or advanced analytics can materially improve outcomes.
Prioritize use cases by expected economic value, strategic importance, feasibility, data readiness, scalability, change impact and risk; stop low-value or poorly grounded initiatives early.
Continuously assess the AI landscape—including generative AI, agents, machine learning, computer vision, optimization, digital twins and industrial AI—and translate relevant advances into practical recommendations for the company.

2. Manufacturing & Intelligent Operations
Work directly with plant, engineering, maintenance, quality and operations leaders to identify AI-enabled improvements in process control, batch optimization, yield, quality, line performance, changeovers, reliability, downtime, energy, waste and safety.
Identify opportunities for predictive quality, predictive maintenance, machine vision, intelligent scheduling, digital twins and decision support where the operational data and economics justify them.
Design pilots with clear operating baselines and success measures, then create the playbook required to replicate proven solutions across relevant sites and assets.
Ensure AI is embedded into standard operating processes and decision routines with appropriate human oversight, rather than operating as a separate technology layer.

3. Contract Manufacturing, Customer Programs & Commercialization
Apply AI to the full customer-program lifecycle, including opportunity identification, RFQ/quoting, formulation and product development, packaging/specification management, commercialization, production readiness, fulfillment and ongoing program profitability.
Develop better decision support around bid/no-bid, pricing floors, capacity implications, changeover burden, working capital, forecast reliability, customer service requirements and true program economics.
Explore AI-enabled customer and category intelligence that can identify assortment gaps, private-label opportunities, cross-sell opportunities, packaging gaps and product concepts the company can proactively bring to customers.
Use connected data to improve launch execution, specification/artwork consistency, retailer/customer compliance, deductions/chargebacks and root-cause learning from complaints and service failures.

4. Supply Chain, Procurement & Planning
Identify AI opportunities in forecasting, S&OP/IBP, inventory, raw-material planning, procurement, sourcing, supplier intelligence, production scheduling, warehousing and transportation.
Improve the company’s ability to predict customer demand and forecast reliability, allocate capacity and materials, sequence production and manage working capital under uncertainty.
Use AI to surface exceptions and recommended actions so teams can spend less time assembling information and more time resolving the decisions that matter.

5. Data, Technology & Partner Orchestration
Define practical data-readiness requirements for AI use cases and work with IT, plant systems, Finance, Quality, R&D and other data owners to improve access, context and reliability.
Evaluate AI platforms, specialist vendors, consultants and implementation partners based on business fit, architecture, security, scalability, interoperability, total cost and expected value.
Make informed build-vs-buy-vs-partner recommendations and ensure the company retains appropriate knowledge, control and portability as capabilities scale.
Act as the business product owner for AI initiatives while technical specialists own the detailed engineering, infrastructure and model construction where appropriate.

6. Governance, Risk & Responsible AI
Establish proportionate AI governance covering privacy, cybersecurity, customer confidentiality and IP, data access, model risk, human oversight, transparency, validation and regulatory requirements.
Create clear decision rights defining where AI may inform, recommend or execute, and where human approval remains required.
Ensure use cases involving regulated products, quality systems or customer-sensitive information are developed and validated with the appropriate functional experts.

7. Change, Adoption & Capability Building
Build AI literacy among executives, plant leaders, managers and frontline users through practical education tied to the company’s work rather than generic technology training.
Create a network of functional and site champions who can identify opportunities, support adoption and help scale what works.
Address resistance, role changes, trust and skill gaps directly; redesign processes and responsibilities where AI changes how work should be performed.
Communicate wins, failures and lessons openly so the organization becomes progressively better at selecting and deploying AI.

8. Value Realization & Executive Reporting
Build business cases and establish measurable baselines before meaningful investment is made.
Track value across cost, margin, working capital, throughput, yield, quality, service, innovation speed, risk reduction and employee productivity as relevant to each use case.
Maintain a portfolio view of AI investments, adoption and realized value, and report progress, risks and priorities to senior leadership.
Treat adoption and sustained operating impact—not the number of pilots launched—as the primary definition of success.

Illustrative Initial Opportunity Areas

Manufacturing:
Batch/process optimization; predictive quality; machine vision; maintenance/reliability; line scheduling/changeovers; energy, yield and waste.
Product & R&D:
Formulation optimization; raw-material substitution; experiment prioritization; specification knowledge; faster customer/product development.
Supply Chain:
Demand forecasting; customer forecast quality; inventory; procurement; supplier intelligence; production planning; logistics and working capital.
Private Label / Commercial:
RFQ and quote intelligence; bid/no-bid; customer/program profitability; assortment whitespace; cross-sell; customer opportunity intelligence.
Commercialization & Quality:
Launch control tower; specification/artwork consistency; complaints-to-root-cause; regulatory/product-stewardship impact analysis; customer compliance.
Knowledge & Administration:
Plant/SOP/maintenance knowledge assistants; document processing; management reporting; finance and back-office workflow automation.

Candidate Profile

The strongest candidate is likely an experienced manufacturing, operations, supply-chain, analytics or business-transformation leader who has become sophisticated in AI—not necessarily a career AI researcher or software engineer. Because modern generative AI and agent technologies are new, depth of practical use and demonstrated outcomes matter more than an arbitrary number of years with “AI” in a title.
Typically 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing, operations, supply chain, digital/business transformation, advanced analytics or a closely related environment.
Demonstrated recent ownership of meaningful AI, advanced-analytics, automation or digital-transformation initiatives from problem definition through deployment and measurable business impact.
Strong understanding of manufacturing economics and operational processes; experience in process manufacturing, CPG, chemicals, private label, contract manufacturing or other complex multi-site industrial environments is strongly preferred.
Practical fluency in current AI capabilities, including generative AI, AI agents, machine learning, predictive analytics, optimization, computer vision and intelligent automation. The candidate does not need to personally code every solution, but must understand enough to challenge technical assumptions and vendors.
Strong financial and business acumen: can build a credible business case, quantify value, understand trade-offs and distinguish an interesting technology from an investable business opportunity.
Proven ability to lead through influence across plant operations, engineering, supply chain, quality, R&D, Finance, IT/data teams and senior leadership without necessarily owning those functions directly.
Experience working with external consultants, software/platform providers and specialist technical partners; capable of making build/buy/partner decisions.
Excellent facilitation and communication skills, from plant-floor working sessions to executive presentations.
Comfort with ambiguity and an entrepreneurial bias toward practical experimentation, learning and scale.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Business, Computer/Data Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced degree is beneficial but not required.
Ability and willingness to travel regularly among company facilities as projects require.

What Success Looks Like

Visit key company sites and build a grounded view of operations, customer-program workflows, current systems/data and organizational readiness.
Create an enterprise AI opportunity map and prioritized initial roadmap with business cases, data requirements,

The Director of FP&A, R&D acts as the strategic finance partner to Engineering, Product, and Data/ML leadership, owning the R&D operating plan and establishing LLM economics as a fundamental financial discipline. This role manages the P&L for R&D headcount and Cost of Revenue (CoR) for AI in production, driving efficiency through direct engagement with our data stack (BigQuery/dbt).

What You'll Do

Partner day to day with engineering, product, and data leaders as their trusted finance counterpart.
Build the analyses that shape build-vs-buy, pricing, and infrastructure decisions.
Support foundation-model and cloud vendor negotiations with data-backed positions.
Deliver clear, concise reporting and variance commentary to the CFO, FP&A leadership, and the board.
Own the R&D budget, forecast, and headcount plan across Engineering, Product, and Data/ML. Drive the re-forecast cycle and keep hiring plans tied to output and priorities.
Make LLM/inference and cloud compute cost a first-class, closely monitored metric. Build the model that tracks unit costs; monitor spend daily; and partner with engineering to find and defend efficiency. This is not a monthly-close afterthought, it's a core operating metric of the business.
Own the connection between usage, inference cost, and gross margin. Model the margin impact of new products, pricing changes, and model/infrastructure choices, and make the tradeoffs legible to leadership.
Bring financial rigor to major R&D spend decisions including foundation-model and API contracts, cloud commitments, data, and dev tooling, including negotiation support and ROI cases.

What We Look For

8+ years in FP&A / corporate finance, with meaningful time supporting R&D, Engineering, or a technical/product org.
Deep comfort with SaaS and AI/usage-based economics: CoR, gross margin, unit economics, and how infrastructure/inference cost drives them.
Strong SQL (BigQuery a major plus) and expert Excel/Sheets modeling, with clean, maintainable model architecture.
Strong grasp of how R&D spend flows through the P&L.
Ability to be a genuine partner to technical leaders, holding substantive conversations with engineering or ML leads to translate technical work into financial views.
Precise, low-ego, self-directed, and concise work ethic.
Nice to have: Experience at a high-growth AI/ML company, familiarity with modern data stacks, contract negotiation experience, people management experience, and CPA/CA/CFA.
Nice to have: Familiarity with a modern data stack (dbt, EPMs) and building repeatable, auditable finance pipelines.

Hubs in San Francisco and Toronto.

Role Summary

This position has a hybrid work arrangement (3/days week in person), and can be based out of our Mississauga or Niagara Falls offices.

Key Responsibilities

BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT

Partner with Operations leadership to support supply chain, manufacturing, inventory, and operational strategies.
Provide financial insights and decision support on productivity initiatives, network optimization, strategic investments, and operating model improvements.
Assess financial implications of operational decisions across cost, service, inventory, cash flow, and profitability objectives.
Deliver scenario analysis and recommendations to support informed decision-making and long-term value creation.

Partner with the EVP Supply Chain on multi-year value creation plans focused on productivity, inventory optimization, working capital improvement

CAPITAL STEWARDSHIP

Lead the annual and long-range capital planning process in partnership with Operations leadership.
Evaluate and prioritize capital investments based on strategic alignment, risk, return, and business impact.
Establish and maintain capital governance processes, including project approval, tracking, reporting, and benefit realization.
Monitor capital portfolio performance and challenge business case assumptions to ensure strong ROI outcomes.
Provide financial oversight of inventory investments, inventory valuation, inventory accuracy, and working capital performance.
Partner with Operations to ensure inventory strategies are aligned with business objectives and reflected appropriately in forecasts, budgets, and financial plans.

FINANCE EXCELLENCE

Provide financial stewardship of Operations results, including COGS, manufacturing costs, inventory, working capital, and capital investments.
Lead forecasting, reporting, and performance management processes that provide visibility into operational results and key business drivers.
Drive fixed and variable COGS analysis to identify productivity opportunities, cost drivers, manufacturing efficiencies, and margin improvement actions.
Deliver meaningful KPI reporting, variance analysis, and insights that drive accountability and business performance.

Lifemark Health Group (LHG) is a market leader in customized healthcare solutions. With over 20 years of service excellence, LHG is one of the largest, most trusted, and most comprehensive providers in Canada. As a national healthcare company, LHG employs over 5,000 highly trained clinicians, medical experts and team members in almost 400 locations coast-to-coast and continues to grow both organically as well as through acquisitions. With that growth, is a vision to be the most innovative healthcare providers in community rehabilitation, workplace health and wellness and medical assessment services. Lifemark was acquired by Loblaw Companies on May 10, 2022.

About the role:

As a senior technology and product leader, you will own the strategy, investment portfolio, architecture alignment and evolution of Lifemark’s Product & Platform ecosystem. You will translate business strategy into a multi-year product and platform roadmap that connects referral management, clinical operations, affiliate and customer partners, patients, and enterprise capabilities across Lifemark’s national care network.

The role is accountable for maximizing the value of Lifemark’s proprietary and third-party platforms, and integrated partner capabilities. You will lead the Product Management organization and work closely with Engineering, Enterprise Architecture, Data & Analytics, Security and business leaders to ensure the ecosystem evolves as an integrated, modular platform rather than a collection of independently managed systems.

A key mandate is to establish a modular enterprise architecture that enables Lifemark to reuse common capabilities across products and businesses, integrate acquisitions more efficiently, and selectively build, buy or partner for new functionality. This includes defining clear platform boundaries, shared services, APIs, integration patterns, enterprise data models and reusable components that allow experiences and capabilities to evolve without requiring replacement of core systems.

Success will be measured through improved patient access, clinician productivity, clinic operational efficiency, referral performance, acquisition scalability, technology reuse and return on technology investment.

Key Responsibilities:

Product & Platform Strategy: Own the multi-year strategy and roadmap for Lifemark’s integrated Product & Platform ecosystem, aligned to enterprise growth, clinical and operational priorities.
Enterprise Architecture & Platform Evolution: Partner with Enterprise Architecture and Engineering to define the target-state architecture for the ecosystem, including platform boundaries, shared services, APIs, integration patterns, dataflowsand technology standards.
Modular Capability Strategy: Establish a modular approach to product development, identifying common capabilities that can be developed once and reused proprietary platforms, acquisition businesses and future platforms. Examples may include scheduling, identity and access, communications, billing, payments, document management, reporting, patient engagement and workflow services.
Build, Buy, Partner & Integrate: Determine where Lifemark should build proprietary capabilities, leverage third-party solutions, establish strategic partnerships or integrate existing enterprise platforms while preserving control of strategically important systems and data.
Portfolio & Investment Management: Prioritize investments across products, platforms and shared capabilities based on business value, strategic fit, architectural alignment, capacity, risk and ROI.
High-Performing Product Organization: Build, lead and develop Product Managers, Business Solution Managers and Business Systems Analysts and establish consistent product-management disciplines across the organization.
Business Outcomes: Establish measurable product outcomes and ensure roadmap investments deliver improvements in clinician productivity, patient experience, referral performance, operational efficiency and network scalability.
Product Discovery & Customer Insight: Establish continuous feedback loops with end users and enterprise stakeholders; use research, analytics and experimentation to inform priorities.
Cross-Product Experience & Interoperability: Ensure workflows operate seamlessly across systems, reducing duplicate capabilities, manual hand-offs and fragmented user experiences.
Enterprise Data & Analytics: Partner with Data & Analytics and Architecture to ensure products contribute to a common enterprise data foundation that enables network-wide operational visibility, advancedanalyticsand future AI capabilities.
Delivery Partnership: Partner with Engineering and Architecture leaders to translate product strategy into executable plans while balancing modernization, new capabilities, technical debt, platform health and delivery capacity.
AI & Automation: Identify, prioritize and scale AI-enabled and automated capabilities that deliver measurable improvements in clinical workflows, operational efficiency and decision-making.
Vendor & Strategic Partnerships: Own product-level strategy and value realization for third-party technology partners, ensuring vendor roadmaps and architectures align with Lifemark’s target-state ecosystem.
Financial Management: Own product and platform budgets, business cases, investment approvals and benefit realization.
Risk, Privacy & Compliance: Ensure products, integrations and shared platform capabilities meet healthcare privacy, cybersecurity, regulatory and enterprise risk requirements.
Executive Communication & Governance: Provide senior leadership with clear visibility into portfolio priorities, architectural decisions, investment trade-offs, dependencies and business outcomes.

Company Description

Headquartered in Montreal, Detroit and Munich, Vention helps manufacturers automate their operations in record time with the only hardware and software AI-powered platform built for the factory floor. Our technology powers over 25,000 machines across 4,000 factories across 5 continents and we have the privilege to work with a significant proportion of Fortune 500 manufacturers, from space rockets, to electrical cars, to robotics.

At Vention, you’ll work alongside driven and talented people who care deeply about their craft and the impact they create. We’re a team of high achievers who grow through meaningful work, solving complex challenges, learning fast, and seeing the results of our efforts every day.

We move quickly and aim high, but we do it together with care, collaboration, and respect. Our culture celebrates diverse perspectives and supports your growth through intentional development, strong leadership, and opportunities to make a real difference.

What You’ll Do

This is not a traditional SaaS product leadership role.

Vention's software platform sits at the intersection of industrial automation, robotics, developer tools, cloud software, embedded systems and Physical AI. Our products are tightly interconnected, with decisions in one part of the stack often creating significant implications elsewhere.

The VP Product will lead a team of Product Managers and UI/UX Designers across a broad portfolio including:

MachineBuilder — 3D machine design and configuration
MachineLogic — Robot programming and automation development
Simulation — machine and robot simulation
Robot Control — real-time control and orchestration
Physical AI — AI-powered automation capabilities
Web & eCommerce — digital purchasing and configuration experience
RemoteSupport & RemoteView — remote machine support and operation
MachineAnalytics — machine data, monitoring and intelligence

The mandate is simple: make Vention's software dramatically better while dramatically increasing the velocity at which we ship it.

You will bring product rigor and leadership to an organization where the CEO and CTO remain deeply involved in product direction. Your role is therefore not to simply "own the roadmap." It is to become the operating engine that translates strategic direction into an exceptional product vision, clear priorities and fast execution.

Set the Product Vision & Experience
Define the long-term product vision across Vention's entire software platform.
Establish a coherent product strategy spanning design, programming, simulation, robotics, AI, eCommerce and machine operations.
Raise the bar for simplicity, usability and design quality across the platform, with an Apple-like obsession for product excellence.
Establish product principles and UX standards that make a highly sophisticated technology stack feel simple and intuitive.
Translate company-level strategic direction into a clear, differentiated product vision and roadmap.
Drive Product Velocity & Execution
Dramatically accelerate the pace at which Vention turns ideas into shipped products.
Establish a high-performance product operating cadence focused on fast decisions, clear accountability and measurable outcomes.
Ruthlessly prioritize initiatives based on customer impact, strategic value and business outcomes.
Remove organizational and process bottlenecks that slow product development.
Build a culture where Product, Engineering and Design are accountable for shipping—not simply planning.
Orchestrate the Platform Roadmap
Own prioritization across a highly integrated portfolio of software, firmware, robotics and Physical AI products.
Manage dependencies and sequencing across MachineBuilder, MachineLogic, simulation, robot control, firmware, analytics, RemoteView, RemoteSupport and eCommerce.
Balance customer-facing features, foundational technology investments, technical debt and emerging opportunities.
Resolve competing priorities across product teams and make difficult trade-offs quickly.
Ensure individual product roadmaps collectively move the Vention platform forward as one integrated system.
Lead Product, Design & Technical Product Management
Lead, develop and scale a high-performing organization of Product Managers and UI/UX Designers.
Raise the technical depth, product judgment and execution standards of the product organization.
Partner closely with Engineering to make sound architectural and product trade-offs.
Stay sufficiently technical to dive into architecture, APIs, code and system design when required.
Develop product leaders who can operate independently while maintaining alignment with Vention's overall product strategy.

What You Bring To The Table

Exceptional product leader with 12+ years of experience in product, software or technology leadership, including significant experience managing multiple product teams.
Deep technical credibility with the ability to understand software architecture, APIs, distributed systems, embedded systems and technical trade-offs—and to go into the code when necessary.
Broad platform experience managing complex, highly integrated products where decisions and dependencies span multiple teams and technology layers.
Outstanding product taste with an instinct for simplicity, elegance, consistency and intuitive user experiences; a genuine obsession with design quality and product perfection.
Proven execution track record with a bias toward action, demonstrated ability to accelerate roadmaps, make decisions quickly and consistently turn strategy into shipped products.
Exceptional prioritization skills with the ability to make difficult trade-offs across competing customer needs, technical investments, product opportunities and business priorities.
Strong systems thinker who can understand how individual products, technologies and teams fit together into a coherent platform and architecture.
Customer- and business-oriented with the ability to balance customer value, strategic differentiation, revenue impact and long-term platform investments.
Strong people leader who can attract, develop and inspire exceptional Product Managers and UI/UX Designers while raising the overall bar for product talent and accountability.
Comfortable operating in a highly engaged leadership environment, able to partner effectively with the CEO, CTO and other leaders while bringing structure, clarity and independent judgment to product execution.
Passion for robotics, AI and industrial technology, with genuine curiosity about how software, robotics, Physical AI and hardware can converge to transform automation.
High ownership and low ego: intellectually rigorous, direct, pragmatic and willing to dive into the details when required to solve a problem.

What We Offer

Career pathing: Real opportunities to grow through personalized development plans, bi-annual employee reviews, and mentorship program
Professional development: Continuous training in performance management, inclusive leadership, leadership operating model, team building, and giving/receiving feedback
Gender diversity & inclusion: Pay equity reviews, inclusive policies, and a Women’s Employee Resource Group offering networking, mentorship, and quarterly learning sessions.
Hybrid work: Enjoy flexibility with our hybrid model, allowing you to work from home on select days.
Community engagement: Two paid volunteering days per year to give back to causes you care about.
Team events: All year round employee events including annual kick-off, employee summit, quarterly happy hours, and department events.
Comprehensive benefits: A complete group benefits plan for you and your family that start day one.
Top-up and benefits for new parents: Additional financial support and resources to support employees during their transition to parenthood.

Basée à Montréal, Detroit et Munich, Vention aide les fabricants à automatiser leurs opérations en un temps record grâce à la seule plateforme matérielle et logicielle alimentée par l’IA conçue pour l’usine. Director, CX AI Delivery

Who We Are

Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital product consultancy and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture

With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, Africa, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across eight core service areas: Digital Product Consulting, Digital Marketing Services, Data & AI, Strategy Consulting, Business Operations Modernization, Enterprise Applications, Cloud Engineering, and QA & Test Engineering.

From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

Location & Flexibility

This role will operate remotely in the United States
or Canada
OR be based out of one of our major North American office locations - Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.

This role may involve travel of up to 25% to contact center and client locations.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Director, CX AI Delivery
: a consultant and delivery expert who can turn complex contact center and AI programs into predictable, measurable outcomes. You will lead delivery across our CX AI portfolio, spanning Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) platforms, conversational and agentic AI, agent assist, and CX intelligence, and serve as a trusted advisor to client executives. You will manage a portfolio of client engagements (generally ~$15–20M in revenue), directly lead delivery, product, and engineering leaders, and step in to stabilize and recover programs when needed.

This is a delivery-first leadership role with an AI lens. You will bring the rigor of a seasoned delivery executive together with a working command of how AI is changing CX: from AI-driven routing and virtual agents to copilots, knowledge, and agentic automation. You will help clients adopt these capabilities responsibly, at scale, and in iterative releases that get value into production quickly. You will also help evaluate vendor and partner solutions and decide how and when new tools enter the ecosystem.

This position reports to the Managing Director, CX AI Delivery and typically manages 8–12 direct reports, including senior managers, managers, and principal-level delivery and technical leaders. It is primarily evaluated on delivery success, client and team feedback, forecast accuracy, portfolio profitability, and growth of key accounts. This is an opportunistically billable position.

Responsibilities

Strategic Account Governance & Growth

Be the executive partner. Act as the primary escalation point and strategic advisor for client executives, ensuring TELUS Digital is viewed as a “Doctor” (consultative partner), not a “Waiter” (order taker).
Run portfolio health. Drive the commercial success of a ~$15–20M portfolio, leading Quarterly Business Reviews that connect delivery progress to the client’s long-term CX and business goals.
Grow organically. Identify expansion opportunities in existing accounts by understanding client pain points and bringing a relevant point of view on CX and AI. Support renewals, upsell, and expansion in partnership with strategic sales and customer success teams.
Extend into managed services and advisory as the practice matures: shape Day 2 support models, operational readiness, and advisory engagements that keep clients engaged after go-live.

Delivery Excellence & Risk Mitigation

Lead a global, multidisciplinary team across multiple concurrent workstreams, ensuring product, engineering, and delivery leaders operate as a cohesive unit to deliver measurable outcomes.
Manage risk proactively. Identify “red” and “yellow” programs early; step into recovery situations to provide clarity, reset expectations, and stabilize teams and client relationships.
Push for iterative delivery. Favor smaller releases and faster cycles over big-bang launches, especially for AI capabilities where learning in production is essential.
Optimize delivery models, balancing onshore/offshore teams, automation, and repeatable assets to improve margins and scalability.

new_jobs.description:
About Powerfleet

Powerfleet (Nasdaq: AIOT; JSE: PWR) is a global leader in the artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) software-as-a-service (SaaS) mobile asset industry. With more than 30 years of experience, Powerfleet unifies business operations through the ingestion, harmonization, and integration of data—regardless of source—and delivers actionable insights to help companies meet their strategic objectives around Safety, Compliance, Efficiency and Sustainability. Our people-first culture and relentless innovation empower customers to achieve measurable, sustainable business improvements. Powerfleet serves over 2.6 million subscribers across more than 48,000 customers in 120 countries, with commercial operations across every major continent.

About The Role

Powerfleet is seeking a Senior Director, AI Transformation to help drive the adoption and business impact of AI across the enterprise. This role will work across functions including Sales, Marketing, Finance, HR, Product, Operations, Customer Success, and Technology to identify, prioritize, and advance high-value AI opportunities.

The Senior Director will serve as a key partner to the AI Transformation leadership, helping establish and execute the enterprise AI transformation roadmap, AI governance, and AI Center of Excellence (CoE). The role will connect business priorities with emerging AI capabilities, helping teams move from ideas and use cases to practical adoption and measurable outcomes.

This is a highly cross-functional, individual contributor role requiring strong business judgment, program leadership, communication, and the ability to influence stakeholders across the organization.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise AI Transformation

Partner with business and functional leaders to identify, evaluate, and prioritize AI opportunities across Sales, Marketing, Finance, HR, Product, Operations, Customer Success, and Technology based on business value, feasibility, readiness, risk, and potential impact.
Build and maintain an enterprise portfolio of AI use cases and support the prioritization, sequencing, and execution of initiatives as part of Powerfleet’s broader AI transformation roadmap.
Help business teams move AI initiatives from ideas and experimentation toward adoption, scale, and measurable business outcomes, including opportunities leveraging AI, GenAI, agents, and intelligent automation.

AI Center of Excellence & Governance

Partner with AI Transformation leadership to establish and evolve Powerfleet’s AI Center of Excellence, including practical frameworks, playbooks, best practices, and knowledge-sharing mechanisms that accelerate responsible AI adoption.
Help develop and operationalize AI governance frameworks, standards, and processes, working with Technology, Security, Legal, Privacy, Risk, and business stakeholders to support responsible and scalable AI adoption.

AI Portfolio & Program Leadership

Lead coordination of major cross-functional AI transformation initiatives, establishing clear objectives, milestones, owners, dependencies, and outcomes while helping teams maintain execution momentum.
Establish metrics to track AI adoption, productivity, business impact, and value realization, and support executive reviews of AI initiatives, progress, risks, opportunities, and outcomes.
Help evaluate build-versus-buy opportunities and identify technologies, platforms, and strategic partners that can accelerate AI adoption.

Executive & Stakeholder Engagement

Prepare and present AI transformation strategies, roadmaps, use cases, recommendations, progress, and business outcomes to executive leadership and translate complex AI concepts and emerging technologies into practical business opportunities and facilitate decision-making across business, product, technology, and executive stakeholders. Act as a trusted advisor to leaders across the organization on AI opportunities, adoption, transformation, and value realization.

AI Adoption & Change

Help establish an enterprise culture of responsible AI adoption and experimentation through communication, education, and enablement. Identify and scale successful AI use cases, patterns, and best practices across functions and geographies.

Qualifications

10+ years of experience in technology, digital transformation, strategy, consulting, product, operations, or related disciplines, with meaningful experience working with AI or emerging technologies.
Strong understanding of AI, GenAI, automation, and emerging AI capabilities and their practical business applications.
Experience identifying, evaluating, prioritizing, and executing technology or AI use cases based on business value and feasibility.
Experience developing executive-level presentations, recommendations, roadmaps, and business cases.
Familiarity with AI governance, responsible AI, data privacy, security, and enterprise technology considerations.
Bachelor’s degree in business, Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.

Hybrid Work Model

About The Role

As Director, Technology Delivery Lead, you are accountable for the end-to-end technology delivery of Em, BMO InvestorLine's premier AI agent. You will lead the integrated delivery system across AI engineering, wealth platforms, Microsoft Azure, data, architecture, quality engineering, cybersecurity, operations, and third parties to deliver safe, resilient, scalable, and measurable client outcomes.

You will operate as the principal technology counterpart to the Product Owner for Em. Together, you are jointly accountable for overall delivery: the Product Owner leads product vision, client value, priorities, and acceptance; the Technology Delivery Lead owns the integrated technology plan, engineering execution, technical quality, production readiness, and predictable delivery. This role is not a program coordination position. It is a hands-on senior technology leadership role with clear decision rights and accountability for outcomes.

Mandate and Decision Rights

Own the integrated technology delivery plan for Em from discovery and architecture through build, evaluation, release, operation, and continuous improvement.
Jointly commit scope, sequencing, release outcomes, and delivery forecasts with the Product Owner, balancing client value, technical feasibility, risk, cost, and capacity.

Protect the product from unmanaged technical debt, fragmented ownership, late-stage controls, and delivery practices that are not fit for AI.

Key Responsibilities

End-to-End Technology Delivery
Lead delivery across multiple cross-functional product and platform teams, establishing one integrated plan, clear critical path, transparent dependencies, and accountable owners.
Convert the product roadmap into executable technology increments, release plans, capacity models, milestones, and outcome-based commitments.
Drive delivery discipline across scope, schedule, cost, quality, resources, risk, and benefits, using forecasts rather than artificial certainty.
Identify constraints early, remove impediments, resolve cross-team trade-offs, and escalate decisions with clear options and recommendations.
Ensure each release has explicit entry, exit, acceptance, operational readiness, and rollback criteria.
AI Engineering and AI SDLC Leadership
Apply deep knowledge of generative AI and agentic systems, including LLM orchestration, tool use, retrieval-augmented generation, prompt and context engineering, evaluations, guardrails, memory, and human oversight.
Embed full-lifecycle AI SDLC practices across requirements, design, build, test, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and model or prompt change management.
Ensure AI quality is measured using fit-for-purpose evaluations covering safety, groundedness, relevance, accuracy, latency, reliability, and client experience.
Champion specification-driven development, automation, reusable engineering patterns, and AI-assisted software delivery where approved.
Ensure deterministic software testing and probabilistic AI evaluation are integrated into CI/CD and release decisions.
Azure, Architecture and Platform Integration
Provide senior technical leadership for solutions deployed on Microsoft Azure and integrated with BMO InvestorLine and Wealth Management platforms.
Partner with solution, enterprise, security, data, and platform architects to maintain an approved, scalable target architecture and prevent local optimization or avoidable technical debt.
Ensure APIs, event flows, data services, identity, access, observability, resilience, and non-functional requirements are designed and delivered end to end.
Drive environment readiness, infrastructure as code, automated deployment, telemetry, performance engineering, capacity planning, disaster recovery, and production support readiness.
Promote reuse of enterprise AI capabilities, shared services, patterns, and controls while preserving clear service boundaries and ownership.
Advanced Agile and Value-Stream Delivery
Establish and continuously improve an advanced Agile operating model organized around persistent, cross-functional teams and measurable client or business outcomes.
Lead portfolio and product-level planning, backlog readiness, dependency management, release forecasting, and flow optimization across multiple teams.
Use evidence-based metrics such as lead time, cycle time, throughput, work in progress, predictability, escaped defects, reliability, evaluation performance, and value realization.
Reduce handoffs, unnecessary governance, meeting load, and blocked work; create fast decision paths and clear single-point accountability.
Coach delivery leaders, Scrum Masters, engineering leads, and teams in modern product delivery, DevSecOps, continuous delivery, and learning-driven retrospectives.
Quality, Risk and Responsible AI
Build quality, privacy, security, regulatory compliance, model risk, accessibility, and responsible AI requirements into delivery from inception, not as release-end checkpoints.
Partner with Legal, Risk, Compliance, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Model Risk, Data Governance, and Technology Risk to establish proportionate controls and auditable evidence.
Ensure full-spectrum observability across application, infrastructure, data, model, prompt, agent, safety, and client-experience performance.
Lead incident response, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and learning reviews for technology or AI quality events.
Maintain transparent risk, issue, dependency, and decision records and ensure material risks are escalated promptly.
Stakeholder, Financial and Partner Leadership
Serve as the senior technology delivery voice for Em with InvestorLine, Wealth, Technology & Operations, Applied AI, governance partners, and executive forums.
Provide concise, fact-based reporting on outcomes, delivery confidence, risks, financials, quality, and decisions required.
Own technology delivery financial stewardship, resource planning, vendor performance, commercial dependencies, and delivery commitments.
Lead co-build and vendor engagements with clear accountability, knowledge transfer, architecture compliance, security obligations, and measurable outcomes.
Create an inclusive, high-accountability environment that develops leaders, strengthens technical depth, and keeps teams focused on client outcomes.

Key Success Measures

Predictable delivery of roadmap outcomes and releases, with transparent forecast accuracy and controlled scope change.
Measurable improvement in delivery flow, engineering productivity, automation, quality, and time to value.
AI evaluation thresholds and non-functional requirements met before release and sustained in production.
Stable, secure, resilient production performance with effective observability, incident management, and continuous improvement.
Clear ownership, faster decisions, fewer cross-team handoffs, and effective dependency resolution.
Measurable client adoption, experience, business value, and risk outcomes delivered in partnership with the Product Owner.
Effective financial, capacity, vendor, and technical-debt management.

Required Skills And Competencies

Expert-level technology delivery leadership in large, complex, regulated environments, with accountability for multiple teams and production outcomes.
Deep practical knowledge of AI/ML and generative AI delivery, including agentic architectures, LLM application patterns, evaluations, guardrails, observability, and responsible AI controls.
Strong knowledge of wealth management and digital investing platforms, including client journeys, advice or guidance experiences, market and portfolio data, trading-related integrations, and regulatory considerations.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Azure cloud architecture and delivery, cloud-native engineering, APIs, integration, identity and access, data services, telemetry, resilience, and DevSecOps.
Mastery of advanced Agile, product operating models, value-stream management, Lean flow, Scrum or Kanban, portfolio planning, CI/CD, test automation, and evidence-based delivery metrics.
Ability to challenge constructively, make decisions under ambiguity, translate technical complexity into business implications, and influence senior executives.
Commercial and financial acumen, including technology investment, capacity, vendor, contract, and delivery-performance management.
Exceptional leadership, communication, facilitation, negotiation, and talent-development skills.

Qualifications And Experience

15+ years of progressive experience in technology delivery, engineering, architecture, platform, or product technology leadership, including senior leadership accountability.
Demonstrated success delivering enterprise-scale digital products or platforms from strategy through production and ongoing operation.
Demonstrated delivery of AI/ML or generative AI solutions in production, ideally involving multi-agent systems or other complex AI-enabled client experiences.
Significant experience with Microsoft Azure and modern software engineering practices in a regulated enterprise.
Experience in wealth management, brokerage, digital investing, banking, or similarly regulated financial services is strongly preferred.
Proven experience leading cross-functional internal and partner teams through complex dependencies and high-stakes releases.
University degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems; relevant advanced degree or certifications are considered assets.

Leadership Expectations

Act as an owner: accountable for outcomes, not activity or coordination alone.
Put clients, safety, quality, and sustainable value ahead of pace without evidence.
Create clarity: make responsibilities, decisions, risks, dependencies, and delivery confidence visible.
Lead with technical credibility while empowering engineering and product leaders closest to the work.

The Work

The Senior Director, Financial Planning and Analysis leads the Bank’s enterprise financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, and management reporting activities and oversees the Financial Planning & Analysis Centre of Excellence within the VP, Financial Planning & Analysis portfolio. The role establishes an integrated view of financial performance, outlook, risks, and opportunities to support executive decision-making and disciplined resource and capital allocation.

The role partners with business and functional leaders to translate strategic priorities into financial plans, challenge assumptions, assess performance drivers, and provide timely, decision-useful insight. It is accountable for the quality, consistency, governance, and continuous improvement of planning and forecasting processes and for establishing a high-performing Financial Planning & Analysis Centre of Excellence that scales common standards, tools, models, data, and insight across the Bank.

Financial Planning, Forecasting & Performance Management

Lead the annual budget, periodic forecast, and multi-year financial planning processes, integrating business plans, economic assumptions, balance sheet and income statement drivers, and enterprise priorities.
Establish planning calendars, standards, controls, accountabilities, and review forums that support complete, accurate, timely, and comparable submissions across the Bank.
Provide an integrated view of actual and forecast performance, including revenue, net interest margin, expenses, profitability, return on equity, capital implications, and key non-financial drivers.
Lead scenario and sensitivity analysis to assess the financial implications of changing market conditions, strategic choices, investments, and emerging risks.
Identify material variances, trends, and forecast risks; ensure clear ownership of actions and provide concise recommendations to senior leadership.

Capital Forecasting, Strategic Capital Allocation, ICAAP & Stress Testing

Lead enterprise capital forecasting and provide a forward-looking view of regulatory capital, leverage, capital generation, and deployment under the strategic and financial plan.
Assess capital capacity, requirements, and trade-offs to support the allocation of capital to strategic investments, business growth, acquisitions, and other enterprise priorities.
Partner with Treasury, Risk Management, business leaders, and other Finance teams to align capital forecasts with earnings, balance sheet growth, risk-weighted assets, funding plans, internal capital targets, and management buffers.
Lead the consolidation of financial forecasts and capital impacts for the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process, enterprise-wide stress testing, regulatory stress testing, and related scenario analysis.
Evaluate adverse but plausible scenarios, key sensitivities, and management actions; identify potential capital constraints or vulnerabilities and recommend actions to protect resilience and support strategic objectives.
Establish robust governance, controls, documentation, and executive reporting for capital assumptions, methodologies, forecasts, stress-testing outputs, and capital-allocation decisions.

Executive & Strategic Financial Storytelling

Lead the development and presentation of clear, Board-ready financial narratives that explain enterprise performance, outlook, key drivers, risks, opportunities, and recommended actions.
Translate complex financial, operational, and strategic analysis into concise, decision-oriented messages tailored to the Board, executive leadership, and management governance forums.
Provide strategic oversight of consolidated financial results and outlook, ensuring consistency across the income statement, balance sheet, capital, business segments, and key performance indicators.
Connect actual and forecast performance to the Bank’s strategy, external environment, and value-creation priorities, highlighting the implications of trends, trade-offs, and emerging issues.
Establish executive communication standards that are punchline-first, analytically sound, and supported by clear evidence, sensitivities, and actionable recommendations.
Coordinate across Finance, Treasury, Strategy, Investor Relations, Risk Management, and business finance partners to maintain a consistent enterprise financial story across Board, executive, regulatory, and external materials.

Management Reporting, Data & Insight

Oversee recurring management reporting and dashboards, ensuring that measures, definitions, commentary, and source data are consistent and decision-useful.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators and financial drivers that connect strategic objectives, operating activity, and financial outcomes.
Strengthen data quality, model governance, documentation, controls, and review practices for material planning and management reporting outputs.
Drive automation and simplification of planning, forecasting, modelling, and reporting processes to improve speed, accuracy, transparency, and analytical capacity.
Partner with Data and Technology stakeholders on requirements, prioritization, testing, implementation, and adoption of financial planning and analytics capabilities.

Leadership, Governance & Continuous Improvement

Establish and oversee the Financial Planning & Analysis Centre of Excellence, including its mandate, governance, operating model, service catalogue, priorities, measures, and capability roadmap.
Develop common planning, forecasting, modelling, reporting, and business-partnering standards, and support adoption across Financial Planning & Analysis and partner teams.
Build reusable tools, templates, driver libraries, scenario models, data definitions, and analytical practices that improve consistency, speed, and decision usefulness.
Create a community of practice that strengthens capability through coaching, knowledge sharing, quality review, and continuous learning.
Lead, coach, and develop a team of finance professionals; establish clear accountability, effective succession and development practices, and high standards for analysis and communication.
Maintain an effective control environment for planning, forecasting, modelling, and management reporting, and address issues identified through review, audit, or control testing.

Lets Talk About You!

University degree in finance, accounting, economics, business, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
CPA or CFA designation or an equivalent recognized finance designation.
At least 12 years of progressive finance experience, including substantial experience in financial planning and analysis, forecasting, management reporting, financial modelling, and executive decision support.
Senior leadership and people-management experience, including experience setting functional priorities, reviewing complex work, coaching leaders and professionals, and delivering through others.
Advanced knowledge of financial statements, performance drivers, budgeting, forecasting, scenario analysis, profitability, return on equity, and capital-aware decision-making within financial services.
Experience producing and presenting concise analysis for executives and governance forums, with the judgment to distinguish material issues, challenge assumptions, and recommend action.
Advanced spreadsheet and presentation skills and experience with enterprise planning, reporting, business intelligence, and financial data tools. Specific systems: To be confirmed.
Strong written and verbal communication, stakeholder-management, analytical, problem-solving, organization, and change-leadership skills.
Experience in a Canadian bank or other regulated financial institution, including knowledge of banking products, net interest margin, balance sheet drivers, capital, and regulatory considerations.

new_jobs.title: Director of AI Content Systems, Marketing
new_jobs.description:
Please Note: This is a fully remote role for candidates with Eastern Timezone overlap.

The role

You won't write most of our content, you'll design, build, and run the AI-powered system (think content engineering) that turns product, customer, and expert knowledge into content that drives organic pipeline.

You're not a software engineer, but you think like one. You're as comfortable vibe coding and building agents as you are customizing WordPress, writing brand guidelines, or proofreading a white paper.

This is the first hire on a new team at Time Doctor. We run it like an engineering team whose product is content: a clear spec, a repeatable production system, quality gates, and measured output. The team stays small and gets its leverage from AI, automation, freelancers, agencies, and subject-matter experts.

Who we are

Time Doctor is a workforce analytics platform that gives distributed teams the visibility they need to improve trust and performance. We serve remote, hybrid and outsourced organisations worldwide, with particular strength in BPO, healthcare and tech services. We are bootstrapped, profitable and fully remote, with team members across 30+ countries. We built a durable business on customer revenue rather than venture capital, and we are now focused on growing it.

What you'll own

Content strategy.
Decide what we publish, for whom, and why, based on search demand, AI-search behavior, buyer questions, and revenue marketing priorities.
The content production system.
Design and run the AI workflows, agents, prompt libraries, briefs, and QA gates that produce content at scale. Treat it like a product: version it, measure it, and keep improving it.
Expert input pipeline.
Build repeatable ways to capture knowledge from product, customer success, sales, customers, and outside experts, and feed it into the system so our content says things competitors can't.
Verbal and visual brand.
Own voice, tone, and editorial standards, and encode them into the system so every asset meets them by default.
SEO and AI search (GEO).
Own strategy for organic search and visibility in AI answers (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and others).
The website.
Own site architecture, content structure, conversion paths, and the website roadmap.
Tooling and vendors.
Choose and manage the AI tools, automation platforms, and outside partners the team runs on, within a budget.

How you'll be measured

You own three outcomes: organic leads, organic traffic, and AI + SEO search visibility. Because organic results lag, your first two quarters are weighted toward leading indicators that show the system is working.

What you'll manage and who you'll work with

You'll build and manage: content development, technical SEO/GEO implementation, and visual design. You'll do the work yourself when speed matters, and bring in agencies, contractors, or freelancers you select and direct against our brand guidelines when scale matters.
Your inputs:
positioning, messaging, and personas come from the VP of Marketing. You turn them into content at scale; you don't own positioning.
Your team:
Freelancers and contractors as needed, with a path to hire as the system proves out.

Who you are

Must have
5+ years in B2B SaaS content, SEO, or growth marketing, including 1+ years leading a function or program.
You've built and run AI-powered content workflows in production. You can walk us through one end to end: inputs, tools, prompts, skills, QA gates, output volume, and results.
Hands-on with AI and automation tools (LLMs, agents, and automation platforms).
Comfortable tinkering with HTML and CSS. Can read Python and scripts. Comfortable with Claude code or eager to learn it.
A track record of growing organic traffic and leads through SEO, with a working understanding of how AI search surfaces and cites content.
Strong editorial judgment. You know when an AI draft is off-brand, generic, or wrong, and you design the system to catch it.
Experience directing freelancers, agencies, and subject-matter experts to a quality bar.
You think in systems and metrics: throughput, cycle time, cost per asset, and outcomes.

Nice to have
Experience owning a B2B website roadmap and conversion optimization.
Background in time tracking, workforce analytics, HR tech, or remote-work software.

This role is not a fit if you want to be the primary writer, or if your strength is CMS or content platform architecture rather than marketing outcomes.

How we'll evaluate:
a walkthrough of a content system you've built, and a short exercise designing a workflow for one of our content types. We won't ask for writing samples.

Why this role

You are the first hire on a new team, and you get to design the content system from the ground up.
You own real outcomes: organic leads, traffic, and AI search visibility, with the authority to choose the tools and partners you run on.
You work AI-first from day one, at a company that expects it and funds the tools.
We are profitable and bootstrapped. Your budget comes from customers, not from a burn rate.
Professional development resources and a learning budget.
Fully remote and flexible, working with talented people in 30+ countries.

Our hiring approach

This is a full-time, 100% remote role. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we value diversity and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status or disability.

We hire globally, but this particular role is open only to candidates based in the United States or Canada, with at least four hours of daily overlap with US Eastern hours. Our Talent Attraction team will walk you through the details during your first conversation.

Learn more about us at https://people.timedoctor.com

Modernize FP&A for a Product Operating Model

Align financial rhythms with product cycles, investment governance, and product portfolio management.
Build FP&A frameworks that support experimentation, iterative planning, and benefit realization.

Elevate forecasting accuracy and enforce strong financial discipline across functions and brands.

Connect franchisor, brand, and franchise partner economics into a clear view of system-wide value creation.

Your leadership will enable diverse teams to successfully implement Apply’s delivery methodologies, firmly rooted in Lean and Agile principles and frameworks.

The Technology Director is a versatile technologist with a broad understanding of artificial intelligence, front-end, back-end, mobile, platform engineering, and testing techniques. This knowledge assists in defining and approving effective solutions and facilitating communication and collaboration amongst the team. The Technology Director fosters a calm, positive, supportive, and solution-oriented atmosphere within the team.

Responsibilities

Technical Leadership & Oversight:

Oversee and guide the work of software engineers and technical team members, ensuring high-quality outcomes in digital consumer-facing solutions.
Leverage AI as a core set of tools, processes, and skills to drive value.
Define and manage the high-level technical architecture and technology stack with a specific eye for delivering high-performing, scalable, secure, and SEO/GEO optimized digital solutions.

AI-Led Customer Experience Solutions:

Leverage partnerships with Google Cloud Platform and other AI providers to deliver AI-enabled solutions such as content scaling, product finders, personalization solutions, customer experiences, AI-enabled commerce, and agentic experiences.

AI-Enabled Delivery:

Leverage AI tools, processes, and teams to deliver solutions quicker and more efficiently while still promoting enterprise quality and security.

Thought Leadership:

Position our consultancy as a leader in delivering leading-edge AI-enabled digital solutions. This includes thought leadership and client education on web platform and mobile app trends, customer experience enhancements, and performance optimizations.

Composable Platforms:

Champion composable architectures and platforms that combine to create enterprise digital experience platforms.
Leverage data and analytics to provide ongoing evaluation and optimization of customer experience solutions.

Mentorship & Team Collaboration:

Develop expertise within the team in delivering cutting-edge digital, e-commerce, and other customer-facing solutions.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to align technology initiatives with business goals. Manage multiple delivery squads, ensuring that deadlines are met and dependencies are properly managed.

Client & Business Management:

Provide expert advice and nurture relationships with stakeholders within client organizations.
Identify and nurture growth within projects, delivering business value for both the client and our organization.

Risk Management & Process Improvement:

Identify, prevent, and mitigate risks that might impact the success of the engagement.
Escalate issues and risks to executive leadership when needed.
Continually seek out and suggest improvements to building software, particularly through the use of AI, to accelerate delivery and innovation.

Requirements

Proven track record in a similar technology leadership role in building and scaling web and mobile app experiences, leveraging modern frameworks and technologies.
Experience in overseeing the delivery of digital solutions that span a wide range of capabilities (customer accounts, products, transactions, personalization, AB testing, real-time webhooks and data streams, etc.), with high importance for customer experience (CX) and performance optimization.
Experience leveraging AI tools, processes, and teams to accelerate the software development process.
Deep understanding of software engineering, system architecture, and project management
Demonstrated experience in providing expert guidance to clients, managing complex and diverse technology projects, and fostering strong client relationships.
Proven ability to mentor team members and foster a high-performance culture in large multidisciplinary teams
Ability to contribute to strategic planning and decision-making at the executive level, with build vs buy recommendations aligning with business goals.
Experience in identifying and managing a wide array of risks, including technical, staffing, scoping, and client relationship risks, within an e-commerce context.
Excellent client-facing skills and experience in vendor selection and management.
Outstanding communication and interpersonal abilities, with the capacity to foster trust and empowerment with stakeholders and team members.
Calm, positive, supportive, and solution-oriented mindset, able to promote a collaborative atmosphere within the team.

LIFE AT APPLY

People are at the core of everything we do at APPLY. We provide you with modern tools, systems and approaches, value your time, safety, and health, and strive to build a work community where you can thrive and grow. Here are a few benefits we offer to support you:

new_jobs.title: Chief of Staff, Enterprise AI
new_jobs.description:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

Serve as a strategic advisor and execution partner to the Chief AI Officer, helping shape and deliver Equinix’s enterprise AI agenda. The role spans AI strategy and governance, enterprise adoption and value realization, organizational capability, and the external AI ecosystem. Translate priorities into funded plans and measurable outcomes, strengthen executive decision-making, and enable the AI leadership team to operate effectively across a global organization.

The successful candidate combines independent judgment, practical AI fluency, and hands-on execution. They anticipate what needs attention, challenge assumptions constructively, and take ownership of complex work from initial framing through completion.

Responsibilities

Strategic Planning & Executive Advisory

Partner with the CAIO to define and communicate the enterprise AI strategy, priorities, and investment roadmap, connecting internal transformation with Equinix’s broader AI business and ecosystem strategy
Develop decision briefs with clear recommendations, alternatives, financial implications, and risks. Provide candid advice and test the assumptions behind major proposals
Assess emerging AI capabilities, competitors, and partnerships, distinguishing developments that warrant action from those that warrant monitoring
Lead strategic initiatives and special projects from problem definition through delivery, establishing ownership and transitioning ongoing responsibilities to the appropriate teams

Business Operations & Execution

Own the AI leadership team’s operating rhythm, including planning, portfolio reviews, leadership meetings, and offsites. Structure forums around decisions, with clear owners, deadlines, and follow-through
Drive portfolio visibility across priorities, dependencies, investment, and results. Work with Finance and business owners to validate value assumptions and distinguish realized benefits from forecasts
Coordinate budget and workforce planning with Finance and HR. Surface resource trade-offs and recommend where to accelerate, adjust, or stop investment
Resolve execution barriers with accountable leaders and escalate material risks early, with options and a recommended course of action
Represent the CAIO as delegated, exercising judgment within agreed decision rights and keeping the CAIO informed of consequential commitments

Cross-Functional Alignment & Stakeholder Engagement

Build trusted partnerships with executive leaders, Chiefs of Staff, and business owners to secure sponsorship and drive enterprise AI adoption and value realization
Resolve cross-functional dependencies and competing priorities. Make ownership explicit and address difficult issues directly and constructively
Lead preparation of Board and executive materials, decision memos, and organizational communications, translating technical detail into clear business implications and specific asks
Prepare the CAIO for customer, partner, and industry engagements. Define the purpose of each engagement and drive follow-through, aligning external messaging with Communications and Marketing

Organizational Effectiveness & Transformation

Partner with the AI leadership team and HR on operating model evolution, workforce priorities, and leadership development. Identify capability gaps and clarify responsibilities as the organization scales
Coordinate with AI governance, Security, Legal, and other control functions to bring responsible AI requirements and unresolved risk decisions into portfolio planning and executive reviews
Advance AI fluency and change initiatives with business leaders, using adoption and outcome evidence to identify what needs to change
Improve how the organization works through simple processes and practical use of AI, reducing manual reporting and unnecessary meetings. Model a culture of High Standard, Low Bureaucracy, Zero Blame

Qualifications

Knowledge & Experience

10+ years of experience in strategy, business operations, consulting, Chief of Staff, product, data, AI, or related leadership roles, with demonstrated ownership of execution and business results
Strong understanding of enterprise AI and technology operating models, including generative AI, agents, shared platforms, adoption barriers, and AI economics and risk. Able to engage credibly with technical and business leaders
Proven experience delivering complex initiatives across a large, global, matrixed organization, including resolving competing priorities and recovering work that is off track
Strong financial and analytical acumen, with experience in business cases, investment prioritization, budget planning, and benefits measurement
Experience personally developing executive communications, Board materials, and strategic plans that require limited revision and support consequential decisions
Experience partnering with C-suite executives through ambiguity and organizational change. Prior Chief of Staff experience is valuable; equivalent operating leadership experience is equally relevant

Skills & Attributes

Strategic judgment: Frame the right problem, make trade-offs, and offer an independent point of view
Execution discipline: Take ownership without waiting for detailed direction and close commitments reliably
Executive communication: Synthesize complex issues into concise, accurate writing and clear discussion
Trust and discretion: Handle sensitive matters with integrity and the confidence to challenge respectfully
Influence and collaboration: Build credibility across functions and hold peers accountable while preserving trust
Learning agility: Develop technical and business context quickly, use AI tools effectively, and verify their outputs
Calm leadership: Remain effective under pressure, recognize when to act independently and when to escalate, and put team outcomes first
